name: com.idosgames/platform
title: iDos Games
description: Create and configure cross-platform and web3 games on iDos Games: config, tokens, NFTs, AI, builds.

tools.name: list_my_titles
tools.description: List the games (Titles) this connection may work with: TitleID, name, publication status and the permissions granted on each — call it first when the user names a game or says "my game", then pass its TitleID as title_id to the other tools. A game's sandbox copy is a separate Title (DevTitleID) with its own permissions (DevAccess); an empty Access means the live game itself is not granted. Filter by name or id with "search"; long lists are paged (skip/limit, HasMore). Read-only; takes no title_id.

search.description: Optional substring of the game's name or TitleID.

skip.description: How many games to skip (paging). Default 0.

tools.name: create_title
tools.description: Create a NEW game (Title) on the publisher's account, the same way the dashboard does. It takes a slot of the publisher's plan, gets the base (sign-in + lobby with profile, inventory, invites, friends, quests, mailbox) plus a game module, a ready starter build playable at once on its own address, and a DEV sandbox copy. The new Title and its '-DEV' copy are added to THIS connection right away, so pass the returned TitleID as title_id to get_<section> / save_<section> and the build tools next. Give a name and the idea; optionally base_game (a starter game module id: board-game, idle-rpg, hero-run, voxelcraft, video-studio, ai-media-app (an AI generator app: photo templates and trends turned into videos, pictures, voice, music, 3D; set up in the title's AI section), kit-game (the game constructor: the game is the title's GameSpec config section, created with a genre from the idea and editable with save_game_spec); otherwise it is picked from the idea, and an idea none of them fits gets a game-constructor game in its genre) and category. Not idempotent: every successful call creates another game, so do not retry a call that succeeded. When the plan has no free slot it fails with TITLE_LIMIT_REACHED and a link where the publisher can upgrade. No token is launched (that needs the publisher's own wallet in the dashboard). Takes no title_id; needs the 'title:create' permission.

name.description: Game name shown to players, up to 50 characters.

idea.description: What the game is about, in a few sentences (up to 50000 characters). Used as the description and to pick the base game and category when they are not given.

base_game.description: Optional starter game module the project is built on (see list_modules). Omit to let the platform pick it from the idea.

category.description: Optional catalog category id (e.g. 'shooter'). An unknown id fails with the list of valid ones.

tools.name: get_launch_options
tools.description: List where and how a game TOKEN can be launched from the publisher's own wallet: each network (EVM chains of the new Uniswap-V4 stack and Solana clusters) with its native coin, creation fee, the most a first buy may be, the creator tax rates you can pick, pair currencies (EVM) or pool fee tiers (Solana), and whether holder staking is available. Read-only. Call it before prepare_token_launch. Needs the 'token:launch' permission.

tools.name: prepare_token_launch
tools.description: Prepare a token launch: creates the game (or uses an existing game given by existing_title_id) as a draft with its token address reserved, the same way the dashboard wizard does, and returns three ways to sign it with ANY wallet: (A) sign_url: give it to the user, they open it in the dashboard, connect a wallet and sign; (B) call build_token_launch_tx with your own wallet address to get the transaction and sign it yourself; (C) the local @idosgames/mcp signs it with a key from its settings (send_launch_tx). Whoever signs becomes the token creator and receives the creator income. Nothing is paid and nothing is signed by this call. A new game takes a slot of the publisher's plan (TITLE_LIMIT_REACHED when full). The new game and its '-DEV' copy join this connection. Pass the returned LaunchID to the other launch tools; then poll get_launch_status. Needs the 'token:launch' permission.

existing_title_id.description: Optional: launch the token for this EXISTING game of the connection (it must have no token yet). Omit to create a new game.

name.description: New game only: the game name shown to players, up to 50 characters.

idea.description: New game only: what the game is about, a few sentences (also picks the base game and category).

base_game.description: New game only, optional: starter game module the project is built on.

chain_id.description: Network id from get_launch_options (Solana: 0 mainnet, 103 devnet).

token_description.description: Optional token description (defaults to the idea).

token_image_url.description: Optional token icon: a URL on cloud.idosgames.com (e.g. from generate_image).

banner_url.description: New game only, optional: banner image URL on cloud.idosgames.com.

creator_tax_percent.description: EVM: creator tax on every trade, one of the rates from get_launch_options (0 = none). Fixed forever.

holders_percent.description: Share of the creator income paid to token stakers, 0-100 (0 = no staking). Fixed forever.

reward_percent.description: EVM: share of the creator income to the game's reward pool, 0-100; holders + reward <= 100. Fixed forever.

first_buy.description: Optional creator's first buy in the pair currency, decimal (e.g. "0.01"). 0 or omitted = none. Not above max_first_buy.

quote_token.description: EVM, optional: pair currency token address from get_launch_options; omit for the native coin.

pool_tier.description: Solana, optional: pool fee tier (pool_configuration) from get_launch_options.

link_only.description: New game only: keep the game off the home page and catalog (only by link).

tools.name: build_token_launch_tx
tools.description: Get the launch transaction of a prepared draft for a given wallet (method B/C). EVM: returns {chainId, to, data, value} (and an ERC-20 approve to send first when the pair currency is a token): send it from exactly that wallet within expires_at (the server-signed launch terms live 30 minutes; call again for fresh ones). Solana: returns the inputs (solana_launch) the local @idosgames/mcp turns into the transaction (build_launch_tx / send_launch_tx). The wallet becomes the draft's creator: only a launch from it can finish this game. After sending, call submit_launch_tx with the hash.

launch_id.description: LaunchID (the game's TitleID) returned by prepare_token_launch.

wallet.description: Address of the wallet that will sign and send the launch (EVM 0x..., Solana base58). It becomes the token creator.

tools.name: submit_launch_tx
tools.description: Report the hash (EVM) or signature (Solana) of a sent launch transaction. The server reads the chain itself, checks that this transaction created this game's token from the wallet given to build_token_launch_tx, and finishes the game (published with its token). Not confirmed yet: status 'submitted', call get_launch_status again in a few seconds.

launch_id.description: LaunchID (the game's TitleID) returned by prepare_token_launch.

tx_hash.description: EVM transaction hash (0x...) or Solana signature of the sent launch.

tools.name: get_launch_status
tools.description: Status of a token launch: waiting_signature (with sign_url), submitted, finalized (game, token and pool links), or failed with the reason. Safe to poll every few seconds.

launch_id.description: LaunchID (the game's TitleID) returned by prepare_token_launch.

tools.name: get_token_market
tools.description: Market data of a game's token from the platform's database: price or market cap, liquidity pool and bonding-curve progress, pair currency rate in USD, trading fees. Any game with a launched token on the new stack (EVM Uniswap-V4 or Solana); pass its TitleID as game_id. Read-only, public data.

game_id.description: TitleID of the game whose token to read.

tools.name: prepare_token_trade
tools.description: Link where the user buys or sells a game's token with their own wallet on idosgames.com (the trade panel opens pre-filled). The agent never trades on the server. To trade from a wallet you control, use the local @idosgames/mcp (quote_token_trade, build_token_trade, send_token_trade).

game_id.description: TitleID of the game whose token to trade.

amount.description: Optional decimal amount: buy = pair currency to spend (e.g. "0.05"), sell = tokens to sell.

tools.name: get_image_data
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'ImageData' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Dictionary<string,string> of arbitrary named image asset URLs/paths for the Title — splash screens, banners, icons, loading screens, marketing art. Key is a project-defined slug (e.g. "main_banner", "login_bg"), value is a URL or storage path. For per-currency icons use Currency.VirtualCurrencies[].AssetPaths; for per-item icons use Item; for character art use Character.

tools.name: save_image_data
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'ImageData' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Dictionary<string,string> of arbitrary named image asset URLs/paths for the Title — splash screens, banners, icons, loading screens, marketing art. Key is a project-defined slug (e.g. "main_banner", "login_bg"), value is a URL or storage path. For per-currency icons use Currency.VirtualCurrencies[].AssetPaths; for per-item icons use Item; for character art use Character.

value.title: DictionaryOfStringAndString
value.description: New value for the ImageData field.

tools.name: get_asset_bundle
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'AssetBundle' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Dictionary<string,string> of named bundle/manifest URLs (Unity AssetBundles, Addressables manifests, etc.). Key is a logical bundle slug, value is its CDN URL. Use this for binary game content; for images alone use ImageData.

tools.name: save_asset_bundle
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'AssetBundle' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Dictionary<string,string> of named bundle/manifest URLs (Unity AssetBundles, Addressables manifests, etc.). Key is a logical bundle slug, value is its CDN URL. Use this for binary game content; for images alone use ImageData.

value.title: DictionaryOfStringAndString
value.description: New value for the AssetBundle field.

tools.name: get_title_custom_data
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'TitleCustomData' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. SCHEMA + limits for the title-wide key-value store (feature flags, project-wide globals, event state, balancing knobs that don't fit any typed definition below). This section holds ONLY the key schema — the VALUES live in the TitleCustomData store, one document per title, managed with the dedicated title-data tools (get_title_data / save_title_data). Each key declares a Scope (Static = authored config; Runtime = mutable state written only by CloudCode scripts) and a Bucket (Public = readable by game clients; Private = server/CloudCode only).

tools.name: save_title_custom_data
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'TitleCustomData' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. SCHEMA + limits for the title-wide key-value store (feature flags, project-wide globals, event state, balancing knobs that don't fit any typed definition below). This section holds ONLY the key schema — the VALUES live in the TitleCustomData store, one document per title, managed with the dedicated title-data tools (get_title_data / save_title_data). Each key declares a Scope (Static = authored config; Runtime = mutable state written only by CloudCode scripts) and a Bucket (Public = readable by game clients; Private = server/CloudCode only).

value.title: TitleCustomDataDefinitions
value.description: Schema and limits of the title-wide key-value store. The VALUES live in the separate TitleCustomData collection (one document per title), not in this config section. Each key declares a Scope (Static = authored config; Runtime = mutable state written only by CloudCode scripts) and a Bucket (Public = readable by game clients; Private = server/CloudCode only). Clients can never write this store.

Keys.description: Schema-managed keys of the TitleCustomData store. Dictionary key is TitleCustomDataKeyDefinition.KeyID. A definition pins the key's Scope (Static/Runtime) and Bucket (Public/Private) — writes to another scope/bucket are rejected. Unregistered keys are free-form unless RejectUnregisteredKeys is true.

DefaultMaxValueLengthBytes.description: Default value size limit in bytes (UTF-8) for unregistered keys. Registered keys use their own MaxValueLengthBytes. Recommended: 8192 (8 KB).

DefaultTtlSeconds.description: Default TTL in seconds for unregistered keys. null means no TTL. Expired records are filtered on read and purged on the next write.

MaxKeysPerBucket.description: Maximum number of keys per (scope, bucket) pair — Static.Public, Static.Private, Runtime.Public, Runtime.Private. Protects the title document from unbounded growth. Recommended: 256.

MaxTotalSizeBytes.description: Total size limit of the whole title store (both scopes, both buckets) in bytes. Protects against MongoDB's 16 MB document limit. Recommended: 4,000,000 (~4 MB).

RejectUnregisteredKeys.description: If true, writes to unregistered keys are rejected (strict schema mode). If false (default), unregistered keys are accepted as free-form with the default limits.

TitleCustomDataKeyDefinition.description: Definition of a single registered TitleCustomData key: its scope, bucket and validation rules.

KeyID.description: Unique key identifier across all scopes and buckets. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

Scope.description: Storage scope: Static (authored config, written via the management backend / AI Coder) or Runtime (mutable state, written only by CloudCode). Fixed by config.

Bucket.description: Visibility bucket: Public (readable by game clients) or Private (server/CloudCode only). Fixed by config.

ValueType.description: Expected value format: String, Int, Bool or Json. Validated on every write. Counters used with CloudCode's IncrementTitleCustomData must be declared as Int.

MaxValueLengthBytes.description: Hard value size limit in bytes (UTF-8) for this key. Overrides TitleCustomDataDefinitions.DefaultMaxValueLengthBytes.

TtlSeconds.description: Key TTL in seconds. null means permanent. On write the server sets ExpiresAt = now + TtlSeconds; expired records are filtered on read.

DefaultValue.description: Default value materialized on read when the record does not exist or has expired. Never written to the DB until an explicit write. null means absent keys stay absent.

Description.description: Developer-facing description of the key's purpose. Does not affect validation.

x-enum-descriptions: Authored configuration. Written by the management backend (publisher dashboard, AI Coder's SaveTitleData) and cached like the rest of the title config. CloudCode can read it but never write it.
Mutable title state. Written ONLY by CloudCode and always read straight from the database (never cached), so a counter read right after a write is correct.
Readable by every player through the client TitleCustomData endpoint. Examples: event schedule, global progress, public feature flags.
Never returned to clients. Server code and CloudCode scripts only. Examples: server-side thresholds, anti-fraud settings, internal counters.
Arbitrary string. Validated by length only.
Integer. Must parse as long via long.TryParse. Returned to the client as a string.
Boolean. Must be "true" or "false" (case-insensitive, via bool.TryParse).
Valid JSON document. Any structure parseable via JToken.Parse. Size limited by MaxValueLengthBytes.

tools.name: get_cloud_code
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'CloudCode' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Server-side scripting (CloudCode): the active JavaScript revision the title runs, plus execution policy — engine limits, rate limits, per-handler metadata, whether logs/stack traces are revealed to clients. Scripts are the ONLY way to write protected player data (UserCustomData ReadOnly/Internal buckets) and mutable title data (TitleCustomData Runtime scope). Prefer the dedicated cloud-code tools over editing this section by hand: they compute the code hash, bump the revision number and archive the previous one.

tools.name: save_cloud_code
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'CloudCode' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Server-side scripting (CloudCode): the active JavaScript revision the title runs, plus execution policy — engine limits, rate limits, per-handler metadata, whether logs/stack traces are revealed to clients. Scripts are the ONLY way to write protected player data (UserCustomData ReadOnly/Internal buckets) and mutable title data (TitleCustomData Runtime scope). Prefer the dedicated cloud-code tools over editing this section by hand: they compute the code hash, bump the revision number and archive the previous one.

value.title: CloudCodeDefinitions

Schedules.description: Handlers run on a schedule: every IntervalMinutes from StartAtUtc, with args = { Trigger: 'Schedule', ScheduleID, ScheduledAtUtc, Args }. At most 20 schedules; the most frequent is every 5 minutes. Runs as the server (no player session); one run per slot, missed slots are not replayed.

Webhooks.description: Incoming webhooks: POST https://api.idosgames.com/api/v2/{titleID}/Public/CloudCode/Webhook/{id} runs a handler for an external service (payments, site forms, bots) with args = { Trigger: 'Webhook', WebhookID, Headers, Query, Body }. The request is verified BEFORE the handler runs — HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with a title secret, or the secret itself as a token header. The handler's result is the HTTP response.

ResourcePolicy.description: The script's right to move player resources and start InApp AI. Enabled=false (default): server.ApplyResourceOperation and server.StartAIGeneration refuse outright.

value.description: New value for the CloudCode field.

CloudCodeHttpPolicy.description: Outbound HTTP policy for CloudCode scripts. Disabled by default; requests are only allowed to explicitly listed hosts.

Enabled.description: Master switch. When false, server.HttpRequest is rejected outright.

AllowedHosts.description: Allowed hosts: exact match (api.stripe.com) or subdomain wildcard (*.stripe.com). An empty list means nothing is allowed — there is deliberately no allow-all mode.

TimeoutMilliseconds.description: Per-request timeout in ms. 0 means the default (5000). Clamped server-side so the call fits inside the 10-second execution budget.

MaxResponseBytes.description: Response size cap in bytes. 0 means the default (65536). A larger body is dropped and flagged instead of truncated silently.

MaxRequestsPerExecution.description: How many outbound requests one execution may make. 0 means the default (3).

AllowInsecureHttp.description: Allow plain http:// in addition to https://. False by default: a substituted secret would travel in clear text.

CloudCodeSchedule.description: A handler run on a schedule.

ID.description: Schedule id (letters, digits, '_' up to 64 chars).

Handler.description: Handler name in the active revision (handlers.<name>).

Enabled.description: null or true = enabled; false = paused.

StartAtUtc.description: Anchor time in UTC: runs happen at StartAtUtc + k × IntervalMinutes. null = aligned to 00:00 UTC (60 = on the hour, 1440 = at midnight UTC).

Args.description: Optional JSON passed to the handler as args.Args (up to 8 KB).

ID.description: Webhook id — the last segment of its URL (letters, digits, '_' up to 64 chars).

Handler.description: Handler name in the active revision (handlers.<name>).

Enabled.description: null or true = enabled; false = requests are refused.

SecretName.description: Name of a title secret (kind Secret) used to verify requests. The value never reaches the script.

Header.description: Header with the signature or token. null = X-Signature (HmacSha256) or X-Webhook-Token (Token).

x-enum-descriptions: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the secret, hex (optionally 'sha256=' prefixed), in Header (default X-Signature).
The secret itself in Header (default X-Webhook-Token).

CloudCodeResourcePolicy.description: The script's right to move player resources and start InApp AI. Enabled=false (default): both methods refuse outright, before any other field is read. Crypto under THIS policy is only the first gate ('the script may touch crypto at all'); the actual safety of a crypto grant (caps, pool backing) is CryptoCurrencyDefinition.ServerGrantPolicy of EACH currency, and always applies regardless of this policy.

Enabled.description: Master switch. false: server.ApplyResourceOperation and server.StartAIGeneration are refused outright.

AllowedGrantTypes.description: Resource types the script may GRANT. null/empty = default (VirtualCurrency, Item). CryptoCurrency and RewardedVideoCredit require explicit listing. Purchase is ALWAYS forbidden (not a storable resource — the player's store money, the script cannot control it).

AllowEventTokens.description: Allow the script to move event tokens (ResourceBundle.EventTokens) — leaderboard scores, event tokens.

AllowedConsumeTypes.description: Resource types the script may CONSUME from the player. null/empty = default (VirtualCurrency, Item). Consuming does not mint value, so this list is intentionally less strict than the grant one, but Purchase is forbidden just the same.

Caps.description: Grant caps by resource key: "VirtualCurrency:{CurrencyID}", "Item:{CatalogID}:{ItemID}", "RewardedVideoCredit". No key = no cap.

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Credits, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account (players see it as "Aspis" — write Aspis in player-facing text). Requires only Amount — the price in whole Credits. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCreditsPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted by every sale of the game author: Store, Lootbox, Collection packs, Craft, DealOffer, TimedBoost, Premium, Item and Character upgrades, skins, CoopEvent spins, GameLoop special mode entry, Workshop publish fee, InApp AI (charged only when the generation is ready). NOT accepted in player-to-player prices or refundable fees (Marketplace listing fee, PvP Match creation) - those refuse with CREDITS_NOT_ALLOWED_HERE; batch calls refuse too. Allowed only in Consume: Credits are never a reward anywhere.

CloudCodeResourceCapRule.description: One CloudCode resource-grant cap. See CloudCodeResourcePolicy.Caps.

PerPlayerDaily.description: Per-player daily cap. null = no cap on this axis.

TitleDaily.description: Title-wide daily cap. null = no cap on this axis.

tools.name: get_currency
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Currency' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Currency catalogue: VirtualCurrencies (Gold, Gems, Energy, etc.) AND CryptoCurrencies (on-chain tokens). Defines IDs, economy (USD value, balance limits), recharge rules for energy-like currencies, conversion rules, and per-currency permissions. The CurrencyID of each entry is referenced by Item prices, Store SKUs, Reward payouts, Quest rewards, Lootbox loot, etc. NOTE: the "Main" CryptoCurrency entry is protected and cannot be overwritten — your changes to that key will be silently ignored.

tools.name: save_currency
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Currency' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Currency catalogue: VirtualCurrencies (Gold, Gems, Energy, etc.) AND CryptoCurrencies (on-chain tokens). Defines IDs, economy (USD value, balance limits), recharge rules for energy-like currencies, conversion rules, and per-currency permissions. The CurrencyID of each entry is referenced by Item prices, Store SKUs, Reward payouts, Quest rewards, Lootbox loot, etc. NOTE: the "Main" CryptoCurrency entry is protected and cannot be overwritten — your changes to that key will be silently ignored.

value.title: CurrencyDefinitions

Spends.description: Spends of the player's resources on actions of the game (Currency/Spend): a revive, other upgrade cards… The server charges the configured price and grants nothing.

PeerTransferHold.description: Peer payout hold — protection against 'buy currency with real money, move it to an alt (marketplace, mailbox transfer, lost PvP stake, Workshop purchase), refund the payment'. null = no hold. To turn it off keep the section and set HoldHours = 0, so already pending payouts still mature on login.

CryptoRewardsFromDeveloperShare.description: Crypto rewards to players that the players' reward pool cannot cover are topped up from the developer's share of the pool. Off by default — the developer turns it on. When off (or the share is short too), the shortfall is granted as the currency's IOU virtual currency (UnbackedRewardCurrencyID).

CryptoIouForScriptsAndAI.description: CloudCode server.ApplyResourceOperation and AI feature rewards also grant the unbacked part of a crypto grant as the currency's IOU instead of refusing. Off by default — module rewards (quests, events, leaderboards, store) always use the IOU when the currency has one.

CryptoAutoRepayIouOnWithdrawal.description: Lazily repay IOUs on withdrawal: when the player's crypto balance does not cover a withdrawal, the missing part is converted from the player's IOUs of that crypto into real crypto from the players' reward pool of the same network (only as much as needed, while the pool lasts). On by default.

value.description: New value for the Currency field.

CurrencyID.description: Unique stable currency identifier (e.g. "GOLD", "GEMS", "ENERGY"). Primary key used in balance operations, analytics events, and cross-references from other entities. Immutable after creation.

DisplayName.description: Display name for internal use (admin panel, logs, tooling). Not intended for player-facing display; player localization is handled separately by CurrencyID key.

AssetPaths.description: Paths to currency assets (icons of various sizes, animated versions, SVG, etc.). Element purpose is defined by project convention on the client side.

Economy.description: Economic parameters: USD value, initial deposit, balance limits, granularity. Describes the currency's value and storage bounds.

Recharge.description: Auto-recharge configuration. Null means the currency does not self-recharge (gold, gems). When set, the currency behaves as an energy resource (hearts, moves, energy).

Conversion.description: Rules for converting this currency to others. Null means conversion is fully disabled.

Permissions.description: Behavioral flags: what can be done with the currency (trade, purchase with real money, convert, refund).

Audit.description: Record metadata: creation and last modification times. Used for audit, incident investigation, and client cache invalidation.

Status.description: Current lifecycle status of the currency. Allows soft retirement without deleting the record so transaction history continues to reference CurrencyID.

ValueInUSD.description: Base USD value per unit of currency. Used for cross-currency conversion equivalence, BI valuation of rewards/lootboxes, and store pricing via the multiplier.

ValueInUSDUpdatedAt.description: Timestamp when ValueInUSD was last updated. Consumers of the cached price can use it to decide whether to refresh the quote.

InitialDeposit.description: Amount of currency granted to a new player at account creation. 0 means none. Applied once during wallet initialization.

MinBalance.description: Minimum allowed balance. Usually 0; negative values are allowed for credit/penalty mechanics. Any debit that would breach this is rejected before balance change.

MaxBalance.description: Hard upper balance cap. Anti-exploit safeguard and global cap over Recharge.Max. long.MaxValue means effectively unlimited.

DailyEarnLimit.description: Max amount of currency a player can EARN per UTC day. Null means no limit.

DailySpendLimit.description: Max amount of currency a player can SPEND per UTC day. Null means no limit. Compliance mechanism for real-money currencies.

Rate.description: Units credited per FULL period, granted as a single batch. Rate=5 with Period=60 means +5 once a minute, not +1 every 12 seconds: an incomplete period credits nothing and its time is carried over.

Max.description: Recharge cap: balance ceiling for auto-recharge. A batch is clipped exactly at this value (if less than Rate is missing, only the remainder is credited); at or above it nothing is credited. Above this, currency can only be gained via explicit grants. Distinct from the global cap in Economy.MaxBalance.

Period.description: Length of one recharge period in seconds. Units are credited on full-period boundaries measured from the last accrual or spend, not on a wall-clock grid.

Enabled.description: Master conversion switch. False disables conversion regardless of Targets content.

RateMode.description: Rate calculation mode for this currency as conversion source. Automatic uses Economy.ValueInUSD; Manual uses per-pair ConversionTarget.Rate.

Fee.description: Conversion fee as a SHARE of the debited amount: 0.05 = 5% (the platform-wide unit, see RateSpec). Empty or 0 means no fee. Taken from the source currency BEFORE calculating the received amount. Deliberately NOT named FeePercent: the Percent suffix is banned platform-wide because it was the source of 0..1 vs 0..100 confusion.

Targets.description: Whitelist of target currencies with conversion parameters. Null/empty means no conversion allowed. One-directional: a target listed here does not imply the reverse is allowed.

x-enum-descriptions: Rate is computed automatically from ValueInUSD of source and target currencies.
Rate is taken manually from ConversionTarget.Rate per pair.

TargetCurrencyType.description: Type of target currency. Determines which dictionary to resolve TargetCurrencyID against (virtual or crypto). Required.

TargetCurrencyID.description: CurrencyID of the target currency the conversion is allowed to.

Rate.description: Fixed conversion rate: units of target per 1 unit of source. Used only when Conversion.RateMode = Manual; ignored under Automatic.

MinAmount.description: Minimum source amount per conversion operation. Null means no limit. Prevents dust conversions that round to 0 target.

MaxAmount.description: Maximum source amount per conversion operation. Null means no limit. Protects against single-shot balance drains.

DailyLimit.description: Per-player daily limit for conversions on this specific pair (in source currency units). Null means no limit. Counted by UTC days.

IsTradable.description: Whether the currency can be transferred between players (gifts, P2P trade, guild bank). False by default.

IsPurchasable.description: Whether the currency can be purchased with real money (IAP, storefront). Used when building storefronts and validating IAP callbacks.

IsRefundable.description: Whether the currency is refundable on IAP refunds and compensations. True by default; disable for derived currencies obtained by conversion.

CreatedAt.description: Record creation time. Set once on insert and immutable thereafter.

UpdatedAt.description: Record last-modified time. Updated on every save. Used for audit and client cache invalidation.

x-enum-descriptions: Available in all operations and shown to players.
Hidden in UI but operations are formally allowed (e.g. internal tests).
New earnings/purchases disabled; existing balance can still be spent.
All operations temporarily blocked (maintenance, emergency stop).

CurrencyID.description: Unique stable crypto-currency identifier (e.g. "BTC", "ETH", "USDT"). Primary key used across balance operations, analytics, and references. Immutable after creation.

DisplayName.description: Display name for internal use (admin panel, logs). Player-facing localization is handled separately by CurrencyID key.

AssetPaths.description: Paths to currency assets (icons, network logos, animations). Element purpose is defined by client convention.

DisplayDecimals.description: Number of decimals to show in UI and accept on user input. Presentational only; on-chain decimals per token+network are in CryptoNetworkBinding.Decimals.

ValueInUSD.description: Cached USD value per unit (from oracle/exchange). Used for USD display, USD-limit/KYC checks, and BI. Not authoritative for real-time conversion — fetch live quote from price service.

ValueInUSDUpdatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last ValueInUSD update. Consumers can decide whether to use cached value or fetch a fresh quote.

UsdPriceRefreshMinutes.description: Main token only: how often (minutes) the engine refreshes the token USD price on in-game crypto spends. Custom value needs a paid plan; default 720 (twice a day). Each refresh counts as an API call. 5..10080.

DeveloperWithdrawalFeePercent.description: Developer fee (percent) on a PLAYER withdrawal of this currency: that share of the withdrawn amount moves to the developer's share of the title pool. Deposits are credited to the player in full; crypto the player spends in-game also goes to the developer. Developer fee + Community Marketing fee + burn must not exceed 50%.

CommunityMarketingWithdrawalFeePercent.description: Community Marketing fee (percent) on a PLAYER withdrawal of this currency: that share of the withdrawn amount funds the Community Marketing pool (rewards for promoting the game on social media). Developer fee + Community Marketing fee + burn must not exceed 50%.

WithdrawalBurnPercent.description: Percentage of a player token withdrawal that is BURNED on-chain (EVM: DEAD address, Solana: incinerator). The server binds the burn amount into the withdrawal signature. Developer fee + Community Marketing fee + burn must not exceed 50%; the platform's own withdrawal commission is separate.

PlayerTradeFeePercent.description: Developer fee (percent) on PLAYER-TO-PLAYER trades in this currency: a marketplace sale, a PvP win, a purchase from a Workshop author. The seller/winner receives the amount minus this fee; the fee moves to the developer's share of the title pool. One value for every trading module. Max 50%. In-game prices are not affected — spent crypto already goes to the developer in full.

TradeShareCommunityMarketingPercent.description: Where the game's share of token trading goes: the percent of trade-fee inflow to the title pool that is credited to the Community Marketing fund; the rest goes to the players' reward pool. Only the title ledger splits it (on-chain the title has one balance per currency), so a change applies to new credits. Null = default: the game token (Main) 0% (all to players), any other currency (the pair currency of the V4-only stack, e.g. WETH, USDC) 100% (all to Community Marketing). 0..100.

Networks.description: Currency-to-network bindings: which networks the currency lives in, with per-network parameters (contract address, on-chain decimals, minimums, fee).

Limits.description: Compliance limits (AML/KYC). Separate from Permissions because this is regulatory. Null means no limits set (usually dev/testnet only).

Permissions.description: Behavioral flags: what can be done with the currency (deposits, withdrawals, in-game spend, conversion to virtual).

Conversion.description: Conversion rules for this currency. Targets can be other crypto or virtual currencies (distinguished by ConversionTarget.TargetCurrencyType). Null means fully disabled.

Audit.description: Record metadata: creation and last-modified times. Shared type with virtual currencies.

Status.description: Current lifecycle status. Allows soft retirement without deleting the record so transaction history continues to reference CurrencyID.

ServerGrantPolicy.description: Daily caps on rewards of this currency (everything but deposits): module rewards (quests, events, season, store, lootboxes, IAP products...), an AI feature Reward and CloudCode's server.ApplyResourceOperation. Rewards are always paid in crypto from the players' reward pool of this title (plus the developer's share if CryptoRewardsFromDeveloperShare is on); what the pool cannot cover, or what exceeds a cap, is granted as the IOU currency (UnbackedRewardCurrencyID). null = no caps. Editable for Main too. Mode matters only for CloudCode and AI rewards while CryptoIouForScriptsAndAI is off. Does not affect deposits, withdrawals or player spend.

UnbackedRewardCurrencyID.description: IOU virtual currency of this crypto: the part of a crypto reward that is not backed at grant time (by the players' reward pool, plus the developer's share if CryptoRewardsFromDeveloperShare is on) is granted in this virtual currency 1:1. The player sees crypto was owed; the developer repays it with real crypto from the dashboard. When the player spends this crypto in the game, the IOU is spent first. Must be a key of VirtualCurrencies. Not set — an unbacked reward is refused.

NetworkID.description: Network identifier from the title-level networks config (e.g. "ethereum", "bsc", "tron"). Network config itself lives elsewhere.

ContractAddress.description: Token smart-contract address in this network (ERC-20/BEP-20/TRC-20). Null for native coins (ETH, BNB, TRX, BTC); distinguishes native transfer vs contract call.

Decimals.description: On-chain decimals for this token in this network. Used to convert whole units to/from smallest units in raw on-chain transactions. Distinct from DisplayDecimals.

MinWithdraw.description: Minimum amount per withdrawal in this network. Enforced on the withdrawal path: a smaller amount is refused.

DepositsEnabled.description: Deposit switch for this currency-network pair. Allows disabling one network during incidents without affecting others.

WithdrawalsEnabled.description: Withdrawal switch for this currency-network pair. Used to pause withdrawals on one network (e.g. drained hot-wallet) while others keep working.

DailyWithdrawUsd.description: Per-player daily withdrawal limit in USD equivalent. Null means no daily limit. AML-driven, USD-denominated for consistency across volatile currencies.

MonthlyWithdrawUsd.description: Monthly withdrawal limit in USD equivalent. Separate from daily because KYC tiers typically have both. Null means no monthly limit.

KycRequiredAboveUsd.description: USD-equivalent threshold for a single withdrawal above which KYC is required. Null means KYC not required for this currency.

DepositsEnabled.description: Global deposit switch for this currency (across all networks). For per-network control use CryptoNetworkBinding.DepositsEnabled.

WithdrawalsEnabled.description: Global withdrawal switch for this currency. See DepositsEnabled.

SpendableInGame.description: Whether the currency can be spent in-game (store purchases, event bets). False restricts it to deposit/withdraw/convert only.

ConvertibleToVirtual.description: Whether this currency can be converted to/from virtual currencies. False rejects targets with TargetCurrencyType=Virtual even if listed in Conversion.Targets.

CryptoServerGrantPolicy.description: Server-issued grant policy for one crypto currency. See CryptoServerGrantMode.

Mode.description: Grant mode.

FundingNetworkID.description: Which network (one of this currency's Networks) pays rewards from its pool. Not needed when the currency lives in one network — that one is used. Required when Mode = Backed.

PerPlayerDailyTokens.description: Per-player daily cap on crypto rewards, in whole tokens. null = no cap. Over the cap: see RefuseOverCap (IOU by default; CloudCode/AI without IOU: refused).

TitleDailyTokens.description: Title-wide daily cap on crypto rewards, in whole tokens. null = no cap. Over the cap: see RefuseOverCap (IOU by default; CloudCode/AI without IOU: refused).

RefuseOverCap.description: What happens when a daily cap is reached. true = the reward is refused entirely with CRYPTO_SERVER_GRANT_CAP_EXCEEDED:{currency} (nothing is granted, not even an IOU). null/false = the reward is granted as the IOU currency.

x-enum-descriptions: Only for CloudCode and AI rewards while CryptoIouForScriptsAndAI is off: their crypto grants are refused. Default. Module rewards ignore the mode.

Only for CloudCode and AI rewards while CryptoIouForScriptsAndAI is off: in the SAME transaction the grant is paid from the players' reward pool, the rest from the developer's share if CryptoRewardsFromDeveloperShare is on. If that is short, the whole operation rolls back. Module rewards ignore the mode.

CurrencySpendDefinition.description: A spend of the player's resources on an action of the game (a revive, other upgrade cards, a speed-up): the game does the action itself, the server only charges the price. The client names the spend, never the amount. Prices: virtual currencies, items, rewarded-video credit; no store payment, no Credits (Aspis), no crypto.

SpendID.description: Spend identifier (the dictionary key is used when empty).

PriceOptions.description: Price options; the client picks one by SelectedOptionID (empty — the first available on its platform).

PriceOption.description: A single way to pay for an entity. Platform-wide standard: everything with a configured price describes it as a PriceOptions dictionary whose key is the OptionID. Options exist because ResourceConsume.Standard is charged as a whole (AND), while a price across platforms is a choice (OR): a store SKU on mobile, a token on web. Platform duties split as "the client renders, the server allows": title config ships as one immutable artifact per (version, field set), so it cannot be filtered per request — the client hides options by AllowedPlatforms, while PriceOptionSelector.Select refuses a charge whose option is not available on the caller's platform.

OptionID.description: Payment-option identifier. If empty, the dictionary key is substituted (PriceOptionResolver) — the client selects an option by this ID, so an option without one would be unselectable.

Name.description: Display name of the option ("For gold", "$0.99"). A localization key or a literal — resolved client-side by the rule own table → fallback table → the key itself.

Cost.description: What is charged for this option. Standard is the base; PremiumDiscounts / PremiumTiers behave as everywhere else. An entry of type Purchase means the option is paid in a store rather than with a player resource: the payment is verified before ResourceService and never enters the resource operation. No initializer on purpose — "unset" must differ from "set to empty"; an unset Cost means the option is free.

AllowedPlatforms.description: Platforms this option is available on. Empty/null = all of them. Do not list Unknown: a client that did not report its platform only gets options with no platform restriction, i.e. those safe everywhere.

AssetPaths.description: Option assets (currency icon, discount badge). Key = asset slug.

ResourceConsume.description: Consume direction container for ResourceOperation. Two mutually exclusive premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumTiers (priority) replaces Standard with the best matching tier's Resources via Replace, and PremiumDiscounts (fallback) applies a percentage discount to Standard only when no PremiumTier matched. Best matching tier wins, no stacking.

Standard.description: Base — what to charge all players including F2P.

PremiumDiscounts.description: Percentage discount on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 - Discount)). Ignored if any PremiumTier matched — Replace takes over.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different price for premium players (different ItemID/CurrencyID/Target). Always Replace, single best matching tier wins. If matched, Standard is fully replaced and PremiumDiscounts is ignored; otherwise fallback to Standard + PremiumDiscounts.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Credits, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account (players see it as "Aspis" — write Aspis in player-facing text). Requires only Amount — the price in whole Credits. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCreditsPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted by every sale of the game author: Store, Lootbox, Collection packs, Craft, DealOffer, TimedBoost, Premium, Item and Character upgrades, skins, CoopEvent spins, GameLoop special mode entry, Workshop publish fee, InApp AI (charged only when the generation is ready). NOT accepted in player-to-player prices or refundable fees (Marketplace listing fee, PvP Match creation) - those refuse with CREDITS_NOT_ALLOWED_HERE; batch calls refuse too. Allowed only in Consume: Credits are never a reward anywhere.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

Type.description: System the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

PremiumTierDiscount.description: Percentage discount on ResourceConsume.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 - Discount) with Math.Ceiling rounding in player's favor. Applies only to Standard; ignored if PremiumTiers matches. Best matching tier wins, discounts do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierBonus.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Discount.description: Discount as a SHARE: 0.1 = -10%, 1.0 = free. Empty or 0 = no discount. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).

x-enum-descriptions: Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

PeerTransferHoldSettings.description: Peer payout hold: virtual currency a player receives from ANOTHER player (marketplace deals, mailbox transfers, PvP match stakes, Workshop sales) is not credited at once but waits HoldHours. If the payer refunds a store purchase in the meantime, their pending payouts created after that purchase are voided: the currency burns and goods the payer got in return go back to the recipient. A matured payout is credited on the recipient's next login or marketplace open. Crypto is never held.

HoldHours.description: How many hours a payout waits. 0 = no hold. Google Play self-service refunds take up to ~48 h, so 72 covers them.

OnlyIfPayerPurchasedWithinDays.description: Hold only when the payer bought something with real money (IAP, Telegram Stars, external payment) within the last N days. Without a recent purchase there is nothing to refund, so the payout is credited at once. 0 = always hold.

CurrencyIDs.description: Which virtual currencies are held. Empty/null = all virtual currencies. Crypto is never held.

ReturnGoodsOnVoid.description: When a payout is voided, give the goods the recipient handed over back to them if the payer still has them (unequipped). Default true.

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Item' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Item catalogue — every consumable, equipment piece, resource, gear or generic inventory entity the player can own. Defines item IDs, names, categories, stack rules, rarities. Referenced by Store SKUs (as contents), Lootbox loot tables, Quest rewards, Craft recipes, and Reward payouts. For premium-tier bundles use Premium; for character entities use Character.

tools.name: save_item
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Item' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Item catalogue — every consumable, equipment piece, resource, gear or generic inventory entity the player can own. Defines item IDs, names, categories, stack rules, rarities. Referenced by Store SKUs (as contents), Lootbox loot tables, Quest rewards, Craft recipes, and Reward payouts. For premium-tier bundles use Premium; for character entities use Character.

value.title: ItemDefinitions
value.description: Root container for all item catalogs of a title. Source of truth for every ItemID used in the game.

Catalogs.description: All catalogs of the title. A catalog is a thematic grouping of items. Key is CatalogID, unique within the title.

Sets.description: Equipment sets: a bonus for wearing several items of one set. Key is SetID; an item belongs to the set when its Metadata.CollectionID equals the key. Null/empty = no sets.

SetSettings.description: Shared set settings (default bonus mode). Null = defaults (Cumulative).

ItemCatalog.description: Catalog: a set of items of one thematic group. Item references (ItemID + CatalogID) resolve here.

Items.description: All items in this catalog. Key is ItemID (unique within the catalog). Full item address is the (CatalogID, ItemID) pair.

ItemDefinition.description: Definition of one item — the template from which player instances are created. Holds all static data and optional blocks (NFT, Stats, Equipment, Metadata).

ItemID.description: Unique item ID within the catalog.

CatalogID.description: Owner catalog ID. Together with ItemID forms the full item address.

ItemClass.description: Item class used for grouping and logic (e.g. "Weapon", "Armor", "Consumable", "Sticker", "LootBox", "Cosmetic").

DisplayName.description: UI display name (localization key or literal string).

Description.description: UI display description (localization key or literal string).

Tags.description: Arbitrary tags for filtering and grouping (e.g. "rare", "event_halloween_2026", "tradable", "seasonal").

CustomData.description: Arbitrary custom data. Used by designers for parameters that don't fit typed blocks.

IsStackable.description: True: copies stack as Amount in ItemTotals. False: each copy is a separate UnstackableItemInstanceState with its own InstanceID, wear and custom data.

IsTradable.description: Whether P2P transfer is allowed. Controls availability in the trade module.

Weight.description: Item weight in randomized drops (crafting, lootboxes, sticker packs). Higher value means higher drop rate in weighted pools.

AssetPaths.description: Paths to visual/audio assets keyed by purpose (e.g. "icon", "model", "thumbnail", "preview_video", "sfx_use").

NFT.description: NFT binding when the item is tokenized on-chain. Null for ordinary off-chain items.

Stats.description: Game stats (flat + percent bonuses). Set only for items granting stats. Null means no effect on the stat system.

Equipment.description: Equipment rules: minimum level, allowed slots and characters. Null means the item cannot be equipped.

Upgrade.description: Upgrade rules for the item instance level. Null = item cannot be upgraded. Independent from equipment — non-equippable items can also be upgradable.

Metadata.description: Meta info: rarity, collection/set membership, author. Used by the Albums subsystem and for UGC attribution.

ExpirationDurationSeconds.description: Instance lifetime in seconds from the moment it enters inventory (AcquiredAt). When set (> 0), each granted UnstackableItemInstanceState gets ExpiresAt = AcquiredAt + this value. Null/<=0 means permanent. Only applies to non-stackable items.

MaxSupply.description: Max number of instances that may exist SIMULTANEOUSLY across the whole title (circulating supply). Enforced centrally in ResourceService at genuine mint/burn sites (lootbox, store, quest, craft): grants increment circulation guarded by this cap, burns decrement it. Moves (trade/marketplace escrow/gift) don't change it. Null/<=0 = unlimited. Stored in the separate TitleSupplyCounters collection, not in config.

NFTModel.description: Blockchain binding for an item. One Item can be bound to multiple networks; deposit/withdraw selects the binding by operation NetworkID.

Networks.description: Per-network bindings. Key is NetworkID from cfg.Blockchain.Networks. The same ItemID has different ContractAddress + TokenID per network.

MetadataUrl.description: URL to token JSON metadata (typically IPFS or Arweave) in OpenSea standard. Shared across networks.

NFTNetworkBinding.description: Binding of one Item to one specific network.

TokenID.description: Token ID within the contract (EVM uint256; Solana mint address or Metaplex edition number).

MaxLevel.description: Number of item levels encoded as a contiguous tokenId block from TokenID (the block base): tokenId(level) = TokenID + (level - 1). 1 (default) = single tokenId (== TokenID). Reverse: level = tokenId - TokenID + 1.

ItemStats.description: Item stat modifiers. Applied as flat additions over base first, then percent multipliers on top.

FlatBonuses.description: Flat bonuses added to the base stat. Key is stat name ("Health", "Damage", "Armor"), value is the addition.

PercentBonuses.description: Percent bonuses multiplying the (base + flat) total. Key is stat name, value is a fraction of 1.0 (0.05 = +5%).

Power.description: Base item Power, added to CharacterModel.Power on equip. Scaled by instance Level via ItemUpgrade.PowerScalingFactor. 0 = no explicit Power contribution.

ItemEquipment.description: Equipment rules: who can equip the item, where, and under what conditions.

MinCharacterLevel.description: Minimum character level (CharacterModel.Level) required to equip. 0 means no requirement.

UseRequirements.description: Item-side stat requirements. Key is StatID, value is minimum stat level on the character. Validated in EquipItems identically to CharacterEquipmentSlot.StatRequirements.

AllowedCharacterIDs.description: Whitelist of characters that can equip the item. Empty or null means any character (subject to other requirements).

AllowedSlotIDs.description: SlotIDs where the item can be placed (e.g. "Head", "Chest", "MainHand", "Trinket1").

IdleRateBonus.description: Bonus to the idle-accrual rate (units per second) while the item is equipped. Summed across all items equipped on the character and added to the IdleRateConfig formula; counted only when the accrual has EquipmentBonusEnabled. 0 = the item does not affect the rate.

ItemUpgrade.description: Upgrade rules for an unstackable item instance: cap, cost curve, stat scaling.

MaxLevel.description: Hard cap on the instance Level. 1 means already at max (cannot be upgraded). Values <= 0 are clamped to 1.

PriceOptions.description: Ways to pay for one upgrade step. Dictionary key = PriceOption.OptionID; each option's Amount is the base cost, scaled linearly per target level via CostScalingFactor. A store-paid option is not allowed here: a store SKU is a fixed price tier and cannot follow a per-level formula.

CostCurve.description: Cost curve over the level. Computed from the price in PriceOptions; the step is the target level (numbered from 1). Empty = the same price at every level. Leave Base empty — the base is the configured price.

FlatBonusCurve.description: Growth curve for ItemStats.FlatBonuses over the instance level. The base is the bonus itself, the step is the item level. Empty = flat bonuses do not grow. Leave Base empty.

PercentBonusCurve.description: Growth curve for ItemStats.PercentBonuses over the instance level. Empty = percent bonuses do not grow. Leave Base empty.

PowerCurve.description: Growth curve for ItemStats.Power over the instance level. Empty = item Power does not grow. Leave Base empty.

Fodder.description: Fodder valuation rules for same-item upgrade payment. Controls W(L) (how a level-L copy is valued) and whether leveled copies can be spent. Null = legacy FlatCount + ProtectLeveled.

PriceOption.description: A single way to pay for an entity. Platform-wide standard: everything with a configured price describes it as a PriceOptions dictionary whose key is the OptionID. Options exist because ResourceConsume.Standard is charged as a whole (AND), while a price across platforms is a choice (OR): a store SKU on mobile, a token on web. Platform duties split as "the client renders, the server allows": title config ships as one immutable artifact per (version, field set), so it cannot be filtered per request — the client hides options by AllowedPlatforms, while PriceOptionSelector.Select refuses a charge whose option is not available on the caller's platform.

OptionID.description: Payment-option identifier. If empty, the dictionary key is substituted (PriceOptionResolver) — the client selects an option by this ID, so an option without one would be unselectable.

Name.description: Display name of the option ("For gold", "$0.99"). A localization key or a literal — resolved client-side by the rule own table → fallback table → the key itself.

Cost.description: What is charged for this option. Standard is the base; PremiumDiscounts / PremiumTiers behave as everywhere else. An entry of type Purchase means the option is paid in a store rather than with a player resource: the payment is verified before ResourceService and never enters the resource operation. No initializer on purpose — "unset" must differ from "set to empty"; an unset Cost means the option is free.

AllowedPlatforms.description: Platforms this option is available on. Empty/null = all of them. Do not list Unknown: a client that did not report its platform only gets options with no platform restriction, i.e. those safe everywhere.

AssetPaths.description: Option assets (currency icon, discount badge). Key = asset slug.

ResourceConsume.description: Consume direction container for ResourceOperation. Two mutually exclusive premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumTiers (priority) replaces Standard with the best matching tier's Resources via Replace, and PremiumDiscounts (fallback) applies a percentage discount to Standard only when no PremiumTier matched. Best matching tier wins, no stacking.

Standard.description: Base — what to charge all players including F2P.

PremiumDiscounts.description: Percentage discount on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 - Discount)). Ignored if any PremiumTier matched — Replace takes over.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different price for premium players (different ItemID/CurrencyID/Target). Always Replace, single best matching tier wins. If matched, Standard is fully replaced and PremiumDiscounts is ignored; otherwise fallback to Standard + PremiumDiscounts.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

Type.description: System the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. PremiumTierDiscount.description: Percentage discount on ResourceConsume.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 - Discount) with Math.Ceiling rounding in player's favor. Applies only to Standard; ignored if PremiumTiers matches. Best matching tier wins, discounts do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierBonus.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Discount.description: Discount as a SHARE: 0.1 = -10%, 1.0 = free. Empty or 0 = no discount. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).
