ScalarCurveSpec.description: Scalar curve f(base, step): how a value grows with a level, rank, stage or count. THE MODULE'S RULE: an empty field does nothing — an unset curve is the identity f(base,n)=base, an unset bound means there is no bound. All rates are shares (0.1 = +10%), never multipliers, so 0 and empty always mean the same thing.

Base.description: Base the curve is computed from. Empty = use the base supplied by the caller. Fill it only where the base is a publisher setting (a multiplier starting at 1.5, a table's value before its first point) — where the base comes from data (a stat value, a level price, an item bonus) leaving it empty is required, otherwise it overrides the real base.

Shape.description: Curve shape. Empty = Flat, i.e. no growth.

PerStep.description: Units added per step (Shape=PerStep). Empty or 0 = no growth.

PerStepRate.description: Share of the base added per step (Shape=PerStepRate): 0.1 = +10% of base per step. Empty or 0 = no growth.

GrowthRate.description: Compounding rate per step (Shape=Geometric): 0.1 = x1.1 per step. Empty or 0 = no growth.

Points.description: Table breakpoints (Shape=Table or TableAbsolute). Empty = no growth.

Interpolation.description: How to interpolate between points. Empty = Step.

TailGrowthRate.description: Growth beyond the last table point (share per step). Empty = hold the last point's value.

MinResult.description: Lower bound of the result. Empty = there is NO lower bound (not 0).

MaxResult.description: Upper bound of the result. Empty = there is NO upper bound (not 0).

x-enum-descriptions: Value does not change with the step. Same behaviour as an unset curve.
Additive in the value's own units: base + PerStep * (step - firstStep).
Additive share of the base: base * (1 + PerStepRate * (step - firstStep)). 0.1 = +10% of base per step.
Compounding: base * (1 + GrowthRate)^(step - firstStep).
Table of multipliers over the base: base * interpolate(Points, step).
Table of absolute values: interpolate(Points, step). The base is ignored.

CurvePoint.description: One breakpoint of a table curve.

AtStep.description: Step (level / rank / stage) at which this point takes effect. Empty = the point is ignored.

Value.description: Value at this point. Empty = the point is ignored.

x-enum-descriptions: Step: hold the previous point's value until the next one. Behaviour of an unset field.
Linear between adjacent points.
Geometric between adjacent points: lo * (hi/lo)^t.

ItemUpgradeFodder.description: Fodder valuation/selection settings for same-item level upgrade. Two axes: ValuationMode (per-level value formula) and Selection (how leveled copies are picked/protected).

ValuationMode.description: Per-level value formula W(L). Self-item cost is expressed in value points; fodder accumulates W(level) until the target is covered.

WeightCurve.description: Curve of a copy's value by its level for FodderValuationMode.Merge: computed from a base of 1, the step is the copy level (numbered from 1), so a level-1 copy is always worth exactly 1. The WHOLE curve is honoured — shape, table points and bounds, not just its growth. The classic rule 'R copies of level L make one L+1' is Shape=Geometric with GrowthRate = R - 1 (R=2 becomes 1), but it is no longer the only option: fodder is charged in VALUE POINTS, not copies. Empty = every copy is worth the same.

Selection.description: How fodder is selected and how leveled (Level>1) copies are treated.

ItemMetadata.description: Item metadata for rarity display, collection membership, and attribution. Used by the Albums subsystem and the UI layer.

RarityID.description: Rarity ID from the title's rarity dictionary (e.g. "Common", "Rare", "Epic", "Legendary"). Drives UI framing and duplicate-conversion value.

CollectionID.description: ID of the collection/set the item belongs to. For stickers, the Album page ID; for cosmetics, the thematic set ID.

AuthorID.description: Author/creator ID. Used for UGC content and branded collaborations (UI attribution, royalty payments).

ItemSetDefinition.description: Equipment set. Members are items whose Metadata.CollectionID equals the SetID (the Sets dictionary key); each equipped member counts as one piece.

DisplayName.description: Set display name (localization key or literal string).

Description.description: Set description (localization key or literal string).

AssetPaths.description: Set assets keyed by purpose (e.g. "icon").

BonusMode.description: Bonus mode for THIS set. Null = the shared SetSettings.BonusMode.

Bonuses.description: Bonus tiers: 'N pieces equipped grants a bonus'. Order does not matter — tiers are sorted by Pieces.

ItemSetBonusTier.description: Set tier. Bonuses of the same kind as ItemStats and merged into the same calculation layers: flat into gear flat, percent into gear percent, Power into explicit item Power. Item levels do not scale set bonuses.

Pieces.description: Number of set pieces required. A tier with Pieces <= 0 never applies.

FlatBonuses.description: Flat bonuses by StatID, same as ItemStats.FlatBonuses.

PercentBonuses.description: Percent bonuses by StatID as a fraction of 1.0, same as ItemStats.PercentBonuses.

BonusMode.description: How set tiers combine by default. A set may override it with its own BonusMode.

tools.name: get_premium
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Premium' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Premium offerings catalogue — paid subscriptions, premium passes, real-money bundle skus, supporter tiers. Distinct from Store (regular in-game shop with virtual-currency prices) and from DealOffer (limited-time promotional offers). Use this specifically for monetization tiers / IAP that grant ongoing benefits.

tools.name: save_premium
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Premium' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Premium offerings catalogue — paid subscriptions, premium passes, real-money bundle skus, supporter tiers. Distinct from Store (regular in-game shop with virtual-currency prices) and from DealOffer (limited-time promotional offers). Use this specifically for monetization tiers / IAP that grant ongoing benefits.

value.title: PremiumDefinitions
value.description: Root container of premium subscriptions / premium passes for the title. Holds a dictionary of definitions keyed by PremiumID. Distinct from Store (in-game shop with virtual-currency prices) and from DealOffer (time-limited promotions).

Definitions.description: List of premium subscription definitions for the title.

PremiumDefinition.description: Definition of a single premium product (subscription, premium pass, VIP tier). Specifies identifier, tier, duration, prices (virtual currency and store products) and the benefits granted to the owner.

PremiumID.description: Stable premium product identifier (e.g. 'silver_vip', 'battle_pass_premium'). Never change after publication — references from Store/Season will break.

DisplayName.description: Display name of the product shown in the client / admin.

Tier.description: Product tier level (1, 2, 3...). Higher = more premium. Compared against SegmentGate.MinPremiumTier and similar gates.

DurationDays.description: Subscription duration in days. 0 = permanent, 30 = monthly, 365 = yearly.

TrialDurationDays.description: Trial period length in days (e.g. 3 or 7). 0 = no trial.

PriceOptions.description: Payment options for the subscription (for different currencies or bundles). Key = PremiumPriceOption.OptionID, value = price definition. Multiple options allow paying with currency, items, or a bundle.

Benefits.description: Free-form benefits granted to the subscriber. Keys are benefit slugs (e.g. 'ExpMult', 'GoldMult', 'DailyVipAccess', 'NoAds', 'SkinSlotBonus'). Values are numeric parameters (e.g. 1.2, 2.0, 1.0=true, 0.0=false, 5.0=slot count). Concrete keys are project-defined and consumed by game code.

PriceOption.description: A single way to pay for an entity. Platform-wide standard: everything with a configured price describes it as a PriceOptions dictionary whose key is the OptionID. Options exist because ResourceConsume.Standard is charged as a whole (AND), while a price across platforms is a choice (OR): a store SKU on mobile, a token on web. Platform duties split as "the client renders, the server allows": title config ships as one immutable artifact per (version, field set), so it cannot be filtered per request — the client hides options by AllowedPlatforms, while PriceOptionSelector.Select refuses a charge whose option is not available on the caller's platform.

OptionID.description: Payment-option identifier. If empty, the dictionary key is substituted (PriceOptionResolver) — the client selects an option by this ID, so an option without one would be unselectable.

Name.description: Display name of the option ("For gold", "$0.99"). A localization key or a literal — resolved client-side by the rule own table → fallback table → the key itself.

Cost.description: What is charged for this option. Standard is the base; PremiumDiscounts / PremiumTiers behave as everywhere else. An entry of type Purchase means the option is paid in a store rather than with a player resource: the payment is verified before ResourceService and never enters the resource operation. No initializer on purpose — "unset" must differ from "set to empty"; an unset Cost means the option is free.

AllowedPlatforms.description: Platforms this option is available on. Empty/null = all of them. Do not list Unknown: a client that did not report its platform only gets options with no platform restriction, i.e. those safe everywhere.

AssetPaths.description: Option assets (currency icon, discount badge). Key = asset slug.

ResourceConsume.description: Consume direction container for ResourceOperation. Two mutually exclusive premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumTiers (priority) replaces Standard with the best matching tier's Resources via Replace, and PremiumDiscounts (fallback) applies a percentage discount to Standard only when no PremiumTier matched. Best matching tier wins, no stacking.

Standard.description: Base — what to charge all players including F2P.

PremiumDiscounts.description: Percentage discount on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 - Discount)). Ignored if any PremiumTier matched — Replace takes over.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different price for premium players (different ItemID/CurrencyID/Target). Always Replace, single best matching tier wins. If matched, Standard is fully replaced and PremiumDiscounts is ignored; otherwise fallback to Standard + PremiumDiscounts.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

tools.name: get_reward
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Reward' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Reward templates — reusable bundles of currency + items + buffs that can be granted to a player. Referenced by Quest, TimedEvent, CoopEvent, Season, DailyLogin, Referral, etc. Define a reward once here, then reference it everywhere instead of inlining payouts.

value.title: RewardDefinitions
value.description: Root config for universal, system-agnostic rewards. Umbrella over four independent subsystems: DailyCalendars, IdleAccruals, Comebacks, Claims.

TierRewards.description: Global tier-reward resolution rules applied to all tiered systems of the title (premium, season, etc.). Null uses defaults (Additive / NoStack).

MilestoneRewardMultiplier.description: Title-wide progression-based milestone reward multiplier (cash multiplier). Applies to ALL milestones of every system (TimedEvent, Leaderboard, DealOffer, Quest, CommunityChest, Referral) via MilestoneRewardResolver as the last overlay. Targeting (IncludeRewards/ExcludeRewards, ResourceBundle by Type+ID; empty = all rewards) is configured in the spec. null = disabled.

DailyCalendars.description: Daily-login calendars. Each calendar is an independent day-by-day progression. Empty/null disables the subsystem.

IdleAccruals.description: Idle-income accruals. Each is an independent resource stream with its own rate, cap and activation requirements. Empty/null disables the subsystem.

Comebacks.description: Comeback reward configs (return-after-absence). Each is an independent policy. Empty/null disables the subsystem.

Claims.description: Simple click-to-claim rewards. Supports one-shot bonuses, repeating claims with rolling-window limits, and server-triggered rewards. Empty/null disables the subsystem.

Windows.description: Reward windows: the end-of-round 'Claim N / x3 for an ad / x5 VIP' screen. Key = window id the game sends. Empty/null disables the subsystem.

Presets.description: Registry of reusable reward config blocks. null = presets unused. Expanded once when the config is materialized (PlatformCache.ResolveCompositeSections).

TierRewardSettings.description: Global tier-reward resolution rules applied to ALL tiered systems of the title (premium, season, battle pass, etc.). One mode per title.

RewardMode.description: Tier-reward resolution mode. Additive: tier rewards are added on top of the base reward. Replace: tier rewards fully replace the base reward.

RewardStackLowerTiers.description: Whether lower-tier rewards stack with higher-tier ones. True: a player at tier 5 gets tiers 1..5 merged. False: only the best matching tier.

x-enum-descriptions: Rewards are granted on top of the base Rewards.
Rewards fully replace the base Rewards.

RewardProgressionMultiplierSpec.description: Milestone overlay: progression-based reward multiplier (cash multiplier). Scales targeted milestone rewards of ANY type — currencies, items and event tokens — by a multiplier derived from a configurable player progression metric (Source) via a shared platform curve (ScalarCurveSpec). What gets scaled is a strictly typed set IncludeRewards/ExcludeRewards (ResourceBundle, matched by Type + ID); empty Include = ALL. Applied in RewardProgressionResolver inside MilestoneRewardResolver, after bonus-window and season-tier. null on a milestone = disabled.

Source.description: Which player progression metric to read (see ProgressionSource).

SourceKey.description: Extra key for sources that need a parameter: VirtualCurrencyBalance -> CurrencyID; SeasonTier -> SeasonChainID; EventTokenTotalEarned -> "{bucket}:{entityID}" (bucket: TimedEvent/Leaderboard/Season/CoopEvent/Quest/DealOffer); CharacterLevel -> CharacterID (empty = "Main"). Ignored for other sources.

Curve.description: Multiplier curve: how the multiplier grows with progress. Evaluated over a base of 1.0, so an unset curve means a multiplier of 1 and an unchanged reward. Shape/PerStep/Points/Interpolation/MinResult/MaxResult are documented on ScalarCurveSpec.

Anchor.description: Progress value from which the curve starts counting. Empty = from zero.

IncludeRewards.description: Rewards to scale — a strictly typed set (ResourceBundle): currencies/items in Entries (matched by Type + ID: ItemID for items, else CurrencyID), event tokens in EventTokens (matched by Address.EntityID). Entry Amount is ignored — this is a selector, not a grant. null/empty (no Entries and no EventTokens) = apply to ALL milestone rewards.

ExcludeRewards.description: Rewards to exclude (same ResourceBundle shape as IncludeRewards). Takes precedence: a reward matched by Type + ID is never scaled. null/empty = no exclusions.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Credits, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account (players see it as "Aspis" — write Aspis in player-facing text). Requires only Amount — the price in whole Credits. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCreditsPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted by every sale of the game author: Store, Lootbox, Collection packs, Craft, DealOffer, TimedBoost, Premium, Item and Character upgrades, skins, CoopEvent spins, GameLoop special mode entry, Workshop publish fee, InApp AI (charged only when the generation is ready). NOT accepted in player-to-player prices or refundable fees (Marketplace listing fee, PvP Match creation) - those refuse with CREDITS_NOT_ALLOWED_HERE; batch calls refuse too. Allowed only in Consume: Credits are never a reward anywhere.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

Type.description: System the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

DailyCalendarDefinition.description: Config of one daily-reward calendar: an ordered sequence of days with per-day rewards. Miss-behavior and claim-mode are calendar-level settings.

CalendarID.description: Unique calendar identifier. Used as the key in UserRewardState.DailyCalendars. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

DisplayName.description: Display name of the calendar for UI.

AssetPaths.description: Arbitrary UI assets (icon, banner, background, etc.). Designer-defined keys. Does not affect server logic.

Days.description: Per-day reward config sorted by DayNumber. Day numbers must be unique starting from 1.

IsLooping.description: After the last day: true loops back to day 1 (infinite calendar); false stops giving rewards.

MissBehavior.description: Action to take on a missed-window progress (see MissThresholdMultiplier).

ResetByDays.description: Used only with MissBehavior = ResetBy: number of days to roll CollectedDays back on miss. Lower bound is 0.

MissThresholdMultiplier.description: Allowed-miss multiplier. Default 2.0 means more than 2 claim units missed in a row triggers MissBehavior.

ClaimMode.description: Mode that determines when a new claim becomes available.

ClaimCooldownSeconds.description: Used only with ClaimMode = SlidingWindow: minimum seconds between consecutive claims.

Availability.description: Who can access the calendar — unified SegmentGate. null/empty = everyone. Lives in the Availability block so it can be shared via presets.

Presets.description: Preset wiring (the Availability block). null = presets unused.

AvailableFromUtc.description: Calendar is unavailable before this UTC moment. Null means no lower bound.

AvailableUntilUtc.description: Calendar is unavailable from this UTC moment onwards. Null means no upper bound.

DailyRewardDay.description: Config of one day in a daily-rewards calendar.

DayNumber.description: Explicit day number (starting from 1). Unique within the calendar; next expected day = CollectedDays + 1.

Rewards.description: Rewards for this day. Supports the full platform premium logic via PremiumBonuses / PremiumTiers.

IsMilestone.description: UI flag for a milestone day (e.g. day 7/14/30). Does not affect server logic; only a hint for the client.

AssetPaths.description: Optional per-day assets (day icon, chest artwork). Designer-defined keys.

ResourceGrant.description: Grant direction container for ResourceOperation. Two independent premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumBonuses applies a percentage uplift to Standard (single best tier wins, no stack), and PremiumTiers provides structurally different rewards governed by cfg.Reward.TierRewards (Additive or Replace mode; in Replace the bonused Standard is wiped). Both mechanisms can be used together or independently.

Standard.description: Base — what to grant to all players including F2P.

PremiumBonuses.description: Percentage uplift on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 + Bonus)). Wiped under Mode=Replace if any PremiumTier matches.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different rewards for premium players (different ItemID/Target/...). Governed by global cfg.Reward.TierRewards.RewardMode (Additive/Replace) and RewardStackLowerTiers.

PremiumTierBonus.description: Percentage bonus on ResourceGrant.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 + Bonus) with Math.Ceiling rounding. Applies only to Standard; in Replace mode the bonused Standard is wiped when any PremiumTier matches. Best matching tier wins, bonuses do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierDiscount.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Bonus.description: Bonus as a SHARE: 0.1 = +10%, 1.0 = double (x2). Empty or 0 = no bonus. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).

x-enum-descriptions: Miss has no effect; next day = CollectedDays + 1. Soft calendar.
On miss, resets CollectedDays to 0. Streak calendar.
On miss, rolls CollectedDays back by ResetByDays. Partial penalty.
New claim available on a new UTC date (LastClaimAt.Date < today). Simple and predictable; ignores player timezone.
New claim available ClaimCooldownSeconds after the previous one. Timezone-friendly but the claim slot drifts over time.

RewardAvailability.description: Reward availability block: audience gate plus claim limits. Direct analogue of QuestAvailability and TimedBoostAvailability. All fields are nullable without initializers — required by preset merging. Read only via RewardDefinitionDefaults.

Gate.description: Who the reward is available to. null/empty = everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Limits.description: Claim limits (CooldownSeconds, MaxPerWindow + WindowSeconds, TotalCap). 0 on an axis = unlimited. null = no limits. Applies to ClaimRewardDefinition; unused by other reward types.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

LimitSpec.description: Unified anti-farm limits ("how much / how often"). Replaces TriggerLimits (Scheduling), DealNodeLimitsDefinition (DealOffer), StoreOfferRules caps (Store) and ClaimRewardDefinition sliding fields (Reward). 0 on an axis = no limit. Superset of axes with DIFFERENT enforcement semantics: DailyCap/DailyWeightCap = calendar UTC day; MaxPerWindow/WindowSeconds = sliding window. Usually one set is filled per system, the rest = 0. Counters are stored/enforced by each system; this is config thresholds only.

TotalCap.description: Lifetime cap per user. 0 = no limit.

DailyCap.description: Cap on triggers/actions per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

DailyWeightCap.description: Cap on weight (e.g. token amount) per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

PerActivationCap.description: Cap within a single activation/session. 0 = no limit.

MaxPerWindow.description: Sliding window: max triggers within WindowSeconds. 0 = disabled.

WindowSeconds.description: Sliding-window length (seconds). Used only when MaxPerWindow > 0.

RewardPresetBindings.description: Container of preset wiring — one PresetBinding per block. Inline data lives on the definition itself. null = presets unused.

Availability.description: Preset binding for the Availability block.

PresetBinding.description: Wiring for one preset block of an entity: a reference into the module's preset registry + optional keys to drop. Reusable Core container, one per preset-able block, held inside the entity's Presets container. Replaces the former scattered flat *PresetID / *Remove fields. Combination is data-driven, no mode (PresetResolver): no PresetID -> inline only; preset + empty inline -> preset; preset + inline -> merge (preset base + inline overrides/adds by key), Remove drops keys. For a single object (Character Equipment) there is nothing to key-merge, so inline wins when both are present.

PresetID.description: Preset key in the module registry (e.g. LeaderboardDefinitions.Presets.Milestones[PresetID]). Empty/null = preset unused (inline layer only).

Remove.description: Keys removed from the merged result. Dictionary key for dictionaries; element key for keyed lists (Rank / SlotID / RuleID). null = remove nothing. Ignored when no preset is set.

IdleAccrualDefinition.description: Config of one idle-income accrual. Income accrues at IdleRateConfig while offline; claim computes accrued seconds (capped), applies the rate, and scales Rewards.

AccrualID.description: Unique accrual identifier. Used as the key in UserRewardState.IdleAccruals. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

AssetPaths.description: Arbitrary UI assets. Designer-defined keys.

Rate.description: Rate composition. Final rate per second = (base + Power and BoardRank coefficients + equipment IdleRateBonus sum) × best premium multiplier.

Rewards.description: Base reward set. Standard amounts are multiplied by (accruedSeconds × finalRatePerSecond) at claim time. PremiumBonuses/PremiumTiers pass through to ResourceService.

MaxAccumulationSeconds.description: Max accumulation time in seconds. Time beyond this is forfeited. 0 means no cap (risky for long-term economy).

MinClaimSeconds.description: Minimum seconds between two claims of the same accrual. Anti-spam. 0 means no limit.

Requirements.description: Activation requirements. All must be satisfied at claim time, otherwise the claim is denied. Denial does not move LastCollectAt.

FirstClaimMode.description: Behavior on the player's first access to this accrual (when LastCollectAt = MinValue).

AvailableFromUtc.description: Accrual is unavailable before this UTC moment. Null means no lower bound. Also used as accrual-start with AccruedFromConfigStart.

AvailableUntilUtc.description: Accrual is unavailable from this UTC moment onwards. Null means no upper bound.

IdleRateConfig.description: Accrual rate formula composition. All addends are summed, then multiplied by the best matching premium multiplier.

BaseRatePerSecond.description: Constant base rate in units per second. Applied to every player unconditionally.

PowerCoefficient.description: Coefficient multiplied by user.PublicData.Power and added to the rate. 0 disables the addend.

BoardRankCoefficient.description: Coefficient multiplied by user.PublicData.BoardRank and added to the rate. 0 disables the addend.

EquipmentBonusEnabled.description: Whether to include the sum of IdleRateBonus from items equipped on EquipmentCharacterID. False disables the addend.

EquipmentCharacterID.description: Character from which to compute the equipment bonus. Null/empty falls back to DefaultData.Main.

PremiumMultipliers.description: Premium rate multipliers. One best-matching multiplier is picked (highest MinPremiumTier) — multipliers do not stack. Defaults to 1.0 when none match.

PremiumTierMultiplier.description: Premium multiplier of an arbitrary value (e.g. idle accrual rate) — third type of premium modifier alongside PremiumTierBonus and PremiumTierDiscount. Best matching tier wins, multipliers do not stack. If no tier matches, effective multiplier is 1.0.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Multiplier.description: Multiplier value. 1.0 = neutral, 2.0 = double, 0.5 = half. Not clamped by the platform; consumer code is responsible for validating non-positive values.

IdleAccrualRequirements.description: Accrual activation conditions. Each field is optional; all set conditions must hold simultaneously (AND).

MinCharacterLevel.description: Minimum level of RequirementsCharacterID. 0 means the condition is not checked.

RequirementsCharacterID.description: Character against which MinCharacterLevel and RequiredEquippedItemIDs are checked. Null/empty falls back to DefaultData.Main.

Availability.description: Premium/audience gate — unified SegmentGate. null/empty = not checked. (Gameplay requirements MinCharacterLevel/RequiredEquippedItemIDs stay separate.) Lives in the Availability block so it can be shared via presets.

RequiredItemIDs.description: ItemIDs each of which must be present in the player's inventory (TotalAmount > 0). Null/empty means the condition is not checked.

RequiredEquippedItemIDs.description: ItemIDs each of which must be equipped on RequirementsCharacterID. Null/empty means the condition is not checked.

x-enum-descriptions: First claim yields 0 and sets LastCollectAt = now. No write on read; player forfeits the first accrual.
On the very first access (incl. read-only), the server initializes LastCollectAt = now. Accrual starts on first sight; costs a DB write on first read.
Accrual counted from AvailableFromUtc. Falls back to now when null. Late joiners get income for the elapsed period (capped by MaxAccumulationSeconds).

ComebackRewardDefinition.description: Config of a single comeback reward (for return after long absence). Tier is locked at the moment of return, not at claim time.

ComebackID.description: Unique comeback config identifier. Used as the key in UserRewardState.Comebacks. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

AssetPaths.description: Arbitrary UI assets. Designer-defined keys.

Tiers.description: Reward tiers by absence duration. The tier with the largest matching MinAbsenceSeconds is locked when pending is fixed.

ClaimCooldownSeconds.description: Minimum seconds between consecutive comeback claims of this config. 0 means no limit.

ClaimWindowSeconds.description: Seconds the pending reward stays available for claim after return. Beyond it the pending is cleared. 0 means infinite.

TrackPresenceOnRead.description: Whether to update LastSeenAt and fix pending in read-only methods. True tracks presence on any call; false confines updates to claim methods.

Availability.description: Who can access the comeback — unified SegmentGate. null/empty = everyone. Lives in the Availability block so it can be shared via presets.

Presets.description: Preset wiring (the Availability block). null = presets unused.

AvailableFromUtc.description: Comeback is unavailable before this UTC moment.

AvailableUntilUtc.description: Comeback is unavailable from this UTC moment onwards.

ComebackTier.description: One tier of a comeback reward.

MinAbsenceSeconds.description: Minimum absence in seconds to qualify for this tier. Compared against (now - LastSeenAt).TotalSeconds at return time.

Rewards.description: Tier reward. Supports the full premium logic (PremiumBonuses / PremiumTiers).

AssetPaths.description: Optional per-tier assets. Designer-defined keys.

ClaimRewardDefinition.description: Config of a simple claim reward. Covers one-shot, repeating-with-limits, and server-triggered scenarios; all limits are optional and combinable.

ClaimID.description: Unique identifier. Used as the key in UserRewardState.Claims. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

AssetPaths.description: Arbitrary UI assets. Designer-defined keys.

Mode.description: Who initiates the claim. Manual: player via client API. Auto: server-only (background job, GM grant, compensation); client calls are rejected.

Rewards.description: Reward to grant. Supports the full premium logic (PremiumBonuses / PremiumTiers).

Availability.description: Claim limits — unified LimitSpec: CooldownSeconds (min seconds between claims); MaxPerWindow + WindowSeconds (sliding "N per M seconds", checked against RecentClaimTimestamps, not calendar-aligned); TotalCap (all-time, 1 = one-shot). 0 on an axis = no limit. Per-tier overrides via PremiumLimitOverrides.

Presets.description: Preset wiring (the Availability block). null = presets unused.

PremiumLimitOverrides.description: Per-tier overrides of limits and cooldown for premium players. One best-matching override is picked (highest MinPremiumTier) — does not stack.

AvailableFromUtc.description: Reward is unavailable before this UTC moment.

AvailableUntilUtc.description: Reward is unavailable from this UTC moment onwards.

x-enum-descriptions: Player initiates the claim via the client API (RewardV2.ClaimReward).
Server-only (background job, GM grant, anti-fraud compensation). Client ClaimReward is rejected.

ClaimLimitOverride.description: Per-tier override of limits and cooldown for a ClaimRewardDefinition. One best-matching override by MinPremiumTier is picked; null fields fall back to base values.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier this override applies to.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Specific premium-ID. Null means any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

CooldownSeconds.description: Override for CooldownSeconds. Null does not override.

MaxClaimsPerWindow.description: Override for MaxClaimsPerWindow. Null does not override; 0 removes the limit for this tier.

WindowSeconds.description: Override for WindowSeconds. Null does not override.

TotalClaimLimit.description: Override for TotalClaimLimit. Null does not override.

RewardWindowDefinition.description: Reward window: the end-of-round screen 'Claim N / x3 for an ad / x5 VIP'. The game reports the round's amount; the server caps it (MaxBaseAmount, daily limits) and picks the multiplier itself: AdMultiplier only after a verified view of AdPlacementID (one view = one window), VipMultiplier only with an active premium subscription.

CurrencyID.description: Currency the window grants (a virtual currency id of the title).

MaxBaseAmount.description: Cap on the base amount of one window: the game may report more, the player gets at most this before the multiplier.

AdPlacementID.description: Rewarded placement (Advertising.Placements) whose verified view unlocks AdMultiplier. Empty = no ad button.

AdMultiplier.description: Multiplier after a verified ad view. Null = 3.

VipMultiplier.description: Multiplier for a VIP player, no ad. Null = 5; 0 or 1 = no VIP button.

VipPremiumID.description: Which premium subscription counts as VIP. Empty = any active subscription of the title.

Limits.description: Limits: DailyCap (windows per UTC day), DailyWeightCap (amount granted per UTC day, after the multiplier), CooldownSeconds, TotalCap. Null = defaults (200 windows a day, 5 s cooldown).

RewardPresetRegistry.description: Registry of reusable reward config blocks. The field mirrors the same-named definition block. Analogue of QuestPresetRegistry.

Availability.description: Reusable availability blocks (gate + limits), keyed by PresetID.

tools.name: get_user_custom_data
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'UserCustomData' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Schema for per-player custom data fields — name, type, default value, visibility, whether the client can write it. This is the SCHEMA only; actual per-user values live on the User document. Use this to declare new player-specific stats, flags, or progress counters.

tools.name: save_user_custom_data
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'UserCustomData' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Schema for per-player custom data fields — name, type, default value, visibility, whether the client can write it. This is the SCHEMA only; actual per-user values live on the User document. Use this to declare new player-specific stats, flags, or progress counters.

value.title: UserCustomDataDefinitions
value.description: Configuration of the Custom User Data V2 system (arbitrary user records). Hybrid architecture combining bucket-based privacy separation (Private/Public/ReadOnly/Internal) with optional typed key schema.

Keys.description: Schema-managed keys. Dictionary key is UserCustomDataKeyDefinition.KeyID. Writes to these keys are validated against the schema (Bucket / ValueType / MaxValueLengthBytes / TtlSeconds). Unregistered keys are either treated as free-form or rejected based on RejectUnregisteredKeys.

DefaultMaxValueLengthBytes.description: Default size limit of UserCustomDataRecord.Value in bytes (UTF-8). Applied to unregistered keys when RejectUnregisteredKeys = false. Registered keys use their own MaxValueLengthBytes. Recommended: 8192 (8 KB).

DefaultTtlSeconds.description: Default TTL for unregistered keys, in seconds. null means no TTL (permanent). When set, free-form writes get ExpiresAt = now + DefaultTtlSeconds. Registered keys use their own TtlSeconds.

MaxKeysPerBucket.description: Maximum number of keys allowed per bucket (applied uniformly to Private/Public/ReadOnly/Internal). Protects against unbounded dictionary growth in the bson document. Recommended: 128.

MaxTotalSizeBytes.description: Total size limit of all Custom User Data V2 per player across all four buckets, in bytes. Protects against MongoDB's 16 MB bson document limit. Recommended: 1,500,000 (~1.5 MB).

RejectUnregisteredKeys.description: If true, writes to unregistered keys are rejected (strict schema mode). If false, unregistered keys are accepted as free-form with default limits. Default: false.

UserCustomDataKeyDefinition.description: Description of a single registered (schema-managed) Custom User Data V2 key. Defines a fixed Bucket and validation rules (ValueType / MaxValueLengthBytes / TtlSeconds) applied on every write.

KeyID.description: Unique identifier of the key across all buckets. Matches the key in UserCustomDataDefinitions.Keys and in the corresponding bucket dictionary. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

Bucket.description: Bucket where the record will physically reside. Defines both privacy (who reads) and writability (who writes). Fixed at config level; client cannot move the key between buckets.

ValueType.description: Expected format of UserCustomDataRecord.Value: String (arbitrary), Int (long.TryParse), Bool ("true"/"false"), or Json (valid JSON document). Validated by server before the DB patch.

MaxValueLengthBytes.description: Hard size limit of UserCustomDataRecord.Value in bytes (UTF-8) for this key. Overrides UserCustomDataDefinitions.DefaultMaxValueLengthBytes. Writes exceeding the limit are rejected before the DB patch.

TtlSeconds.description: Key TTL in seconds. null means no TTL (permanent record). When set, every write computes ExpiresAt = now + TtlSeconds. Expired records are filtered on read and atomically purged on next write to the same bucket.

DefaultValue.description: Default value returned by the API when no record with this KeyID exists or it has expired. null means absent keys are returned as absent. Default is used on read only; not materialized in the DB until an explicit write.

Description.description: Developer-facing description of the key's purpose for documentation. Not returned to the client in Get* operations and does not affect validation.

x-enum-descriptions: Visible only to the owner. Client can read and write. Examples: personal UI settings, tutorial progress, local preferences.
Visible to the owner and to any other player via cross-user endpoints. Client can read and write its own. Examples: custom title, bio string, avatar frame color, badges.
Visible only to the owner. Client can read but cannot write; only the server writes into this bucket. Examples: tutorial progress, server-side feature flags, A/B variants.
Never returned to the client. Server jobs / admin / analytics only. Cross-user endpoints do not see this bucket. Examples: anti-cheat marks, risk score, segmentation metadata.
Arbitrary string. Validated by length only.
Integer. Must parse as long via long.TryParse. Returned to the client as a string.
Boolean. Must be "true" or "false" (case-insensitive, via bool.TryParse).
Valid JSON document. Any structure parseable via JToken.Parse. Size limited by MaxValueLengthBytes.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Usage' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Retention policy for the player's activity history (Usage). The engine keeps a rolling window of per-day records and folds everything older into monthly totals, then months of finished years into yearly totals — otherwise the per-day map grows forever inside the hottest document on the platform. WARNING: the fold is IRREVERSIBLE, per-day detail outside the window is gone for good. Do not lower DailyWindowDays below 400 without also lowering the analytics range cap: publisher analytics (DAU/WAU/MAU, retention cohorts, funnels) is computed lazily from those very per-day records, accepts ranges of up to 366 days, and needs 30 extra preceding days per requested day for MAU. Also holds SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes: how many minutes of silence end a session (default 30, the same rule Firebase/GA4 use, so the two reports stay comparable). The session boundary is decided by the SERVER from the player's last activity — the client's IsNewSession flag is not trusted for counting. Leave every field null unless you have a specific reason — the defaults (enabled, 400-day window, 30-minute session gap) are what the analytics horizon was sized against.

tools.name: save_usage
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Usage' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Retention policy for the player's activity history (Usage). The engine keeps a rolling window of per-day records and folds everything older into monthly totals, then months of finished years into yearly totals — otherwise the per-day map grows forever inside the hottest document on the platform. WARNING: the fold is IRREVERSIBLE, per-day detail outside the window is gone for good. Do not lower DailyWindowDays below 400 without also lowering the analytics range cap: publisher analytics (DAU/WAU/MAU, retention cohorts, funnels) is computed lazily from those very per-day records, accepts ranges of up to 366 days, and needs 30 extra preceding days per requested day for MAU. Also holds SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes: how many minutes of silence end a session (default 30, the same rule Firebase/GA4 use, so the two reports stay comparable). The session boundary is decided by the SERVER from the player's last activity — the client's IsNewSession flag is not trusted for counting. Leave every field null unless you have a specific reason — the defaults (enabled, 400-day window, 30-minute session gap) are what the analytics horizon was sized against.

value.title: UsageDefinitions

RollupEnabled.description: Master switch for usage history rollup (days -> months -> years). Null = enabled. Turn off temporarily when you need full per-day history retained; the rollup is irreversible.

DailyWindowDays.description: How many recent days are kept per-day before being folded into monthly totals. Null = 400. Do not set below 400 unless you also lower the analytics range cap: publisher analytics reads these per-day records lazily, accepts a range of up to 366 days, and each requested day additionally needs the 30 preceding days for MAU.

MaxDaysFoldedPerPass.description: Max per-day records folded in a single login. Null = 400. Not a gameplay limit — just batch size; the remainder is folded on the next login.

SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes of inactivity that end a session. Null = 30 (same rule as Firebase/GA4, so the two reports stay comparable). The boundary is decided by the server from the player's last activity — the client's IsNewSession flag is not trusted for counting.

value.description: New value for the Usage field.

tools.name: get_timed_event
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'TimedEvent' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Solo time-limited events — daily challenges, weekly missions, holiday events, login streaks. Defines event IDs, schedules (start/end/recurrence), objectives, progress tracking, milestone rewards. For multi-player team events use CoopEvent; for long-form battle-pass-style progression use Season.

tools.name: save_timed_event
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'TimedEvent' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Solo time-limited events — daily challenges, weekly missions, holiday events, login streaks. Defines event IDs, schedules (start/end/recurrence), objectives, progress tracking, milestone rewards. For multi-player team events use CoopEvent; for long-form battle-pass-style progression use Season.

value.title: TimedEventDefinitions
value.description: Root configuration of the limited-time events system. Lives at the top level of TitlePublicConfiguration, separate from GameLoops/Quests/Store. Supports both Scheduled (fixed-date) and Chain (cyclic) events.

Definitions.description: All title events (both Scheduled and Chained) in one dictionary keyed by TimedEventID. The mode (single window vs chain) is determined by Schedule.Mode.

Presets.description: Registry of reusable event presets (milestones / token sources). Phases/events reference them via EventContent.Presets. null = unused.

Settings.description: Global settings shared across all events.

TimedEventDefinition.description: Definition of a single event. The mode lives in Schedule (Mode = Scheduled | Chained): Scheduled = single window (Schedule.Scheduled) + the single Content; Chained = chain of phases (Schedule.Chain) + Events (each phase has its own Content). One dictionary TimedEventDefinitions.Definitions keyed by TimedEventID.

TimedEventID.description: Unique event/chain ID (e.g. "halloween_2026", "main_rotation"). Key in TimedEventDefinitions.Definitions and in the player state.

DisplayName.description: Display name for UI (chain name for Chained; Scheduled may use Content.DisplayName).

AssetPaths.description: Images (icon, banner, background). Keys chosen by the developer.

Schedule.description: Unified schedule container. Mode = Scheduled (single window Schedule.Scheduled) or Chained (chain Schedule.Chain + Events). On/off via Schedule.IsActive.

Content.description: Event content for Mode = Scheduled (token, sources, rewards, milestones, bonus window). For Chained the content lives on the phases (ChainedEventDefinition.Content).

Events.description: Chain phases for Mode = Chained (each with its own DurationSec and Content). After the last phase the cycle restarts. Empty for Scheduled.

Gate.description: Audience gate for the event — standard SegmentGate (Core/Segment), like Store/Reward/TimedBoost/Quest/Experiment. null = available to all. Players failing the gate do not see the event among active ones and cannot grant/spend its tokens.

ScheduleSpec.description: "How an entity activates" container, embedded into each system's definition. Exactly one sub-field is filled for the chosen Mode (plus ActivationTriggers for Triggered). Resolved via ScheduleResolver.

Mode.description: Activation mode. Determines which sub-field is used.

IsActive.description: Unified global on/off. false = entity paused without deleting config (replaces scattered IsActive/Enabled).

Scheduled.description: Single-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Scheduled.

Chain.description: Chain config. Required and used only when Mode = Chained.

Cyclic.description: Calendar-cycle config. Required and used only when Mode = Cyclic.

ActivationTriggers.description: Sources that cause activation/grant. Required and used only when Mode = Triggered. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

Relative.description: Relative-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Relative.

x-enum-descriptions: Active whenever enabled, no time gate (eternal leaderboard, manual boost).
Single fixed window [StartUtc..EndUtc] (see ScheduledWindow).
Recurring ordered list of phases (see ScheduleChain).
Activated/granted when a source fires (see ScheduleSpec.ActivationTriggers).
Calendar-aligned cycles with reset (see CyclicSchedule).

Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see RelativeWindow). Resolved only when a parent is passed to ScheduleResolver.ResolveActive. Enables staged unlocking of sub-entities inside a recurring event (e.g. "Day N opens (N-1)x24h after the current cycle instance start"), so one config auto-repeats without absolute dates.

ScheduledWindow.description: Single fixed-date window. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of ScheduledEventDefinition / LeaderboardScheduledConfig / ScheduledBoostDefinition.

StartUtc.description: Window start (UTC). The entity is active from this moment. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active (BOTH bounds are required).

EndUtc.description: Window end (UTC). After this, earning stops unless AllowEarningAfterEnd. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active.

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after EndUtc (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after EndUtc for claiming rewards. Default 48.

ScheduleChain.description: Recurring phase chain. Holds ONLY chain timing — the phase list lives on the module (a phase composes ScheduleChainPhase + its payload), so the resolver takes a projected IReadOnlyList<ScheduleChainPhase>. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of EventChainDefinition / LeaderboardChainConfig / BoostChainDefinition / CoopEventChainDefinition / SeasonChainDefinition.

AnchorUtc.description: Anchor date (UTC). The first phase of the first cycle starts here; all subsequent dates are computed from the anchor + phase durations + pauses. null = no anchor → the chain is unconfigured and never resolves.

MaxCycles.description: Maximum number of full cycles. 0 = infinite.

PauseBetweenPhasesSec.description: Pause between phases inside one cycle (seconds). 0 = no pause.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: Pause between full cycles (seconds). 0 = no pause.

CyclicSchedule.description: Calendar-aligned cycles with reset. Unified replacement of LeaderboardScheduleMode.Cyclic + LeaderboardCycleReset.

IntervalSeconds.description: FixedInterval only: window length in SECONDS (e.g. 86400 = 1 day, 21600 = 6 hours, 864000 = 10 days). default = 86400 (1 day). Ignored for calendar resets.

AnchorUtc.description: FixedInterval only: anchor instant (coerced to UTC, used as-is including time-of-day) from which IntervalSeconds windows are counted; the anchor defines alignment. null/unset = 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC. Ignored for calendar resets.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: FixedInterval only: pause (SECONDS) between active windows. 0 = back-to-back. When >0 the cycle 'pulses': active for IntervalSeconds, then a pause of this length (inactive during the pause — CanEarn=false/IsInPause), then the next window. Full period = IntervalSeconds + PauseBetweenCyclesSec. Ignored for calendar resets (they are gapless by definition).

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after cycle end to claim previous-cycle rewards. 0 = current cycle only.

x-enum-descriptions: Every CyclicSchedule.IntervalSeconds seconds from CyclicSchedule.AnchorUtc — a fixed interval, not calendar-aligned (e.g. "every 6 hours" or "every 10 days"). Alignment is defined by the anchor.
No reset — eternal (all-time) instance.

TriggerSource.description: Unified trigger source: which game event grants progress/grant and under which filters. Replaces EventTokenSource (TimedEvent), LeaderboardScoreSource (Leaderboard) and BoostTriggerSource (TimedBoost). SourceType reuses the existing EventTokenSourceType. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

SourceType.description: Source type. Identifies which game event fires.

BaseWeight.description: Base "weight" per trigger: token amount (TimedEvent) or score (Leaderboard). Unifies the former BaseAmount/BaseScore. Unused for TimedBoost triggers (a boost has no quantity).

ScaleWithRollMultiplier.description: Whether BaseWeight scales with the player's RollMultiplier. true: Weight = BaseWeight x M_roll. false: fixed amount.

TileTypeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile types (BoardTileType names or CustomTypeID) that fire on landing. Case-insensitive. Empty/null = any tile (not recommended).

TileIndexFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile indices. Empty/null = any index. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter.

ChanceOutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding on Chance tiles. Whitelist of ChanceOutcome.OutcomeID values. Case-insensitive. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter/TileIndexFilter. Empty/null = not applied.

OutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardAttack / BoardRaid / BoardBuild. Whitelist of outcomes. Empty/null = any. BoardAttack: ["HIT"]/["BLOCKED"]; BoardRaid: ["FINISHED_SMALL"]/["FINISHED_MEDIUM"]/["FINISHED_BIG"]; BoardBuild: ["BUILD"]/["STAGE_COMPLETE"].

Params.description: Context parameters for filtering/identifying the source. CustomAction: {"ActionName":"watch_ad"}. QuestComplete: {"QuestID":"win_5_raids"} and/or {"CycleID":"daily"}. StorePurchase: {"OfferID":"starter_pack"}. MarketplaceSell/MarketplaceBuy: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType. An unset or empty parameter means "any". Keys not listed here are not checked by the matcher.

Limits.description: Anti-farm limits of the source — unified LimitSpec (per-day weight cap DailyWeightCap, per-day trigger cap DailyCap, CooldownSeconds). null = no limits (e.g. leaderboards intentionally apply none).

x-enum-descriptions: Landing on an EventToken tile on the board.
Passing start (GO) on the board.
Successful board attack.
Successful board raid.
Building or repairing a structure on the board.
Completing a board stage.

Completing a board Special mode — either via Instant choice or via Claim after the Timed window. Post-resolution source (mirrors BoardAttack/BoardRaid): fires at the final Special reward grant, separately from BoardTileLanding (which fires on the actual tile landing during Roll).
Completing a quest.
Store purchase.
Daily login.
Referral invite.
Token grant as a reward for a milestone or streak in another event. Server-only source — the client cannot invoke it directly.
Arbitrary action — the developer calls the server API with ActionName in Params.
Marketplace (v2) sale — deal settlement on the seller side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
Marketplace (v2) purchase — deal settlement on the buyer side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
In-game currency spend — any scenario where a resource operation actually consumed currency. Server-only source. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.
Opening a lootbox/chest. Server-only source. The multiplier equals how many boxes were opened in the call. Filter Params: LootboxID.

Real-money store purchase (IAP). Server-only source: fired in PurchaseV2 AFTER the receipt is verified and rewards are granted. The multiplier equals the number of product units granted. Filter Params: ProductID, Store. Deliberately separate from StorePurchase, which covers in-game currency spending.
Crypto deposit credited to the in-game balance. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Crypto withdrawal CONFIRMED on chain. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Spending crypto currency in-game. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.

In-game currency GRANT — mirror of CurrencySpent. The multiplier equals the amount granted, so ScaleWithRollMultiplier picks the meaning: "earn N currency" or "receive currency N times". Filter Params: CurrencyID and Origin ("Gameplay" | "RewardClaim"), the latter separating gameplay earnings from reward payouts — without it a goal like "earn N" would be closed by another quest's reward.
CRYPTO currency GRANT in-game (wallet deposits are NOT included — that is CryptoDeposit). The multiplier equals the amount granted. Filter Params: CurrencyID, Origin.

Leaderboard ScoreSources only: the board accepts the NUMBER the game submits itself (SubmitScore / SubmitScoresBatch). Not an event — it grants nothing and matches nothing, it only allows. Without it the board refuses a score from the game: an empty ScoreSources list means the board is not set up. Caps live in Limits: PerActivationCap = max score of ONE submission, DailyCap / DailyWeightCap = submissions / total score per UTC day, CooldownSeconds, MaxPerWindow + WindowSeconds, TotalCap = submissions for all time. A submission over a cap is refused, not trimmed. BaseWeight is not read. Set caps the game can really reach: the client is not trusted, they are the only limit on a forged score.
The player joined a clan (Clan section): by themselves, by application or by invitation. Params: KindID, ClanID. Use for a tutorial step 'join a clan', quests, event tokens.

The player helped the clan: donated to a request (Params.Kind = Request, weight = units) or helped a timer (Params.Kind = Help, weight = 1). Params: KindID, Kind, RequestKindID, ResourceID. Filter by Params.Kind.
The player claimed a clan gift. Params: KindID, GiftID.
The player upgraded an item (Item upgrade, batch included). Weight = levels gained. Params: ItemID, CatalogID, Level (the new level). Server-side only.
The player took revenge for a clanmate on the board (clan Revenge): an attack or raid on the offender of a taken revenge. Params: KindID, ClanID, Action (Attack / Raid). Server-side only.

LimitSpec.description: Unified anti-farm limits ("how much / how often"). Replaces TriggerLimits (Scheduling), DealNodeLimitsDefinition (DealOffer), StoreOfferRules caps (Store) and ClaimRewardDefinition sliding fields (Reward). 0 on an axis = no limit. Superset of axes with DIFFERENT enforcement semantics: DailyCap/DailyWeightCap = calendar UTC day; MaxPerWindow/WindowSeconds = sliding window. Usually one set is filled per system, the rest = 0. Counters are stored/enforced by each system; this is config thresholds only.

TotalCap.description: Lifetime cap per user. 0 = no limit.

DailyCap.description: Cap on triggers/actions per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

DailyWeightCap.description: Cap on weight (e.g. token amount) per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

PerActivationCap.description: Cap within a single activation/session. 0 = no limit.

MaxPerWindow.description: Sliding window: max triggers within WindowSeconds. 0 = disabled.

WindowSeconds.description: Sliding-window length (seconds). Used only when MaxPerWindow > 0.

RelativeWindow.description: Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see ScheduleMode.Relative). Window start = parent.StartUtc + OffsetSecondsFromParentStart. End = start + DurationSeconds, or (if DurationSeconds <= 0) the parent's end; never extends past the parent's end. Lets one config auto-repeat: sub-entity dates are computed from the current parent instance instead of being written absolutely.

OffsetSecondsFromParentStart.description: Window start offset in SECONDS from the parent instance start. 0 = open immediately with the parent. E.g. "Day N" = (N-1) * 86400.

DurationSeconds.description: Window length in SECONDS. 0 (or less) = the window lasts until the parent's end (typical for "stage opens and stays until the event ends"). >0 = lasts exactly that long (but never longer than the parent).

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after the window ends (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after the window ends for claiming rewards. Default 0.

EventContent.description: Event content: display, token, sources, rewards, shop. Unified structure used by both ScheduledEvent and ChainedEvent.

DisplayName.description: Event display name shown in the UI. Example: "Halloween Havoc", "Raid Rush", "Golden Hour".

Description.description: Event description shown in the UI. Example: "Collect Pumpkin Coins and earn spooky rewards!"

AssetPaths.description: Event images (icon, banner, background, etc.). Developer chooses keys and meaning.

Token.description: Event token definition. The token is a separate entity, NOT a VirtualCurrency. Stored in UserEventProgress rather than the VirtualCurrency dictionary.

TokenSources.description: Whitelist of token sources. Developer explicitly enumerates which systems may grant tokens for this event. Sources not on the list are blocked. Uses the unified TriggerSource (BaseWeight = tokens per trigger; Limits = anti-farm caps). Sources not on the list are blocked.

ClaimMode.description: null = unset, platform default applies (see TimedEventDefinitionDefaults.EffectiveClaimMode). Read only via that accessor. When set: Instant = as soon as the threshold is reached, AfterEventEnd = only after the event ends, FeaturedAfterEnd = regular ones instantly, IsFeatured ones after the end.

Milestones.description: Milestone rewards earned after accumulating a certain amount of tokens. Checked against TokensEarnedTotal (not the current balance). When Presets.Milestones is set, this is the override/add layer on top of the preset (merge).

Presets.description: Container of content preset wiring (milestones / token sources). null = presets unused. Resolved by PresetResolver.

BonusWindow.description: Cyclic window of boosted rewards (Coin Master-style). Global schedule across all players. When the bonus phase is active, BonusRewards are added to the base Rewards. null = window disabled for this event.

EventTokenDefinition.description: Event-token definition. An event token is a separate entity, not a VirtualCurrency. Balance lives in UserEventProgress.TokenBalance, ensuring isolation between events and automatic burn-on-end behavior.

DisplayName.description: Token name shown in UI. Example: "Pumpkin Coins", "Raid Points".

AssetPaths.description: Token images: icon and similar assets.

MaxBalance.description: Max token balance the player can accumulate. 0 = unlimited. Protects against unbounded accrual.

MaxPerGrant.description: Max tokens per single grant (anti-abuse). Caps the maximum portion of a single grant.

DailyEarnCap.description: Max tokens per day across all sources. 0 = unlimited. Global daily cap.

BurnOnEventEnd.description: Whether tokens burn at event end. true = balance is zeroed (or converted via BurnConversion). false = tokens persist (collectible).

BurnConversion.description: Conversion rules for the leftover balance at burn. If set, the remainder is converted to the specified VirtualCurrency. null = balance is zeroed without compensation.

EventTokenConversion.description: Conversion rules for event tokens at burn. Lets the platform compensate the player for unused tokens.

TargetCurrencyID.description: What to convert to (VirtualCurrency ID). Example: "IG" (in-game gold), "DICE".

Rate.description: Conversion rate: 1 event token = Rate units of the target currency. Example: 0.1 means 10 tokens = 1 unit of currency.

MaxConvertAmount.description: Max number of tokens eligible for conversion. Inflation guard — if the player has 100000 tokens, only up to MaxConvertAmount is converted.

x-enum-descriptions: Claim instantly when the threshold is reached (accumulated progress >= RequiredProgress). Simplest, most predictable mode.
Claim only after the instance ends (within the system's grace window, if any). All milestones accumulate and are claimed in one batch. Motivates playing to the end.
Hybrid: regular milestones (IsFeatured = false) claim instantly; featured ones (IsFeatured = true) only after the instance ends.

MilestoneDefinition.description: Unified milestone primitive for all platform systems (TimedEvent, Leaderboard, Quest, CommunityChest, DealOffer). Replaces the per-module milestone definitions. Threshold is checked against accumulated progress (RequiredProgress): EventToken systems use EventTokenBalanceData.TotalEarned; CommunityChest uses shared group progress. Reward overlays BonusRewards (bonus-window) and SeasonTierRewards (season-tier) are platform-wide optional fields applied via MilestoneRewardResolver; leave null if unused.

MilestoneID.description: Unique milestone ID within its owning entity (Mongo-safe, claim idempotency key).

DisplayName.description: Display name for UI/CMS. null = unset.

AssetPaths.description: Milestone images (icon, badge). null = unset.

RequiredProgress.description: Threshold over ACCUMULATED progress to unlock. EventToken systems: EventTokenBalanceData.TotalEarned (not current balance). CommunityChest: shared group progress.

Rewards.description: Base rewards. Always granted on a successful claim.

BonusRewards.description: Bonus-window overlay: extra rewards on top of Rewards when the bonus phase is active at claim time (MilestoneRewardContext.BonusActive). Applied via MilestoneRewardResolver. null = no bonus part.

SeasonTierRewards.description: Season-tier overlay: reward scaling by the player's season tier. Applied via MilestoneRewardResolver (SeasonTierRewardResolver.Resolve) only when MilestoneRewardContext.SeasonChainID is set. null = disabled.

SortOrder.description: Sort order in the UI (lower = higher/earlier).

IsFeatured.description: Featured milestone: special UI styling. With MilestoneClaimMode.FeaturedAfterEnd these can only be claimed after the instance ends.

ResourceGrant.description: Grant direction container for ResourceOperation. Two independent premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumBonuses applies a percentage uplift to Standard (single best tier wins, no stack), and PremiumTiers provides structurally different rewards governed by cfg.Reward.TierRewards (Additive or Replace mode; in Replace the bonused Standard is wiped). Both mechanisms can be used together or independently.

Standard.description: Base — what to grant to all players including F2P.

PremiumBonuses.description: Percentage uplift on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 + Bonus)). Wiped under Mode=Replace if any PremiumTier matches.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different rewards for premium players (different ItemID/Target/...). Governed by global cfg.Reward.TierRewards.RewardMode (Additive/Replace) and RewardStackLowerTiers.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.
