EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

Type.description: System the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

PremiumTierBonus.description: Percentage bonus on ResourceGrant.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 + Bonus) with Math.Ceiling rounding. Applies only to Standard; in Replace mode the bonused Standard is wiped when any PremiumTier matches. Best matching tier wins, bonuses do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierDiscount.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Bonus.description: Bonus as a SHARE: 0.1 = +10%, 1.0 = double (x2). Empty or 0 = no bonus. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).

SeasonTierRewardSet.description: Generic container of season-tier reward scaling. Used by any platform system (leaderboards, lootboxes, shop, daily) that wants to scale a ResourceGrant by the player's current tier in a season chain. Empty/null lists = neutral.

Bundles.description: Structurally different rewards for specific tiers. On match, replaces the base ResourceGrant entirely (Replace).

Multipliers.description: Multipliers applied to Amount of the base ResourceGrant. Used ONLY if no Bundles entry matched.

SeasonTierRewardBundle.description: Structurally different rewards for a season-chain tier. Analogous to PremiumTierBundle but the trigger is the player's season tier. Selection picks the single best match (MinSeasonTier <= playerTier); not stacked.

SeasonChainID.description: SeasonChainID this tier is linked to. Selection matches only tiers with the same SeasonChainID.

MinSeasonTier.description: Minimum player season tier required for this bundle to apply. Matches SeasonTierDefinition.Tier / UserSeasonState.CurrentTier.

Rewards.description: Rewards for this tier. Passed unmodified into ResourceService via a regular ResourceOperation.Grant.

SeasonTierRewardMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to Amount of the base ResourceGrant for a season-chain tier. Applied to every ResourceEntry.Amount and EventTokenOperation.Amount in Standard and in PremiumTiers.Resources.

SeasonChainID.description: SeasonChainID this tier is linked to.

MinSeasonTier.description: Minimum player season tier required for this multiplier to apply.

Multiplier.description: Multiplier. 1.0 = neutral (resolver returns the base reward without copying). Rounding: (long)Math.Round(Amount * Multiplier). Entries with final Amount <= 0 are dropped.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

EventTokenDefinition.description: Event-token definition. An event token is a separate entity, not a VirtualCurrency. Balance lives in UserEventProgress.TokenBalance, ensuring isolation between events and automatic burn-on-end behavior.

DisplayName.description: Token name shown in UI. Example: "Pumpkin Coins", "Raid Points".

AssetPaths.description: Token images: icon and similar assets.

MaxBalance.description: Max token balance the player can accumulate. 0 = unlimited. Protects against unbounded accrual.

MaxPerGrant.description: Max tokens per single grant (anti-abuse). Caps the maximum portion of a single grant.

DailyEarnCap.description: Max tokens per day across all sources. 0 = unlimited. Global daily cap.

BurnOnEventEnd.description: Whether tokens burn at event end. true = balance is zeroed (or converted via BurnConversion). false = tokens persist (collectible).

BurnConversion.description: Conversion rules for the leftover balance at burn. If set, the remainder is converted to the specified VirtualCurrency. null = balance is zeroed without compensation.

EventTokenConversion.description: Conversion rules for event tokens at burn. Lets the platform compensate the player for unused tokens.

TargetCurrencyID.description: What to convert to (VirtualCurrency ID). Example: "IG" (in-game gold), "DICE".

Rate.description: Conversion rate: 1 event token = Rate units of the target currency. Example: 0.1 means 10 tokens = 1 unit of currency.

MaxConvertAmount.description: Max number of tokens eligible for conversion. Inflation guard — if the player has 100000 tokens, only up to MaxConvertAmount is converted.

QuestGroupCompletionDefinition.description: Grand reward for completing N tasks sharing the QuestLinking.GroupID label (e.g. "all event tasks"). Counted by the NUMBER of completed quests, unlike cycle milestones which are counted by points.

RequiredCompletedQuests.description: How many quests must be completed (Completed or Claimed). 0 = ALL quests carrying the label per config (this cycle's quests with a matching QuestLinking.GroupID).

Gate.description: Optional audience gate for the reward (Core/Segment). AND-ed with the cycle gate.

PointsReward.description: Points into the cycle track for the completion (optional, on top of per-quest points). 0 = none.

QuestPhaseDefinition.description: One phase of a quest chain: the window (ScheduleChainPhase fields) plus its own content. Analogous to TimedEvent's ChainedEventDefinition, but the content is optional: any unset field falls back to the cycle level, so "eight weeks with identical milestones" is eight empty phases rather than eight copies of the settings.

PhaseID.description: Phase ID, unique within the chain. Mongo-safe — it becomes part of the points-track key.

Order.description: Phase order within the cycle (0, 1, 2...). Defines the sequence.

DurationSec.description: Phase duration in seconds. Must be > 0 or the phase will not resolve.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after the phase ends during which rewards can still be claimed. 0 = only while the phase is active.

AssetPaths.description: Phase assets. null = inherited from the cycle.

CustomParams.description: Arbitrary client-side parameters for the phase. null = inherited from the cycle.

Gate.description: Phase audience gate (Core/Segment). AND-ed with the cycle gate and the quest gate. null = open to everyone the cycle let through.

Milestones.description: Points-track milestones of THIS phase. null = the cycle's milestones are used (one ladder shared by all phases). An empty dictionary explicitly means "no milestones in this phase" and does NOT inherit the cycle's.

Presets.description: Phase preset wiring. Applied to this phase's Milestones.

PointsToken.description: Phase points-token definition. null = the cycle's token.

QuestPresetBindings.description: Preset wiring container — one PresetBinding per block, like CharacterPresetBindings. Bindings are independent: take the schedule from one preset, the reward from another, and write the objectives inline.

Milestones.description: Milestones preset — cycles and chain phases only (merge by MilestoneID).

Availability.description: Availability preset (field-level overlay).

Objectives.description: Objectives preset: merge by ObjectiveID, field-level overlay inside a matched objective, PresetBinding.Remove drops inherited objectives.

PresetBinding.description: Wiring for one preset block of an entity: a reference into the module's preset registry + optional keys to drop. Reusable Core container, one per preset-able block, held inside the entity's Presets container. Replaces the former scattered flat *PresetID / *Remove fields. Combination is data-driven, no mode (PresetResolver): no PresetID -> inline only; preset + empty inline -> preset; preset + inline -> merge (preset base + inline overrides/adds by key), Remove drops keys. For a single object (Character Equipment) there is nothing to key-merge, so inline wins when both are present.

PresetID.description: Preset key in the module registry (e.g. LeaderboardDefinitions.Presets.Milestones[PresetID]). Empty/null = preset unused (inline layer only).

Remove.description: Keys removed from the merged result. Dictionary key for dictionaries; element key for keyed lists (Rank / SlotID / RuleID). null = remove nothing. Ignored when no preset is set.

QuestDefinition.description: Quest definition. Only the ID lives at the root; everything else is split into blocks, each optional and each able to come wholly or partly from a preset (Presets).

QuestID.description: Quest ID (e.g. "win_3_raids"). Mongo-safe. Matches the dictionary key.

Identity.description: Display part: name, description, order, assets, custom params.

Linking.description: Links: cycles, group label, phases, prerequisites.

Availability.description: Availability: window, accrue-while-locked, audience gate, point limits.

Objectives.description: Quest objectives. The quest is completed when ALL objectives are completed. Key = ObjectiveID. Merged by key on top of the preset's objectives, and inside a matched objective the same "unset = from preset" rule applies: "same objective but 50 instead of 15" is { "task": { "TargetValue": 50 } }, not a copy of the triggers.

Reward.description: Claim reward: the grant plus points into the cycle track.

Presets.description: Preset wiring — one binding per block. The only reuse mechanism.

QuestIdentity.description: Display part of a quest. Analogous to CharacterIdentity: everything needed to draw it and nothing that affects the rules.

Description.description: Quest description for UI. Usually shared by a batch of tasks — lives in a preset.

AssetPaths.description: Quest assets (task icon). Key = logical slot name.

CustomParams.description: Arbitrary client-side parameters: things the UI needs to draw that do not belong in the backend schema (localization key, day number, category tag, colour). The engine never interprets them.

QuestLinking.description: Quest links: which cycles and phases it belongs to, which label groups it, and what it depends on. Analogous to CharacterClassification — categorical traits and references.

CycleIDs.description: List of CycleIDs the quest belongs to. Empty list => permanent. Otherwise cyclic, one entry per cycle it appears in.

GroupID.description: Group label (Mongo-safe): UI sections/tabs and the QuestGroupCompletionDefinition grand reward ("complete N tasks of the group"). Just a string — the module has no separate "group" entity.

PhaseIDs.description: Chain phases (QuestPhaseDefinition.PhaseID) in which this quest is active. Empty = every phase of the cycle. Only meaningful for a cycle with Mode = Chained. Gates both progress accrual and claiming.

RequiredQuestIDs.description: Prerequisites: which QuestIDs must be Completed/Claimed. What the dependency affects is set in PrerequisiteMode. The dependency is looked up where its progress lives (permanent -> PermanentQuests; cyclic -> the same cycle, otherwise its first cycle).

PrerequisiteMode.description: What prerequisites (RequiredQuestIDs) affect: BlockProgressAndClaim (default) — the quest does NOT start accruing progress and thus cannot be claimed; BlockClaimOnly — progress accrues immediately but the REWARD cannot be claimed until dependencies complete. Ignored when RequiredQuestIDs is empty.

QuestAvailability.description: Quest access rules: when it is open, who may see it, under which limits. Analogous to CharacterUnlock.

Schedule.description: Per-quest availability/unlock window — standard ScheduleSpec (Core/Scheduling), like TimedEvent/Leaderboard/TimedBoost. Resolved by the same ScheduleResolver: progress accrues while CanEarn, claim allowed while CanClaim (with grace). Unset = the quest inherits its cycle window. This IS the staged unlock: "days" are a special case (Relative windows with staggered starts, or Chained phases).

AccrueProgressWhenLocked.description: Whether to accrue progress while the quest window (Schedule) is not yet open / already closed, as long as the event (cycle) window is active. false (default) — progress follows the quest schedule strictly: a locked stage accrues nothing (the lock on "Day N"). true — progress always accrues within the event window, but the REWARD is still claimable only after unlock. Applies only when Schedule is set.

Gate.description: Quest audience gate — standard SegmentGate (Core/Segment). Unset = available to all. Effective gate = cycle gate AND quest gate.

Limits.description: Limits on this quest's POINT grants into the track — standard LimitSpec (Core/Limits). Mapped into EventTokenGrantContext as per-source caps/cooldown (DailyWeightCap->DailyCapFromSource, DailyCap->DailyTriggerCap, CooldownSeconds). Unset = no per-source limits. Global point caps live in QuestCycleDefinition.PointsToken.

QuestObjectiveDefinition.description: Quest objective — a counter driven by exactly one mechanism, selected by Source: ClientApi/ServerApi advance it by the string key MetricID (client calls Quest/AddQuestProgress, server calls server.AddQuestProgress from CloudCode); SystemEvent advances it from the Triggers list, i.e. the same in-game events (TriggerSource) that feed TimedEvent tokens and leaderboard score — no HTTP call involved. Every field is optional: an objective may be a delta over the preset's objective, setting only TargetValue. An unset field is taken from the objective with the same ObjectiveID in the preset, and only then from the hard default (ClientApi / 0 / 1 / Sum).

ObjectiveID.description: Objective ID within the quest (e.g. "raid_wins"). Mongo-safe. Matches the dictionary key.

Source.description: Who advances the progress. Selects which field is read: MetricID (ClientApi/ServerApi) or Triggers (SystemEvent). Default ClientApi.

MaxProgressPerCall.description: Delta cap for a SINGLE AddQuestProgress call. Applies to ClientApi only: exceeding it is treated as cheating and BANS the player (see QuestV2.AddQuestProgress) rather than silently clamping. Default 0 = no cap. For SystemEvent the step size comes from TriggerSource.BaseWeight.

MetricID.description: Metric key that contributes progress (e.g. "raid_win", "currency_spent"). Read ONLY when Source = ClientApi/ServerApi; matched exactly (Ordinal, trimmed). Ignored for SystemEvent.

Triggers.description: In-game events that advance this objective. Read ONLY when Source = SystemEvent. Same TriggerSource used by EventContent.TokenSources (TimedEvent) and LeaderboardDefinition.ScoreSources: event type + filters (tile, outcome, Params) + BaseWeight as the progress step per fire. Matched by the shared TriggerMatcher; the list is OR-ed. An empty list = the objective never advances.

TargetValue.description: Required value to complete the objective. Default 1. This is the field an objective is normally overridden for on top of a preset.

QuestReward.description: Quest claim reward: the resource grant plus points into the cycle track.

Grant.description: Claim grant. Grant only — ResourceGrant, not ResourceOperation. Premium resolution runs in ResourceService against global cfg.Premium settings.

PointsReward.description: Points into the cycle track ("crown points") granted on quest claim. Default 0 = the quest gives no points. Backed by a Quest token (EventTokenType.Quest, EntityID "{cycleID}:{instanceKey}") inside the same atomic claim TX. Meaningful only for cyclic quests.

QuestPresetRegistry.description: Registry of reusable quest config blocks. Each field is a dictionary keyed by PresetID and mirrors the same-named QuestDefinition block. Direct analogue of CharacterPresetRegistry (Stats / Levels / Equipment).

Milestones.description: Reusable milestone sets (shared MilestoneSet) for cycles and phases, keyed by PresetID.

Linking.description: Reusable linking blocks: cycles, group label, phases, prerequisites.

Availability.description: Reusable availability blocks: window, accrue-while-locked, audience gate, point limits.

Reward.description: Reusable reward blocks: the grant plus points into the cycle track.

Objectives.description: Reusable objective sets (inner dictionary key = ObjectiveID). The preset says HOW an objective advances (Source, Triggers, aggregation); a quest normally overrides only TargetValue.

MilestoneSet.description: Thin wrapper for a reusable milestone set. Its single field mirrors the inline shape (EventContent.Milestones / LeaderboardDefinition.Milestones / DealOfferDefinition.Milestones) so the resolver returns a compatible dictionary. Cross-module type (used by TimedEvent, Leaderboard, DealOffer) -- lives in Core next to MilestoneDefinition. Resolved by PresetResolver.MergeDictionary.

Milestones.description: Milestone set keyed by MilestoneID (same shape as the inline Milestones dictionary).

tools.name: get_tutorial
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Tutorial' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Tutorial / onboarding definitions — flows (ordered scenarios) built from steps that teach the player a mechanic. A step completes either by client acknowledgement or by a real game event (the same TriggerSource vocabulary as Quest), so "make a roll", "buy something", "open a chest" need no client-side bookkeeping. A step may also PREDETERMINE the outcome of another module (TutorialScriptedOutcome — e.g. force the board dice to land on a Raid tile), which is the only way to demonstrate a mechanic instead of randomness. Flows carry an audience gate (SegmentGate) and a schedule (ScheduleSpec); putting an Experiment condition in that gate is how two tutorial versions are A/B-tested. Gating other content on tutorial progress is done via SegmentGate.Tutorial per entity, or via Settings.Blocking to close whole modules until onboarding is finished.

tools.name: save_tutorial
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Tutorial' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Tutorial / onboarding definitions — flows (ordered scenarios) built from steps that teach the player a mechanic. A step completes either by client acknowledgement or by a real game event (the same TriggerSource vocabulary as Quest), so "make a roll", "buy something", "open a chest" need no client-side bookkeeping. A step may also PREDETERMINE the outcome of another module (TutorialScriptedOutcome — e.g. force the board dice to land on a Raid tile), which is the only way to demonstrate a mechanic instead of randomness. Flows carry an audience gate (SegmentGate) and a schedule (ScheduleSpec); putting an Experiment condition in that gate is how two tutorial versions are A/B-tested. Gating other content on tutorial progress is done via SegmentGate.Tutorial per entity, or via Settings.Blocking to close whole modules until onboarding is finished.

value.title: TutorialDefinitions
value.description: Root block of the tutorial (onboarding) system in the title config.

Flows.description: Tutorial flow (onboarding scenario) definitions keyed by FlowID.

Settings.description: Module-wide settings: master switch and the policy for blocking other modules.

Presets.description: Registry of reusable blocks (Core/Presets) — the module's only reuse mechanism. Flows reference it via TutorialFlowDefinition.Presets.

TutorialFlowDefinition.description: Definition of a single onboarding scenario. Only the ID lives at the root; everything else is split into blocks, each optional and each able to come wholly or partly from a preset.

FlowID.description: Flow ID (e.g. "first_session"). Mongo-safe. Matches the dictionary key.

Identity.description: Display part: name, description, order, assets, custom params.

Availability.description: Availability: schedule, audience gate, prerequisites, event-driven auto-start.

Policy.description: Policy: skipping, restart, expiry, blocking flag, feature unlocks.

Steps.description: Flow steps keyed by StepID. Ordering comes from TutorialStepDefinition.Order, not from key order — BSON dictionaries guarantee no order. Merged by key on top of the preset's steps, with the same "unset = from preset" rule inside a matched step.

Presets.description: Preset wiring — one binding per block.

TutorialIdentity.description: Display part of a flow: everything needed to draw it and nothing that affects the rules.

DisplayNameKey.description: Localization key for the name. When set, the client resolves it via its own dictionary and ignores DisplayName; when empty, DisplayName is shown as-is.

DescriptionKey.description: Localization key for the description. Same semantics as DisplayNameKey.

AssetPaths.description: Flow assets (icon, banner). Key = logical slot name.

CustomParams.description: Arbitrary client-side parameters: things the UI needs to draw that do not belong in the backend schema (theme, category tag, colour). The engine never interprets them.

TutorialAvailability.description: Flow access rules: when it is open, who may see it, what starts it.

Schedule.description: Availability window — standard ScheduleSpec (Core/Scheduling). Unset = always available (equivalent to AlwaysOn). Plain onboarding needs no schedule; a seasonal tutorial for a new feature does.

Gate.description: Audience gate — standard SegmentGate (Core/Segment). Unset = available to all. A/B lives HERE: Gate.Experiment binds the flow to an experiment variant, so two tutorial versions differ by a single config field.

RequiredFlowIDs.description: Prerequisites: which FlowIDs must be finished (Completed or Skipped) first. Empty = no gate.

AutoStart.description: Auto-start on the first request from a player who passes the gate. Default true — onboarding must start by itself: a client that forgets to call StartFlow would otherwise silently leave the player without a tutorial. false = the flow starts only via an explicit call or a trigger.

StartTrigger.description: Game event that starts the flow (the same TriggerSource used by quests). When set, the flow starts on a fire regardless of AutoStart. Needed for just-in-time tutorials: explain raids not at session start but when the player first lands on the matching tile.

ScheduleSpec.description: "How an entity activates" container, embedded into each system's definition. Exactly one sub-field is filled for the chosen Mode (plus ActivationTriggers for Triggered). Resolved via ScheduleResolver.

Mode.description: Activation mode. Determines which sub-field is used.

IsActive.description: Unified global on/off. false = entity paused without deleting config (replaces scattered IsActive/Enabled).

Scheduled.description: Single-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Scheduled.

Chain.description: Chain config. Required and used only when Mode = Chained.

Cyclic.description: Calendar-cycle config. Required and used only when Mode = Cyclic.

ActivationTriggers.description: Sources that cause activation/grant. Required and used only when Mode = Triggered. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

Relative.description: Relative-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Relative.

x-enum-descriptions: Active whenever enabled, no time gate (eternal leaderboard, manual boost).
Single fixed window [StartUtc..EndUtc] (see ScheduledWindow).
Recurring ordered list of phases (see ScheduleChain).
Activated/granted when a source fires (see ScheduleSpec.ActivationTriggers).
Calendar-aligned cycles with reset (see CyclicSchedule).

Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see RelativeWindow). Resolved only when a parent is passed to ScheduleResolver.ResolveActive. Enables staged unlocking of sub-entities inside a recurring event (e.g. "Day N opens (N-1)x24h after the current cycle instance start"), so one config auto-repeats without absolute dates.

ScheduledWindow.description: Single fixed-date window. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of ScheduledEventDefinition / LeaderboardScheduledConfig / ScheduledBoostDefinition.

StartUtc.description: Window start (UTC). The entity is active from this moment. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active (BOTH bounds are required).

EndUtc.description: Window end (UTC). After this, earning stops unless AllowEarningAfterEnd. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active.

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after EndUtc (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after EndUtc for claiming rewards. Default 48.

ScheduleChain.description: Recurring phase chain. Holds ONLY chain timing — the phase list lives on the module (a phase composes ScheduleChainPhase + its payload), so the resolver takes a projected IReadOnlyList<ScheduleChainPhase>. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of EventChainDefinition / LeaderboardChainConfig / BoostChainDefinition / CoopEventChainDefinition / SeasonChainDefinition.

AnchorUtc.description: Anchor date (UTC). The first phase of the first cycle starts here; all subsequent dates are computed from the anchor + phase durations + pauses. null = no anchor → the chain is unconfigured and never resolves.

MaxCycles.description: Maximum number of full cycles. 0 = infinite.

PauseBetweenPhasesSec.description: Pause between phases inside one cycle (seconds). 0 = no pause.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: Pause between full cycles (seconds). 0 = no pause.

CyclicSchedule.description: Calendar-aligned cycles with reset. Unified replacement of LeaderboardScheduleMode.Cyclic + LeaderboardCycleReset.

IntervalSeconds.description: FixedInterval only: window length in SECONDS (e.g. 86400 = 1 day, 21600 = 6 hours, 864000 = 10 days). default = 86400 (1 day). Ignored for calendar resets.

AnchorUtc.description: FixedInterval only: anchor instant (coerced to UTC, used as-is including time-of-day) from which IntervalSeconds windows are counted; the anchor defines alignment. null/unset = 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC. Ignored for calendar resets.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: FixedInterval only: pause (SECONDS) between active windows. 0 = back-to-back. When >0 the cycle 'pulses': active for IntervalSeconds, then a pause of this length (inactive during the pause — CanEarn=false/IsInPause), then the next window. Full period = IntervalSeconds + PauseBetweenCyclesSec. Ignored for calendar resets (they are gapless by definition).

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after cycle end to claim previous-cycle rewards. 0 = current cycle only.

x-enum-descriptions: Every CyclicSchedule.IntervalSeconds seconds from CyclicSchedule.AnchorUtc — a fixed interval, not calendar-aligned (e.g. "every 6 hours" or "every 10 days"). Alignment is defined by the anchor.
No reset — eternal (all-time) instance.

TriggerSource.description: Unified trigger source: which game event grants progress/grant and under which filters. Replaces EventTokenSource (TimedEvent), LeaderboardScoreSource (Leaderboard) and BoostTriggerSource (TimedBoost). SourceType reuses the existing EventTokenSourceType. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

SourceType.description: Source type. Identifies which game event fires.

BaseWeight.description: Base "weight" per trigger: token amount (TimedEvent) or score (Leaderboard). Unifies the former BaseAmount/BaseScore. Unused for TimedBoost triggers (a boost has no quantity).

ScaleWithRollMultiplier.description: Whether BaseWeight scales with the player's RollMultiplier. true: Weight = BaseWeight x M_roll. false: fixed amount.

TileTypeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile types (BoardTileType names or CustomTypeID) that fire on landing. Case-insensitive. Empty/null = any tile (not recommended).

TileIndexFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile indices. Empty/null = any index. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter.

ChanceOutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding on Chance tiles. Whitelist of ChanceOutcome.OutcomeID values. Case-insensitive. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter/TileIndexFilter. Empty/null = not applied.

OutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardAttack / BoardRaid / BoardBuild. Whitelist of outcomes. Empty/null = any. BoardAttack: ["HIT"]/["BLOCKED"]; BoardRaid: ["FINISHED_SMALL"]/["FINISHED_MEDIUM"]/["FINISHED_BIG"]; BoardBuild: ["BUILD"]/["STAGE_COMPLETE"].

Params.description: Context parameters for filtering/identifying the source. CustomAction: {"ActionName":"watch_ad"}. QuestComplete: {"QuestID":"win_5_raids"} and/or {"CycleID":"daily"}. StorePurchase: {"OfferID":"starter_pack"}. MarketplaceSell/MarketplaceBuy: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType. An unset or empty parameter means "any". Keys not listed here are not checked by the matcher.

Limits.description: Anti-farm limits of the source — unified LimitSpec (per-day weight cap DailyWeightCap, per-day trigger cap DailyCap, CooldownSeconds). null = no limits (e.g. leaderboards intentionally apply none).

x-enum-descriptions: Landing on an EventToken tile on the board.
Passing start (GO) on the board.
Successful board attack.
Successful board raid.
Building or repairing a structure on the board.
Completing a board stage.

Completing a board Special mode — either via Instant choice or via Claim after the Timed window. Post-resolution source (mirrors BoardAttack/BoardRaid): fires at the final Special reward grant, separately from BoardTileLanding (which fires on the actual tile landing during Roll).
Completing a quest.
Store purchase.
Daily login.
Referral invite.
Token grant as a reward for a milestone or streak in another event. Server-only source — the client cannot invoke it directly.
Arbitrary action — the developer calls the server API with ActionName in Params.
Marketplace (v2) sale — deal settlement on the seller side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
Marketplace (v2) purchase — deal settlement on the buyer side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
In-game currency spend — any scenario where a resource operation actually consumed currency. Server-only source. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.
Opening a lootbox/chest. Server-only source. The multiplier equals how many boxes were opened in the call. Filter Params: LootboxID.

Real-money store purchase (IAP). Server-only source: fired in PurchaseV2 AFTER the receipt is verified and rewards are granted. The multiplier equals the number of product units granted. Filter Params: ProductID, Store. Deliberately separate from StorePurchase, which covers in-game currency spending.
Crypto deposit credited to the in-game balance. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Crypto withdrawal CONFIRMED on chain. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Spending crypto currency in-game. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.

In-game currency GRANT — mirror of CurrencySpent. The multiplier equals the amount granted, so ScaleWithRollMultiplier picks the meaning: "earn N currency" or "receive currency N times". Filter Params: CurrencyID and Origin ("Gameplay" | "RewardClaim"), the latter separating gameplay earnings from reward payouts — without it a goal like "earn N" would be closed by another quest's reward.
CRYPTO currency GRANT in-game (wallet deposits are NOT included — that is CryptoDeposit). The multiplier equals the amount granted. Filter Params: CurrencyID, Origin.

Leaderboard ScoreSources only: the board accepts the NUMBER the game submits itself (SubmitScore / SubmitScoresBatch). Not an event — it grants nothing and matches nothing, it only allows. Without it the board refuses a score from the game: an empty ScoreSources list means the board is not set up. Caps live in Limits: PerActivationCap = max score of ONE submission, DailyCap / DailyWeightCap = submissions / total score per UTC day, CooldownSeconds, MaxPerWindow + WindowSeconds, TotalCap = submissions for all time. A submission over a cap is refused, not trimmed. BaseWeight is not read. Set caps the game can really reach: the client is not trusted, they are the only limit on a forged score.
The player joined a clan (Clan section): by themselves, by application or by invitation. Params: KindID, ClanID. Use for a tutorial step 'join a clan', quests, event tokens.

The player helped the clan: donated to a request (Params.Kind = Request, weight = units) or helped a timer (Params.Kind = Help, weight = 1). Params: KindID, Kind, RequestKindID, ResourceID. Filter by Params.Kind.
The player claimed a clan gift. Params: KindID, GiftID.
The player upgraded an item (Item upgrade, batch included). Weight = levels gained. Params: ItemID, CatalogID, Level (the new level). Server-side only.
The player took revenge for a clanmate on the board (clan Revenge): an attack or raid on the offender of a taken revenge. Params: KindID, ClanID, Action (Attack / Raid). Server-side only.

LimitSpec.description: Unified anti-farm limits ("how much / how often"). Replaces TriggerLimits (Scheduling), DealNodeLimitsDefinition (DealOffer), StoreOfferRules caps (Store) and ClaimRewardDefinition sliding fields (Reward). 0 on an axis = no limit. Superset of axes with DIFFERENT enforcement semantics: DailyCap/DailyWeightCap = calendar UTC day; MaxPerWindow/WindowSeconds = sliding window. Usually one set is filled per system, the rest = 0. Counters are stored/enforced by each system; this is config thresholds only.

TotalCap.description: Lifetime cap per user. 0 = no limit.

DailyCap.description: Cap on triggers/actions per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

DailyWeightCap.description: Cap on weight (e.g. token amount) per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

PerActivationCap.description: Cap within a single activation/session. 0 = no limit.

MaxPerWindow.description: Sliding window: max triggers within WindowSeconds. 0 = disabled.

WindowSeconds.description: Sliding-window length (seconds). Used only when MaxPerWindow > 0.

RelativeWindow.description: Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see ScheduleMode.Relative). Window start = parent.StartUtc + OffsetSecondsFromParentStart. End = start + DurationSeconds, or (if DurationSeconds <= 0) the parent's end; never extends past the parent's end. Lets one config auto-repeat: sub-entity dates are computed from the current parent instance instead of being written absolutely.

OffsetSecondsFromParentStart.description: Window start offset in SECONDS from the parent instance start. 0 = open immediately with the parent. E.g. "Day N" = (N-1) * 86400.

DurationSeconds.description: Window length in SECONDS. 0 (or less) = the window lasts until the parent's end (typical for "stage opens and stays until the event ends"). >0 = lasts exactly that long (but never longer than the parent).

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after the window ends (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after the window ends for claiming rewards. Default 0.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

TutorialFlowPolicy.description: Flow progression policy: what the player may do with it and what it unlocks.

Skippable.description: Whether the whole flow may be skipped. Default false: onboarding is mandatory by default, and skippability is a deliberate publisher decision.

SkippableFromOrder.description: From which TutorialStepDefinition.Order skipping becomes available. Default 0 (skippable immediately when Skippable = true). Lets you force the first N steps and release the player afterwards.

RestartPolicy.description: Whether the flow can be taken again. Default Never.

ExpireAfterSeconds.description: After how many seconds an unfinished flow is considered Expired and stops blocking/showing. 0 (default) = never expires.

IsBlocking.description: Whether this flow participates in hard module blocking (TutorialBlockingPolicy). Default false. The flag alone closes nothing — the restriction set is defined by the policy in TutorialGlobalSettings.

UnlockFeatures.description: What completing the flow unlocks — arbitrary feature labels for the CLIENT ("shop", "raids"). This is the soft gating level: the server only reports them, it does not enforce them. Server-side enforcement is SegmentGate.Tutorial on the entity itself, or TutorialBlockingPolicy.

x-enum-descriptions: Not allowed. Default.
Only on an explicit player request (a "replay tutorial" button in the settings).
Again whenever the availability conditions hold. Careful: for a rewarded flow this would mean re-granting, so such a flow's reward is granted on the first pass only.

TutorialStepDefinition.description: Definition of a single tutorial step.

StepID.description: Step ID (e.g. "first_roll"). Mongo-safe. Matches the dictionary key.

Order.description: Step order within the flow (lower = earlier). Default 0. Steps sharing an order are sorted by StepID — otherwise the tutorial sequence would depend on BSON key order, which is not guaranteed.

Identity.description: Display part of the step: copy, UI anchor, assets.

Effects.description: What happens when the step completes.

Script.description: Predetermined outcome in another module while this step is active (scripted board). null = nothing is forced and the mechanics run honestly.

TutorialStepIdentity.description: Display part of a step. This is what makes A/B over wording possible: copy and anchors live in the config, so two tutorial variants differ without rebuilding the game.

TitleKey.description: Localization key for the title. When set, it wins over Title.

BodyKey.description: Localization key for the body. When set, it wins over Body.

AnchorID.description: Logical name of the UI element the hint attaches to ("roll_button", "shop_tab"). The engine never interprets it — it is a contract between the config and the game.

HighlightTarget.description: What to highlight when it is not the anchor itself (e.g. the hint sits by a button but the whole panel must be lit). Empty = AnchorID is highlighted.

AssetPaths.description: Step assets (image, video, arrow). Key = logical slot name.

UiHint.description: Arbitrary rendering hints for the client: popup position, mask shape, whether tapping outside is allowed. The engine never interprets them.

Mode.description: How the step completes. Selects which fields are read: SystemEvent -> Triggers; other modes need no triggers. Default ClientAck.

Triggers.description: Game events that complete the step. Read only when Mode = SystemEvent. The same TriggerSource and the same TriggerMatcher used by quest objectives — so a step can wait for ANY platform event (board roll, purchase, chest open, currency spend) without a single edit in the source module. An empty list = the step never completes on its own.

TargetValue.description: How many fires are required. Default 1. "Roll the dice three times" is TargetValue = 3.

RequireAllTriggers.description: Whether ALL triggers in the list are required (each at least once) or any one suffices. Default false = any one (the list is OR-ed, as in quests). Read only when Mode = Composite.

x-enum-descriptions: The client calls Tutorial/CompleteStep itself ("the player tapped Next"). Default.
An internal engine game event (Completion.Triggers), with no separate HTTP call: the step is closed by the very action it was asking for.
Completes immediately on being shown (ReportStepShown) — an informational aside.
Several triggers with an explicit all/any rule (Completion.RequireAllTriggers).

TutorialStepEffects.description: Side effects of completing a step.

Grant.description: Grant for completing the step. Grant only (ResourceGrant). Applied through ResourceService inside the same atomic operation as the step progress write.

UnlockFeatures.description: Feature labels unlocked by this step (soft gating level, see TutorialFlowPolicy.UnlockFeatures).

ResourceGrant.description: Grant direction container for ResourceOperation. Two independent premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumBonuses applies a percentage uplift to Standard (single best tier wins, no stack), and PremiumTiers provides structurally different rewards governed by cfg.Reward.TierRewards (Additive or Replace mode; in Replace the bonused Standard is wiped). Both mechanisms can be used together or independently.

Standard.description: Base — what to grant to all players including F2P.

PremiumBonuses.description: Percentage uplift on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 + Bonus)). Wiped under Mode=Replace if any PremiumTier matches.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different rewards for premium players (different ItemID/Target/...). Governed by global cfg.Reward.TierRewards.RewardMode (Additive/Replace) and RewardStackLowerTiers.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Credits, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account (players see it as "Aspis" — write Aspis in player-facing text). Requires only Amount — the price in whole Credits. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCreditsPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted by every sale of the game author: Store, Lootbox, Collection packs, Craft, DealOffer, TimedBoost, Premium, Item and Character upgrades, skins, CoopEvent spins, GameLoop special mode entry, Workshop publish fee, InApp AI (charged only when the generation is ready). NOT accepted in player-to-player prices or refundable fees (Marketplace listing fee, PvP Match creation) - those refuse with CREDITS_NOT_ALLOWED_HERE; batch calls refuse too. Allowed only in Consume: Credits are never a reward anywhere.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

Type.description: System the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

PremiumTierBonus.description: Percentage bonus on ResourceGrant.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 + Bonus) with Math.Ceiling rounding. Applies only to Standard; in Replace mode the bonused Standard is wiped when any PremiumTier matches. Best matching tier wins, bonuses do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierDiscount.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Bonus.description: Bonus as a SHARE: 0.1 = +10%, 1.0 = double (x2). Empty or 0 = no bonus. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).

TutorialScriptedOutcome.description: Predetermined outcome in another module, active while the tutorial step is current. Exists for exactly one reason: to show the player the mechanic rather than the randomness — "the first roll lands on Raid, the second on the shop" is otherwise impossible, since the board is honestly random and the tutorial would narrate a raid while showing an empty tile. THIS IS A SERVER-SIDE CHEAT PATH, locked behind three simultaneous conditions: the flow must be InProgress, this step must be the current one, and MaxUses must not be exhausted. Without all three, a client able to keep the tutorial open would choose its own tiles forever.

Module.description: Which module is forced. Currently only GameLoop (the board) is supported.

Board.description: Board script. Read when Module = GameLoop.

MaxUses.description: How many times the script fires within the step. Default 1: the mechanic is shown, then the game is honest again. 0 = unlimited (only for a step that closes itself by TargetValue).

x-enum-descriptions: The GameLoop board: dice value, Chance outcome, RandomAction resolution.

TutorialBoardScript.description: Predetermined board roll. All three fields are independent: you may force only the tile and leave the Chance outcome honest.

TileType.description: Tile type to land on — a BoardTileType name or a CustomTypeID, case-insensitive (the same convention as TriggerSource.TileTypeFilter). The NEAREST matching tile forward along the board is used. Empty = type not forced.

TileIndex.description: Exact tile index. When set, it wins over TileType: an index is unambiguous while a type may occur many times on the board. null = not forced.

ChanceOutcomeID.description: Chance tile outcome (ChanceOutcome.OutcomeID). Forcing it separately is necessary: without it, a step saying "a chance tile is coming and you will get coins" would show a random outcome from the table, i.e. contradict its own copy. Empty = honest outcome.

RandomActionType.description: What a RandomAction tile resolves to — Raid or Attack. Same reason as ChanceOutcomeID: otherwise the random-action tile shows a different mechanic than the step describes. null = honest roll.

x-enum-descriptions: Raid.
Attack.

Skippable.description: Whether this particular step may be skipped without abandoning the flow. Default false. Distinct from TutorialFlowPolicy.Skippable, which skips the whole scenario; this skips one step (e.g. an optional aside).

TimeoutSeconds.description: After how many seconds from being shown the step auto-completes. 0 (default) = no time-based completion. Needed for informational asides that await no player action.

Grant.description: Completion grant. Grant only — ResourceGrant, not ResourceOperation: nobody pays for a tutorial. Premium resolution runs in ResourceService against global cfg.Premium settings.

AutoClaim.description: Whether to grant automatically on finishing the last step. Default false — the reward is taken by an explicit ClaimFlowReward: the client needs a moment at which to show the "here is what you got" screen.

TutorialPresetBindings.description: Preset wiring container — one PresetBinding per block. Bindings are independent: take the schedule from one preset, the reward from another, and write the steps inline.

Availability.description: Availability preset (field-level overlay).

Steps.description: Steps preset: merge by StepID, field-level overlay inside a matched step, PresetBinding.Remove drops inherited steps.

PresetBinding.description: Wiring for one preset block of an entity: a reference into the module's preset registry + optional keys to drop. Reusable Core container, one per preset-able block, held inside the entity's Presets container. Replaces the former scattered flat *PresetID / *Remove fields. Combination is data-driven, no mode (PresetResolver): no PresetID -> inline only; preset + empty inline -> preset; preset + inline -> merge (preset base + inline overrides/adds by key), Remove drops keys. For a single object (Character Equipment) there is nothing to key-merge, so inline wins when both are present.

PresetID.description: Preset key in the module registry (e.g. LeaderboardDefinitions.Presets.Milestones[PresetID]). Empty/null = preset unused (inline layer only).

Remove.description: Keys removed from the merged result. Dictionary key for dictionaries; element key for keyed lists (Rank / SlotID / RuleID). null = remove nothing. Ignored when no preset is set.

IsEnabled.description: Master switch. false = the module serves no flows and advances no progress; already started flows stay untouched in the player document.

MaxActiveFlows.description: How many flows the player may keep InProgress at once. 0 = no limit. Exceeding it fails StartFlow rather than silently closing an older flow — auto-closing would discard progress the player never agreed to lose.

Blocking.description: Policy for hard-blocking other modules while the tutorial is in progress. null/empty = nothing is blocked (the default for a title that never configured blocking).

TutorialBlockingPolicy.description: Hard module blocking while a tutorial is in progress. Modelled on BanLevelDefinition's BlockedModules/BlockedActions: names are FunctionName values and module action-enum values, matched case-insensitively; an unknown name simply does not match and never breaks the request. This is the cheapest of the three gating levels — one check in ClientRun instead of a gate on every entity. Costs nothing for titles that leave it empty.

BlockingFlowIDs.description: Which flows block. Empty = every flow with Policy.IsBlocking = true blocks. List them explicitly when only some mandatory flows should block.

BlockedModules.description: Modules closed entirely until the blocking flow completes (FunctionName values: "Store", "Marketplace", ...).

BlockedActions.description: Individually closed actions: module -> action list. Lets you close purchasing while leaving the shop readable — otherwise the client cannot draw the very screen the tutorial is showing.

BlockBeforeStart.description: Whether blocking applies BEFORE the player starts the flow. true (default) — yes: the point of mandatory onboarding is that you cannot walk past it. false — blocking starts only after StartFlow, and a player who never began is unrestricted.

SkipLiftsBlock.description: Whether a Skipped flow lifts the block. true (default) — yes: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the full game. false — skipping closes the tutorial but the restrictions remain ("you may skip, but the shop still opens only after completing").

TutorialPresetRegistry.description: Registry of reusable tutorial config blocks. Each field is a dictionary keyed by PresetID and mirrors the same-named TutorialFlowDefinition block. Direct analogue of QuestPresetRegistry.

Availability.description: Reusable availability blocks: schedule, audience gate, prerequisites, auto-start.

Policy.description: Reusable policy blocks: skipping, restart, expiry, blocking flag.

Steps.description: Reusable step sets (inner dictionary key = StepID). The preset says HOW a step closes (Completion, Script); a flow normally overrides only the copy and the order.

tools.name: get_localization
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Localization' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Localization SETTINGS — which locales the title offers, which one is the default (and therefore the fallback), what to render for a missing key, and the store limits. The translation TABLES are deliberately NOT here: they live in the separate TitleLocalization collection (one document per title+locale) and are delivered one file per locale, because text changes far more often than balance and must not invalidate the whole title config. Client resolution is t(x) = own table -> fallback table -> x itself, which is why a title whose DisplayName fields hold literal names keeps working unchanged: a literal is simply a key with no translation. Add or edit translations through the Localization endpoints, not through this section.

tools.name: save_localization
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Localization' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Localization SETTINGS — which locales the title offers, which one is the default (and therefore the fallback), what to render for a missing key, and the store limits. The translation TABLES are deliberately NOT here: they live in the separate TitleLocalization collection (one document per title+locale) and are delivered one file per locale, because text changes far more often than balance and must not invalidate the whole title config. Client resolution is t(x) = own table -> fallback table -> x itself, which is why a title whose DisplayName fields hold literal names keeps working unchanged: a literal is simply a key with no translation. Add or edit translations through the Localization endpoints, not through this section.

value.title: LocalizationDefinitions
value.description: Localization settings of the title. The translation TABLES are not stored here: they live in the separate TitleLocalization collection (one document per title+locale) and are delivered one file per locale. This section only declares which locales exist, which one is the fallback, and the store limits.

IsEnabled.description: Master switch. When false the server serves neither the manifest nor any table, and the client renders the config strings as-is.

DefaultLocale.description: Default locale, which is also the FALLBACK: its table is what the client additionally downloads when its own locale is not fully translated. Stored canonically (lower-case, '-' separator). Empty means "en".

Locales.description: Locales offered to the player, keyed by canonical locale code ("en", "pt-br"). The same code becomes part of the table document _id and of the CDN object key.

MissingKeyMode.description: What the client renders when a key is missing from both its own and the fallback table.

MaxEntriesPerLocale.description: Maximum number of entries in a SINGLE locale table. Guards the document against unbounded growth (BSON's 16 MB ceiling) and the importer against an accidentally uploaded foreign file. Recommended: 20000.

MaxValueLengthBytes.description: Length limit of a single translation in bytes (UTF-8). Long-form text (rules, licences) belongs in TitleCustomData, not here. Recommended: 4096.

LocalizationLocaleDefinition.description: A single entry of the available-languages list. It exists so the game can draw the language picker BEFORE any table has been downloaded.

Locale.description: Canonical locale code — a readability mirror of the dictionary key. It does not affect resolution: the dictionary key is the identifier, as in every other config section.

DisplayName.description: Language name written IN THAT LANGUAGE ("Русский", "Deutsch") — an endonym, not a translation: the picker is read by someone who may not know the current language. Localizing it through the table itself would be circular, so it lives in the config.

IsEnabled.description: When false the language is hidden from the picker and not served, but its table is kept. This is how a language is switched off while it is being translated, without discarding the translator's work.

Order.description: Order in the picker. Ties are broken by locale code.

x-enum-descriptions: Render the key itself. This is the default, and it is what keeps titles whose config holds literal names (rather than keys) working unchanged.
Render the key wrapped in markers (⟦quest.daily.title⟧) — proofreading mode: gaps are visible on screen instead of in a report.
Render an empty string. Appropriate when blank space is preferable to a technical string on top of finished artwork.

tools.name: get_referral
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Referral' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Referral / invite system configuration — invite codes, attribution rules, milestones (e.g. invite N friends → reward), per-side rewards (inviter + invitee). Reward bundles reference Reward.

tools.name: save_referral
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Referral' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Referral / invite system configuration — invite codes, attribution rules, milestones (e.g. invite N friends → reward), per-side rewards (inviter + invitee). Reward bundles reference Reward.

value.title: ReferralDefinitions
value.description: Title's referral system configuration. Stored in TitlePublicConfigurationModel.ReferralDefinitions.

IsEnabled.description: Whether the referral system is enabled for this title. Disabled by default: the subsystem grants resources (activation reward, invite milestones, percent kickback to the referrer), so it must be switched on deliberately. While false, every mutating action of the module is refused; reads stay available.

ActivationReward.description: One-time reward to the current user for the first activation of another user's referral code.

InviteRewards.description: Staged rewards to the referrer for hitting follower thresholds — unified MilestoneDefinition (Core/Milestone). Key = MilestoneID. RequiredProgress is checked against UserReferralState.FollowersCount; claimed manually via ClaimInviteReward (claimed state lives in UserReferralState.InviteRewardStates, not EventToken).

SpendRewards.description: Percent-based referral kickback config per feature. Determines what percent of a follower's spend goes to the referrer. The calling API must invoke ReferralV2.ProcessSpendRewardAsync after a successful deduction.

Qualification.description: Conditions an invited player must meet before the invite counts (anti-farming, and invite leaderboards that count only real players). Until met, everything waits: the referrer's +1 (invite milestones), ReferralInvite event tokens and leaderboard points, the spend kickback and the invitee's activation reward. No deadline. Null or disabled = the invite counts immediately on binding.

Threshold is checked against accumulated progress (RequiredProgress): EventToken systems use EventTokenBalanceData.TotalEarned; CommunityChest uses shared group progress. Reward overlays BonusRewards (bonus-window) and SeasonTierRewards (season-tier) are platform-wide optional fields applied via MilestoneRewardResolver; leave null if unused.

MilestoneID.description: Unique milestone ID within its owning entity (Mongo-safe, claim idempotency key).

DisplayName.description: Display name for UI/CMS. null = unset.

AssetPaths.description: Milestone images (icon, badge). null = unset.

RequiredProgress.description: Threshold over ACCUMULATED progress to unlock. EventToken systems: EventTokenBalanceData.TotalEarned (not current balance). CommunityChest: shared group progress.

Rewards.description: Base rewards. Always granted on a successful claim.

BonusRewards.description: Bonus-window overlay: extra rewards on top of Rewards when the bonus phase is active at claim time (MilestoneRewardContext.BonusActive). Applied via MilestoneRewardResolver. null = no bonus part.

SeasonTierRewards.description: Season-tier overlay: reward scaling by the player's season tier. Applied via MilestoneRewardResolver (SeasonTierRewardResolver.Resolve) only when MilestoneRewardContext.SeasonChainID is set. null = disabled.

SortOrder.description: Sort order in the UI (lower = higher/earlier).

IsFeatured.description: Featured milestone: special UI styling. With MilestoneClaimMode.FeaturedAfterEnd these can only be claimed after the instance ends.

SeasonTierRewardSet.description: Generic container of season-tier reward scaling. Used by any platform system (leaderboards, lootboxes, shop, daily) that wants to scale a ResourceGrant by the player's current tier in a season chain. Empty/null lists = neutral.

Bundles.description: Structurally different rewards for specific tiers. On match, replaces the base ResourceGrant entirely (Replace).

Multipliers.description: Multipliers applied to Amount of the base ResourceGrant. Used ONLY if no Bundles entry matched.

SeasonTierRewardBundle.description: Structurally different rewards for a season-chain tier. Analogous to PremiumTierBundle but the trigger is the player's season tier. Selection picks the single best match (MinSeasonTier <= playerTier); not stacked.

SeasonChainID.description: SeasonChainID this tier is linked to. Selection matches only tiers with the same SeasonChainID.

MinSeasonTier.description: Minimum player season tier required for this bundle to apply. Matches SeasonTierDefinition.Tier / UserSeasonState.CurrentTier.

Rewards.description: Rewards for this tier. Passed unmodified into ResourceService via a regular ResourceOperation.Grant.

SeasonTierRewardMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to Amount of the base ResourceGrant for a season-chain tier. Applied to every ResourceEntry.Amount and EventTokenOperation.Amount in Standard and in PremiumTiers.Resources.

SeasonChainID.description: SeasonChainID this tier is linked to.

MinSeasonTier.description: Minimum player season tier required for this multiplier to apply.

Multiplier.description: Multiplier. 1.0 = neutral (resolver returns the base reward without copying). Rounding: (long)Math.Round(Amount * Multiplier). Entries with final Amount <= 0 are dropped.

SpendRewardDefinition.description: A single referral kickback rule: for which follower action, from which currency, and what percent the referrer receives. Rules are independent — they can be switched on and off individually, several per feature, each with its own limits.

FeatureKey.description: Feature identifier — which follower action is paid for. Values are listed in ReferralV2.SpendFeatureKeys. An unknown key simply never matches, so the rule stays silent.

IsEnabled.description: Whether this rule is enabled. A disabled rule is never evaluated and never pays.

Basis.description: What to calculate the percent from: the follower's spend or their gain. Defaults to spend.

Rate.description: Share the referrer receives: 0.05 = 5%. Empty or 0 = no kickback. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent. Calculated from the ACTUALLY applied operation, so premium discounts and tier prices are already accounted for.

SourceCurrencyID.description: ID of the follower's currency the percent is calculated from. EMPTY = any virtual currency: the rule fires for each currency of the operation separately.

TargetCurrencyID.description: ID of the currency the referrer receives. EMPTY = the same currency as the source (handy together with an empty SourceCurrencyID).
