Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

ExperimentVariant.description: Experiment variant (an A/B/C arm, incl. control).

VariantID.description: Variant ID (mongo-safe): e.g. "control", "A", "B". Unique within the experiment.

Weight.description: Relative allocation weight. 0 = not allocated. E.g. 50/50 -> [50,50]; 90/10 -> [90,10].

IsControl.description: Control (baseline) variant. Flagged for analytics and as the default behavior.

Params.description: Variant params — a simple way to carry inline overrides (e.g. {"discount":"20"}) without separate gated entities per variant.

ExperimentGoal.description: Experiment goal — a single report metric.

Kind.description: Metric kind: EventConversion | EventCountPerUser | EventValuePerUser | RetentionD1 | RetentionD7 | PayerConversion | Arpu.

EventName.description: Custom event name — for the Event* kinds.

IsPrimary.description: Primary goal: the experiment's overall verdict is based on it. One per experiment.

tools.name: get_advertising
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Advertising' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Advertising — logical ad Placements (rewarded video, interstitial, banner, app-open), the mediation Providers that serve them (AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay, ...) with per-platform app IDs and ad unit IDs, per-format settings, frequency capping, premium ad-removal perks, GDPR/ATT consent policy, rewarded-video server-side verification (SSV) and the daily revenue import from the provider's Reporting API. Shared secrets (SSV keys, report keys) are NOT stored here — only the NAME of the TitleSecrets entry that holds them.

tools.name: save_advertising
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Advertising' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Advertising — logical ad Placements (rewarded video, interstitial, banner, app-open), the mediation Providers that serve them (AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay, ...) with per-platform app IDs and ad unit IDs, per-format settings, frequency capping, premium ad-removal perks, GDPR/ATT consent policy, rewarded-video server-side verification (SSV) and the daily revenue import from the provider's Reporting API. Shared secrets (SSV keys, report keys) are NOT stored here — only the NAME of the TitleSecrets entry that holds them.

value.title: AdvertisingDefinitions
value.description: Title-level advertising configuration: placements, SDK providers, per-format settings, frequency capping, premium ad reductions, consent and rewarded-video server-side verification.

Enabled.description: Master switch for the whole advertising system. When false the server rejects every ad permit/impression request regardless of per-placement settings.

Placements.description: Catalog of logical ad placements. Key is AdPlacementDefinition.PlacementID.

Providers.description: Ad SDK provider configuration. Key is AdProviderDefinition.ProviderID (e.g. "applovin").

RewardedVideo.description: Global rewarded-video settings shared by all rewarded placements.

FrequencyCapping.description: Global frequency caps applied on top of per-placement and per-format limits.

PremiumAdReductions.description: Premium perks that disable ad formats for subscribers. Single best matching tier wins, no stacking (standard PremiumTierModifier selection).

Verification.description: Server-side verification (SSV) settings for rewarded video.

MaxClientRevenueMicrosPerImpression.description: Cap on client-reported revenue per single impression, in micro-USD (1 USD = 1000000). Anything above is clamped and flagged. Client-side revenue can be forged, and one player could otherwise poison the report the publisher buys traffic on. Default 5000000 ($5) is generous for a real impression. 0 disables clamping (test stands only).

Reporting.description: LEGACY single-provider report import, kept for back-compat (it predates multi-provider support and describes AppLovin only). Per-provider settings live in AdProviderDefinition.Reporting and win; this block is consulted only when a provider has none AND its Kind is AppLovinMax. Resolution lives in AdReportingDefaults.EffectiveFor.

CreditSinks.description: Catalog of places where the player may SPEND RewardedVideoCredit. Key is AdCreditSinkDefinition.SinkID. Normally the credit is spent by the very operation it pays for and needs no sink; this catalog is for spends whose mechanic is entirely client-side and therefore has no server operation of its own (ability reroll inside a run, continue-after-death, skipping an offline timer). Cost and limits come from config, not from the client: the client only names the sink.

AdPlacementDefinition.description: One logical ad placement. Concrete SDK ad units are bound through AdProviderDefinition.Units keyed by the same PlacementID.

PlacementID.description: Unique placement identifier. Used as the key in Advertising.Placements and in the player's Advertising.Placements. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

Type.description: Ad format type of this placement.

Enabled.description: Per-placement switch.

CooldownSeconds.description: Minimum interval between impressions of this placement, in seconds. Checked against the player's LastShownAt. 0 = no cooldown.

DailyImpressionCap.description: Maximum impressions of this placement per UTC day. 0 = unlimited.

CreditsRewarded.description: Base amount of RewardedVideoCredit granted per verified view on this placement. Meaningful only for RewardedVideo and RewardedInterstitial; ignored otherwise.

AllowedProviderIDs.description: Provider whitelist for this placement. null or empty means every enabled provider is allowed.

x-enum-descriptions: Persistent banner ad.
Full-screen ad that interrupts gameplay.
Rewarded video: watched to completion, grants the player a reward.
Hybrid of interstitial and rewarded: shown like an interstitial but grants a reward when watched to completion.
Ad shown when the app returns from background.
Native ad embedded into the game UI.

AdProviderDefinition.description: Configuration of one ad SDK provider (AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay, AdMob, ...).

ProviderID.description: Unique provider identifier within the title (e.g. "applovin").

Kind.description: Mediation vendor; selects the SSV verification algorithm and the report-import strategy. Absent = AppLovinMax.

Enabled.description: Per-provider switch.

Priority.description: Provider priority in mediation. Higher value = higher priority in the client SDK waterfall.

AndroidAppID.description: Provider app ID for the Android build.

IosAppID.description: Provider app ID for the iOS build.

WebAppID.description: Provider app ID for the Web build.

Units.description: Ad unit IDs per placement. Key is AdPlacementDefinition.PlacementID.

Reporting.description: Report-import settings for this provider. Absent = fall back to the root Advertising.Reporting, and only for AppLovinMax. Resolved by AdReportingDefaults.EffectiveFor.

x-enum-descriptions: AppLovin MAX: the publisher composes the callback URL from macros, signature is sha1(EVENT_ID + Event Key), the response body is ignored.

Unity LevelPlay (formerly ironSource): the provider composes the callback URL with its own fixed parameter names, signature is md5(timestamp+eventId+userId+rewards+privateKey), and the response must carry an acknowledgement body or the callback is retried.

AdUnitConfig.description: One ad unit: platform-specific IDs for a given placement at a given provider.

Type.description: Expected format of this ad unit. Must match the placement's Type; the server validates this when issuing a permit.

AdProviderReportingSettings.description: Report-import settings for ONE provider; overrides the root Advertising.Reporting where present. A separate block is required because vendors need a different number of credentials: AppLovin authenticates with a single Report Key, LevelPlay with a PAIR (Secret Key + Refresh Token) exchanged for a bearer token.

Enabled.description: Whether report import is enabled for this provider.

SecretName.description: Name of the TitleSecrets entry holding the primary reporting credential: AppLovin Report Key, or LevelPlay Secret Key. The value is never exposed.

RefreshTokenSecretName.description: Name of the TitleSecrets entry holding the SECOND credential, for vendors that need a pair. LevelPlay Refresh Token; unused for AppLovin.

RevisionWindowDays.description: How many recent days to re-pull on every import. 0 = inherit the root Advertising.Reporting.RevisionWindowDays.

RewardedVideoSettings.description: Global rewarded-video settings, shared by every rewarded placement.

DefaultCreditsPerView.description: Default credit reward used when the placement's CreditsRewarded is 0.

MaxCreditsBalance.description: Maximum RewardedVideoCredit balance a single player may accumulate. 0 = unlimited.

DailyCreditEarnCap.description: Maximum credits a player may earn per UTC day. 0 = unlimited.

DailyViewCap.description: Maximum rewarded views per UTC day across all placements. 0 = unlimited.

MinSecondsBetweenViews.description: Global minimum interval between rewarded views of different placements. Prevents bypassing per-placement cooldowns by switching placements.

CooldownSeconds.description: Minimum interval between interstitial impressions, in seconds, on top of the per-placement cooldown.

MinSessionTimeBeforeFirstSeconds.description: How many seconds from session start interstitials are suppressed, protecting the first minutes of gameplay.

DailyImpressionCap.description: Maximum interstitial impressions per UTC day. 0 = unlimited.

MaxImpressionsPerSession.description: Maximum interstitial impressions per session. 0 = unlimited.

Enabled.description: Banner switch, applied on top of the master Advertising.Enabled switch.

RefreshIntervalSeconds.description: Banner auto-refresh interval in seconds. Typical range 30-60.

PermitTtlSeconds.description: Banner permit lifetime in seconds; default 6 hours. Separate from the shared TTL because a banner lives for the whole session and keeps reporting against its permit, while a fullscreen ad is done in a minute.

MaxImpressionsPerMinute.description: Maximum banner impressions the server accepts per minute of permit lifetime. A banner physically refreshes no faster than RefreshIntervalSeconds, so anything well above that rate is fabricated by the client. 0 disables the check.

AppOpenSettings.description: App-open ad settings (shown when the app returns from background).

Enabled.description: App-open switch, applied on top of the master Advertising.Enabled switch.

CooldownSeconds.description: Minimum interval between app-open impressions, in seconds.

DailyImpressionCap.description: Maximum app-open impressions per UTC day. 0 = unlimited.

AdFrequencyCappingSettings.description: Global ad frequency caps counted across all formats, applied on top of per-placement and per-format limits.

MaxImpressionsPerHour.description: Maximum ad impressions per hour. 0 = unlimited.

MaxImpressionsPerDay.description: Maximum ad impressions per UTC day. 0 = unlimited.

MaxImpressionsPerSession.description: Maximum ad impressions per game session. 0 = unlimited.

PremiumAdReduction.description: Premium perk that disables ad formats for subscribers. Enforced server-side before a permit is issued. Single best matching tier wins, no stacking.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

DisableInterstitials.description: Disable interstitials for subscribers of this tier.

DisableBanners.description: Disable banners for subscribers of this tier.

DisableAppOpen.description: Disable app-open ads for subscribers of this tier.

RequirePersonalizedAdsConsent.description: Whether explicit consent for personalized ads is required.

RequireTrackingConsent.description: Whether explicit tracking consent is required (ATT prompt on iOS).

CurrentPolicyVersion.description: Current privacy-policy version. Bumping it invalidates previously stored consents and forces a re-prompt.

RegulatedRegions.description: ISO country codes where consent collection is mandatory. Outside this list ads run under legitimate interest.

AdVerificationSettings.description: Server-side verification (SSV) settings for rewarded video. Only shared-secret providers are supported (AppLovin MAX, Unity LevelPlay); the secret lives in TitleSecrets and is referenced by name only.

RequireServerSideVerification.description: Whether SSV confirmation is required before crediting the player. When false the client's own completion report is trusted (test/dev mode).

PendingRequestTtlSeconds.description: Pending request TTL in seconds; after it expires the request can no longer be confirmed. Typical range 60-180.

MaxPendingRequestsPerUser.description: Maximum concurrent pending requests per player. Guards the player document against pending-request flooding.

ClientGrantFallbackSeconds.description: How many seconds to wait for the SSV callback after the client reports completion before granting the reward without it. 0 (default) = never grant without SSV. Only meaningful when RequireServerSideVerification is true; a late callback is idempotent and never double-grants.

SignatureMode.description: AppLovin ONLY. Which provider token to verify. EventToken (default) is sha1(EVENT_ID + key) as documented; EventTokenAll covers every callback parameter but its canonical string must be confirmed against a live callback before enabling. Providers of other Kinds have a single documented scheme and ignore this field.

RejectedCallbackAck.description: What to answer a callback that FAILED signature verification. Only meaningful for vendors that require an acknowledgement body (LevelPlay); AppLovin ignores the body. Default AckAcceptedOnly.

SecretNameByProvider.description: Name of the TitleSecrets entry holding the provider's shared secret (e.g. AppLovin Event Key). Key is ProviderID, value is the secret NAME such as "APPLOVIN_EVENT_KEY". The secret value itself is never stored here and never leaves the server.

x-enum-descriptions: Acknowledge only ACCEPTED callbacks. A rejected one keeps being retried, which surfaces a wrong key in the provider's own dashboard instead of silently dropping rewards. Cost: retry traffic while the key is wrong, and the response differs between a valid and an invalid callback.

Acknowledge EVERYTHING, including rejected callbacks. No retries and no observable difference between a valid and an invalid callback. Cost: the provider's dashboard looks healthy, so a wrong key is only visible in our own AdEventLog (InvalidSignature outcome).

AdReportingSettings.description: Daily import of revenue from the provider's Reporting API. This is the only source that matches the actual payout; it arrives a day late and keeps being revised for a few more days, so the import re-pulls a window of recent days rather than just yesterday.

Enabled.description: Whether report import is enabled for this title.

SecretName.description: Name of the TitleSecrets entry holding the provider's Report Key. The key is PER TITLE, not per publisher: one publisher may hold several mediation accounts. The value is never exposed.

RevisionWindowDays.description: How many recent days to re-pull on every import. The provider keeps revising a closed day for several days, so a one-shot import would freeze an unrevised number forever. Default 4.

AdCreditSinkDefinition.description: One place where RewardedVideoCredit is spent (see AdvertisingDefinitions.CreditSinks). The server guarantees only that the credit is debited exactly once and within the configured limits; it cannot deliver what was paid for, because the mechanic is client-side. Use for conveniences (reroll, continue, speed-up), never as the gate to server-side value — that must be paid for by the operation that grants it.

SinkID.description: Sink identifier — also the key in Advertising.CreditSinks and in the player's counters. Must not contain '.' or '$': it becomes a path inside the Mongo document.

Enabled.description: A disabled sink answers with a denial but stays in the config.

Cost.description: How many credits one unit costs. Anything below 1 is treated as 1: there is no free sink, that would be a mere counter.

MaxUnitsPerRequest.description: How many units one request may spend. A larger request is clamped, not rejected.

DailyLimit.description: How many times per UTC day this sink may be spent. 0 = unlimited.

SessionLimit.description: How many times per game session this sink may be spent. 0 = unlimited.

Gate.description: Who the sink is available to. null/empty = everyone. Unified platform gate — resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

tools.name: get_authentication
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Authentication' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Authentication — which third-party sign-in methods the title offers and the public OAuth client IDs each platform build needs (currently Google: Web / Android / iOS / Desktop client IDs). Contains NO secrets: OAuth client IDs are public by protocol design, and none of the sign-in flows uses a client secret. Device / e-mail / Telegram / SSO logins need no configuration and are absent from this section. The ID-token audience differs per platform (web and Android tokens carry the Web client ID, iOS tokens the iOS client ID), so several IDs are filled at once and the server accepts any of them.

tools.name: save_authentication
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Authentication' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Authentication — which third-party sign-in methods the title offers and the public OAuth client IDs each platform build needs (currently Google: Web / Android / iOS / Desktop client IDs). Contains NO secrets: OAuth client IDs are public by protocol design, and none of the sign-in flows uses a client secret. Device / e-mail / Telegram / SSO logins need no configuration and are absent from this section. The ID-token audience differs per platform (web and Android tokens carry the Web client ID, iOS tokens the iOS client ID), so several IDs are filled at once and the server accepts any of them.

value.title: AuthenticationDefinitions
value.description: Title-level authentication settings: which third-party sign-in methods the title offers and the public OAuth client IDs each platform build needs. Contains NO secrets - OAuth client IDs are public by protocol design. Device / e-mail / Telegram / SSO logins need no configuration and are not listed here.

Google.description: Google sign-in configuration (public OAuth client IDs per platform build).

Apple.description: Sign in with Apple configuration (bundle ID for native iOS, Services ID for the web flow).

Sessions.description: Session policy: token lifetimes, concurrent-device cap, re-authentication window and nonce strictness.

AntiAbuse.description: Abuse thresholds: account creation per IP, password brute-force lockout, e-mail sending caps.

Email.description: Who transactional e-mails come from. The SMTP password is NOT here - it lives in the private config.

NativeSso.description: Signing in through idosgames.com from NATIVE builds (Android, iOS, desktop). The web and iframe flows need no configuration and are not affected by this block.

GoogleAuthDefinition.description: Google sign-in. The ID-token audience differs per platform, which is Google behaviour and not a choice: Web/GIS and Android/Credential-Manager tokens carry aud = WebClientID, iOS tokens carry aud = IosClientID, loopback/PKCE desktop tokens carry aud = DesktopClientID. The server accepts a token whose aud matches ANY of the filled IDs.

Enabled.description: Master switch. When false the server rejects LoginWithGoogle / LinkGoogle and the client hides the button.

WebClientID.description: Web OAuth client ID. Used by the web build (GIS), by Android (as Credential Manager serverClientId) and optionally by iOS (as serverClientID). Most titles need only this one.

AndroidClientID.description: Android OAuth client ID. NEVER an ID-token audience (Android tokens carry aud = WebClientID). Kept so the dashboard and the build check can tell the publisher whether their package name + SHA-1 is registered: without that registration Android sign-in fails on the device and leaves no trace on the server.

IosClientID.description: iOS OAuth client ID. Also the source of the reversed-client-ID URL scheme written into Info.plist at build time.

DesktopClientID.description: Desktop OAuth client ID ("Desktop app" client type) used by the Unity Editor and desktop builds via the system browser + PKCE. Empty = no Editor sign-in.

AdditionalAudiences.description: Extra accepted audiences, for migrating between OAuth clients while builds carrying the old client ID are still in players hands.

DisablePlatformFallback.description: Disable the platform-wide fallback client (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID env var). Default false on purpose: the default must mean the behaviour that existed before this section, otherwise adding it would silently break Google sign-in for every existing title.

AppleAuthDefinition.description: Sign in with Apple. No secrets: verifying the identity token needs only Apple's public keys and the audience. The .p8 private key belongs to the authorization-code flow, which is not used here. Unlike Google there is no platform-wide fallback: the audience is the app's bundle ID, which is unique per game.

Enabled.description: Master switch. When false the server rejects Apple login/link and the client hides the button.

BundleID.description: iOS app bundle ID. This is what the native build's token carries in aud.

ServiceID.description: Services ID — Apple's separate identifier for the WEB flow (with its own return URLs). Web tokens carry it in aud instead of the bundle ID. Empty = no Apple sign-in on the web.

AdditionalAudiences.description: Extra accepted audiences: a second app of the same team, a build with a different bundle ID, or a migration between identifiers.

AuthSessionsDefinition.description: Session policy of the title: access/refresh lifetimes, concurrent session cap, re-auth window, nonce strictness. Zero means "keep the previous behaviour".

AccessTtlHours.description: Access ticket lifetime in hours. 0 = the previous hardcoded 24h.

RefreshTtlDays.description: Refresh token lifetime in days. 0 = platform default.

MaxConcurrentSessions.description: Max concurrent devices per player. 0 = platform default, which is 1; values above the platform ceiling of 10 are clamped, not refused. When exceeded the OLDEST session is revoked rather than refusing the new login.

ReauthWindowMinutes.description: How recent the login must be for sensitive operations (unlink, revoke-all), in minutes. 0 = platform default.

RequireNonce.description: Require a nonce in Google/Apple tokens. Default false for compatibility: builds already in players' hands do not send one. A nonce that IS sent is always verified regardless of this flag.

AuthAntiAbuseDefinition.description: Anti-abuse thresholds for authentication. Zero means the platform default, NOT "unlimited".

AccountsPerIpPerDay.description: How many accounts a single IP may create per day. 0 = platform default.

PasswordAttemptsBeforeLock.description: Failed password attempts before a temporary lock. 0 = platform default.

PasswordLockMinutes.description: How long the temporary password lock lasts, in minutes. 0 = platform default.

EmailsPerIpPerHour.description: Password-reset e-mails a single IP may trigger per hour. 0 = platform default.

LinkAttemptsPerHour.description: Identity link attempts per player per hour. 0 = platform default.

RefreshPerHour.description: Session refreshes per hour. 0 = platform default.

VerificationEmailsPerIpPerHour.description: Registration confirmation e-mails a single IP may trigger per hour. Separate from EmailsPerIpPerHour on purpose: registrations must not eat the password-reset quota. 0 = platform default.

NativeSsoPollsPerHour.description: Native-SSO request polls per hour. This is the only action the client repeats by design, so the per-second flood limit does not describe it. 0 = platform default.

AuthEmailDefinition.description: Sender of transactional e-mails. Public part only: no credentials. Empty = platform sender, exactly as before.

UseTitleSmtp.description: Send through the title's own SMTP. False = platform sender (settings are kept but unused).

SenderEmail.description: From address. Empty = the one configured in the private SMTP settings.

SenderName.description: Display name the player sees in the From field.

ReplyTo.description: Reply-To address. Worth setting even for a no-reply sender: players do reply, and without it the reply is lost.

TemplateKeyPrefix.description: Localization key prefix for e-mail subjects and bodies. Empty = platform keys.

PasswordSecretName.description: Name of the TitleSecrets entry holding the SMTP password. Takes precedence over the plaintext password in the private config.

VerificationCodeTtlMinutes.description: Lifetime of the registration confirmation code, in minutes. 0 = platform default.

VerificationMaxAttempts.description: Wrong-code attempts before the code is burnt and a new one must be requested. 0 = platform default.

VerificationResendCooldownSeconds.description: Cooldown between resends of the confirmation code to the SAME address, in seconds. 0 = platform default.

AuthNativeSsoDefinition.description: How the sign-in result gets from the browser back into a NATIVE build. Poll needs no publisher setup and works everywhere; DeepLink returns instantly but requires a URL scheme in both the config and the build. Contains no secrets.

ReturnMode.description: Return mechanism: Poll (default, zero setup, works on every platform) or DeepLink (instant, requires a URL scheme registered in the config AND in the build).

UrlScheme.description: App URL scheme without the '://' part, e.g. "mygame". Only used in DeepLink mode. Taken from the config and never from the request - a client-supplied return address would be an open redirect.

RequestTtlSeconds.description: How long a Poll-mode sign-in request stays valid, in seconds. This is the window in which the person is expected to finish signing in and come back. 0 = platform default.

PollIntervalSeconds.description: How often the game should poll for the result, in seconds. A hint for the client so it does not run into the poll quota by accident - the actual limit is NativeSsoPollsPerHour. 0 = platform default.

tools.name: get_feature_tracking
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'FeatureTracking' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Feature tracking — which CONCRETE actions are recorded as their own line in the player's FeatureUsage, on top of the default per-module tracking. Entries look like "Character:EquipItems" (module name from the route + the module's action name). Purely an analytics setting: it makes those actions selectable as steps in custom funnels (Analytics → Funnels). Tracking starts when an action is added — there is no data for the past, because the action was not recorded then. Capped at 40 entries: every tracked id becomes a key in the player document, which is read on every request.

tools.name: save_feature_tracking
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'FeatureTracking' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Feature tracking — which CONCRETE actions are recorded as their own line in the player's FeatureUsage, on top of the default per-module tracking. Entries look like "Character:EquipItems" (module name from the route + the module's action name). Purely an analytics setting: it makes those actions selectable as steps in custom funnels (Analytics → Funnels). Tracking starts when an action is added — there is no data for the past, because the action was not recorded then. Capped at 40 entries: every tracked id becomes a key in the player document, which is read on every request.

value.title: FeatureTrackingDefinitions

Enabled.description: Master switch. Off — only module-level feature usage is recorded, as before.

Actions.description: Actions to record separately, as "Module:Action" (e.g. "Character:EquipItems"). Names match the route: FunctionName and the module's action enum. Case-insensitive.

value.description: New value for the FeatureTracking field.

tools.name: get_attribution
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Attribution' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Acquisition attribution — how the engine records WHERE a player came from. The signal (utm_source/medium/campaign/term/content, the ad network's click id, the referrer, the invite code) arrives with the login request and is stored as a chain of touch points on the player: the first touch is immutable, the last touch tracks win-backs, and the chain in between feeds multi-touch models. This section only tunes that recording: how many touches to keep, how long after a touch an identical signal is still considered the same click rather than a new one, and optional aliases that normalise messy source/medium values into canonical ones for analytics. Referral invites are recorded through this same mechanism as a channel, so they show up in the acquisition reports alongside paid traffic.

tools.name: save_attribution
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Attribution' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Acquisition attribution — how the engine records WHERE a player came from. The signal (utm_source/medium/campaign/term/content, the ad network's click id, the referrer, the invite code) arrives with the login request and is stored as a chain of touch points on the player: the first touch is immutable, the last touch tracks win-backs, and the chain in between feeds multi-touch models. This section only tunes that recording: how many touches to keep, how long after a touch an identical signal is still considered the same click rather than a new one, and optional aliases that normalise messy source/medium values into canonical ones for analytics. Referral invites are recorded through this same mechanism as a channel, so they show up in the acquisition reports alongside paid traffic.

value.title: AttributionDefinitions

MaxHistoryEntries.description: Max length of the player's touch-point chain (UserAttributionState.History). When exceeded, MIDDLE entries are evicted — the first touch and the last touch are always kept. 0 or negative disables multi-touch entirely (only FirstTouch/LastTouch are stored). Recommended 10..50, default 20.

ReengagementWindowMinutes.description: Deduplication window in minutes. A new signal arriving less than this long after the last touch is treated as a repeat click on the same link and is NOT recorded as a separate touch. 0 disables dedup — every signal becomes a new touch. Recommended 5..60, default 30.

SourceAliases.description: Optional normalisation for utm_source. Key is what the client sent (lower-cased and trimmed), value is the canonical name used in analytics — e.g. "fb" -> "facebook", "g" -> "google". Leave empty to store values exactly as received.

MediumAliases.description: Same as SourceAliases but for utm_medium — e.g. "cpc" -> "paid_search", "social-cpc" -> "paid_social".

DeferredMatchEnabled.description: Whether to match an install against a click registered earlier, when the request itself carried no signal at all. Needed where the marketing tag cannot survive the trip: the player taps an ad in a browser, goes through the app store and comes back inside the game, and the parameter is lost on the way. WARNING: this is a GUESS, not a fact - the click is matched by fingerprint (network, platform, OS version, country), and behind a mobile carrier's shared address there can be hundreds of candidates. Such touches are marked with trust level Inferred and must be shown as a separate line in reports.

DeferredMatchTtlMinutes.description: How many minutes a registered click waits for its install before expiring. A day is the compromise: the store visit and the download take hours, but the wider the window, the more candidates share one fingerprint. 0 or less means the default. WARNING: SHORTENING this on live traffic temporarily loses some matches - the fingerprint index is read from the newest end, and a shorter TTL makes new claims expire BEFORE older ones, so a still-live older claim drops below the cut-off and is never seen. It heals itself after one old window; raising the value is always safe.

DeferredMatchMaxCandidates.description: How many matching click records still count as a match. This is the only guard against false attribution: behind a carrier's shared NAT one fingerprint covers a whole building, so once the number of candidates passes this limit nothing is matched at all - guessing one out of forty is worse than attributing nobody. 0 or less means the default.

StoreLinks.description: Where to send a person who opened this title's link: one URL per platform, shown on the shareable invite page idosgames.com/go/{titleID}. Sits inside attribution but answers a DIFFERENT question - the rest of this section configures HOW a touch is recorded, this says WHERE to send someone. Each URL is validated BY HOST when saved; an empty one means the platform is not configured and its button is not rendered at all.

value.description: New value for the Attribution field.

GooglePlayUrl.description: Google Play listing URL. Validated BY HOST on save: only play.google.com, market.android.com, play.app.goo.gl or a market:// scheme. Link shorteners are refused - what hides behind them cannot be checked without following them. Empty means the platform is not configured and its button is not rendered, which is honest; a button leading somewhere wrong is not.

AppleAppStoreUrl.description: App Store listing URL. Only apps.apple.com, itunes.apple.com, appstore.com, apple.co or an itms-apps:// scheme. Empty hides the button.

TelegramUrl.description: Telegram mini app or bot URL. Only t.me, telegram.me, telegram.dog or a tg:// scheme. Empty hides the button.

AutoRedirectMobile.description: Send a phone straight to its own store instead of showing the platform picker. OFF by default, and never applied on desktop: the link is often opened on a work computer while the person plays on a phone, so there the choice must stay. WARNING - the page first waits for the click to be registered (with a short cap) and only then leaves: navigating away immediately would kill that request mid-flight and break deferred matching in exactly its main case, an ad tapped on a phone followed by a store install. Inside Telegram no redirect happens either - someone opening the link in a chat wants the mini app, not a store page.

IconUrl.description: Square app icon shown on the invite page idosgames.com/go/{titleID} (19.11.2026). Only an image uploaded through the dashboard: https on cloud.idosgames.com or static.idos.games, anything else is refused on save - a foreign address would let a third party swap the picture or count every visitor. Empty falls back to the title's main image.

HideWebButton.description: Hide the 'play in browser' button on the invite page even though the title has a web build (19.11.2026), for a title that wants installs from the stores only. Stored negatively on purpose: a missing field means the button is shown, exactly as before the field existed.

AppUrlScheme.description: URL scheme of the installed app without '://', e.g. "sigmagame" (20.11.2026). Lets the invite page open an app that is already installed: an 'Already installed? Open' button, and on Android in Chrome the redirect opens the app itself, falling back to Google Play. The opened link carries the click's utm_* and idos_click, which the game SDK reads for exact attribution. The scheme must also be registered in the game build. Lowercase letters, digits, '+', '-', '.', starting with a letter; web and system schemes are refused. Empty means no button.

tools.name: get_chat
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Chat' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Player chat - the catalog of persistent CHANNELS the title offers (world / announcement / group), plus direct-message settings, moderation rules and polling economics. A channel declares who SEES it (SegmentGate + ScheduleSpec) and who may WRITE to it (a second gate plus LimitSpec anti-spam: slow mode, daily cap); an announcement channel is simply one nobody passes the write gate of. A channel may be PARTITIONED by the player's language or country and sharded by capacity - the partition key is computed by the SERVER (language is validated against this title's Localization locales, country comes from IP), so the set of rooms is bounded by config and never by client input. Type=Group is the extension point for clans: membership comes from an external provider named in GroupSource, and no provider exists yet, so such a channel is currently hidden rather than shown empty. Messages themselves are NOT here - they live in the ChatMessages collection and expire by Retention.HistoryHours; only the hot tail is cached in Redis. Muting a player and reviewing reports are admin actions, not config.

tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Chat' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. A channel declares who SEES it (SegmentGate + ScheduleSpec) and who may WRITE to it (a second gate plus LimitSpec anti-spam: slow mode, daily cap); an announcement channel is simply one nobody passes the write gate of. A channel may be PARTITIONED by the player's language or country and sharded by capacity - the partition key is computed by the SERVER (language is validated against this title's Localization locales, country comes from IP), so the set of rooms is bounded by config and never by client input. Type=Group is the extension point for clans: membership comes from an external provider named in GroupSource, and no provider exists yet, so such a channel is currently hidden rather than shown empty. Muting a player and reviewing reports are admin actions, not config.

value.title: ChatDefinitions
value.description: Configuration of the title's player chat: the catalog of persistent channels (world/announcement/group), direct-message settings, moderation rules and polling economics. Channels are addressed by ChannelID; a channel may be partitioned by the player's language or country and sharded by capacity, and the partition key is computed by the SERVER, never sent by the client. Messages themselves are not here - they live in the ChatMessages collection.

IsEnabled.description: Master switch for the chat module. Not set = enabled (a missing section means 'not configured', not 'disabled').

Channels.description: Catalog of the title's persistent channels, key = ChannelID (e.g. "world", "trade", "news", "clan"). Direct 1-on-1 messages are NOT here - they have their own Direct block.

Direct.description: Direct (1-on-1) message settings. Not set = direct messages are unavailable.

Moderation.description: Moderation rules shared by every channel: the word blocklist, the per-player ignore list and player reports.

Polling.description: Polling economics: how often the client may poll and how much a single poll returns. The client MUST take the interval from here - every poll counts against the title's API quota.

Presets.description: Preset registry: shared blocks referenced by channels through their Presets bindings. null = presets unused.

ChatChannelDefinition.description: One persistent chat channel. Type decides who may write and where membership comes from; Partitioning and Capacity decide how the channel is split into the room the player is actually placed into.

ChannelID.description: Channel identifier. May be omitted in config - the resolver fills it in from the dictionary key.

Identity.description: Presentation: what the channel is called and how it looks in the client.

Type.description: Channel type: Global (anyone who passes the gate), Announcement (publisher writes, players only read), Group (membership resolved by an external provider named in GroupSource, e.g. a clan).

GroupSource.description: Membership provider name for a Group channel (e.g. "Clan"). No providers are registered in the engine today: a Group channel answers 'not a member' until the module that owns the roster is built.

Partitioning.description: How the channel is split into rooms. The partition key is computed by the SERVER from the player's locale and IP country - the client never chooses it, otherwise it would forge it.

Capacity.description: Member cap of a single room. 0 / not set = no sharding, one room. Above the cap the next shard of the same partition is opened.

Availability.description: Who SEES the channel: audience gate plus an optional schedule.

Write.description: Who WRITES to the channel and under which limits. A channel whose Write gate nobody passes is readable but silent - that is how a read-only channel is expressed.

Retention.description: How long the channel's messages live: the hot tail depth kept in Redis and the durable history window in MongoDB.

Presets.description: Preset wiring: one binding per preset-able block (Availability / Write / Retention).

DisplayNameKey.description: Localization KEY of the channel name (not a literal). Client resolution is 'own table -> fallback table -> the key itself', so a literal still renders - but a title written with literals cannot be translated.

SortOrder.description: Sort order in the channel list, lower = higher. Not set = 0.

IconPath.description: Path to the channel icon in the client atlas.

JoinedByDefault.description: Whether the channel is open to the player by default. Not set = true (a channel that passed the visibility gate is visible without an explicit join). false = the player must call JoinChannel.

x-enum-descriptions: Title-wide channel: anyone passing the write gate may post.
Publisher announcements: players read only. The publisher posts through the admin path, not through a player action.
Group channel: the roster comes from the external provider named in GroupSource. This is the extension point for clans.
Not split: one room per title (plus capacity shards).
By the player's language (locale from the Localization module).
By the player's country (resolved from IP on the server).

Gate.description: Audience gate (level, country, premium tier, account age, A/B variant). null = everyone sees it.

Schedule.description: Schedule during which the channel exists. null = always.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

ScheduleSpec.description: "How an entity activates" container, embedded into each system's definition. Exactly one sub-field is filled for the chosen Mode (plus ActivationTriggers for Triggered). Resolved via ScheduleResolver.

Mode.description: Activation mode. Determines which sub-field is used.

IsActive.description: Unified global on/off. false = entity paused without deleting config (replaces scattered IsActive/Enabled).

Scheduled.description: Single-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Scheduled.

Chain.description: Chain config. Required and used only when Mode = Chained.

Cyclic.description: Calendar-cycle config. Required and used only when Mode = Cyclic.

ActivationTriggers.description: Sources that cause activation/grant. Required and used only when Mode = Triggered. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

Relative.description: Relative-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Relative.

x-enum-descriptions: Active whenever enabled, no time gate (eternal leaderboard, manual boost).
Single fixed window [StartUtc..EndUtc] (see ScheduledWindow).
Recurring ordered list of phases (see ScheduleChain).
Activated/granted when a source fires (see ScheduleSpec.ActivationTriggers).
Calendar-aligned cycles with reset (see CyclicSchedule).

Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see RelativeWindow). Resolved only when a parent is passed to ScheduleResolver.ResolveActive. Enables staged unlocking of sub-entities inside a recurring event (e.g. "Day N opens (N-1)x24h after the current cycle instance start"), so one config auto-repeats without absolute dates.

ScheduledWindow.description: Single fixed-date window. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of ScheduledEventDefinition / LeaderboardScheduledConfig / ScheduledBoostDefinition.

StartUtc.description: Window start (UTC). The entity is active from this moment. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active (BOTH bounds are required).

EndUtc.description: Window end (UTC). After this, earning stops unless AllowEarningAfterEnd. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active.

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after EndUtc (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after EndUtc for claiming rewards. Default 48.

ScheduleChain.description: Recurring phase chain. Holds ONLY chain timing — the phase list lives on the module (a phase composes ScheduleChainPhase + its payload), so the resolver takes a projected IReadOnlyList<ScheduleChainPhase>. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of EventChainDefinition / LeaderboardChainConfig / BoostChainDefinition / CoopEventChainDefinition / SeasonChainDefinition.

AnchorUtc.description: Anchor date (UTC). The first phase of the first cycle starts here; all subsequent dates are computed from the anchor + phase durations + pauses. null = no anchor → the chain is unconfigured and never resolves.

MaxCycles.description: Maximum number of full cycles. 0 = infinite.

PauseBetweenPhasesSec.description: Pause between phases inside one cycle (seconds). 0 = no pause.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: Pause between full cycles (seconds). 0 = no pause.

CyclicSchedule.description: Calendar-aligned cycles with reset. Unified replacement of LeaderboardScheduleMode.Cyclic + LeaderboardCycleReset.

IntervalSeconds.description: FixedInterval only: window length in SECONDS (e.g. 86400 = 1 day, 21600 = 6 hours, 864000 = 10 days). default = 86400 (1 day). Ignored for calendar resets.

AnchorUtc.description: FixedInterval only: anchor instant (coerced to UTC, used as-is including time-of-day) from which IntervalSeconds windows are counted; the anchor defines alignment. null/unset = 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC. Ignored for calendar resets.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: FixedInterval only: pause (SECONDS) between active windows. 0 = back-to-back. When >0 the cycle 'pulses': active for IntervalSeconds, then a pause of this length (inactive during the pause — CanEarn=false/IsInPause), then the next window. Full period = IntervalSeconds + PauseBetweenCyclesSec. Ignored for calendar resets (they are gapless by definition).

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after cycle end to claim previous-cycle rewards. 0 = current cycle only.

x-enum-descriptions: Every CyclicSchedule.IntervalSeconds seconds from CyclicSchedule.AnchorUtc — a fixed interval, not calendar-aligned (e.g. "every 6 hours" or "every 10 days"). Alignment is defined by the anchor.
No reset — eternal (all-time) instance.

TriggerSource.description: Unified trigger source: which game event grants progress/grant and under which filters. Replaces EventTokenSource (TimedEvent), LeaderboardScoreSource (Leaderboard) and BoostTriggerSource (TimedBoost). SourceType reuses the existing EventTokenSourceType. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

SourceType.description: Source type. Identifies which game event fires.

BaseWeight.description: Base "weight" per trigger: token amount (TimedEvent) or score (Leaderboard). Unifies the former BaseAmount/BaseScore. Unused for TimedBoost triggers (a boost has no quantity).

ScaleWithRollMultiplier.description: Whether BaseWeight scales with the player's RollMultiplier. true: Weight = BaseWeight x M_roll. false: fixed amount.

TileTypeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile types (BoardTileType names or CustomTypeID) that fire on landing. Case-insensitive. Empty/null = any tile (not recommended).

TileIndexFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile indices. Empty/null = any index. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter.

ChanceOutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding on Chance tiles. Whitelist of ChanceOutcome.OutcomeID values. Case-insensitive. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter/TileIndexFilter. Empty/null = not applied.

OutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardAttack / BoardRaid / BoardBuild. Whitelist of outcomes. Empty/null = any. BoardAttack: ["HIT"]/["BLOCKED"]; BoardRaid: ["FINISHED_SMALL"]/["FINISHED_MEDIUM"]/["FINISHED_BIG"]; BoardBuild: ["BUILD"]/["STAGE_COMPLETE"].

Params.description: Context parameters for filtering/identifying the source. CustomAction: {"ActionName":"watch_ad"}. QuestComplete: {"QuestID":"win_5_raids"} and/or {"CycleID":"daily"}. StorePurchase: {"OfferID":"starter_pack"}. MarketplaceSell/MarketplaceBuy: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType. An unset or empty parameter means "any". Keys not listed here are not checked by the matcher.

Limits.description: Anti-farm limits of the source — unified LimitSpec (per-day weight cap DailyWeightCap, per-day trigger cap DailyCap, CooldownSeconds). null = no limits (e.g. leaderboards intentionally apply none).

x-enum-descriptions: Landing on an EventToken tile on the board.
Passing start (GO) on the board.
Successful board attack.
Successful board raid.
Building or repairing a structure on the board.
Completing a board stage.

Completing a board Special mode — either via Instant choice or via Claim after the Timed window. Post-resolution source (mirrors BoardAttack/BoardRaid): fires at the final Special reward grant, separately from BoardTileLanding (which fires on the actual tile landing during Roll).
Completing a quest.
Store purchase.
Daily login.
Referral invite.
Token grant as a reward for a milestone or streak in another event. Server-only source — the client cannot invoke it directly.
Arbitrary action — the developer calls the server API with ActionName in Params.
Marketplace (v2) sale — deal settlement on the seller side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
Marketplace (v2) purchase — deal settlement on the buyer side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
In-game currency spend — any scenario where a resource operation actually consumed currency. Server-only source. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.
Opening a lootbox/chest. Server-only source. The multiplier equals how many boxes were opened in the call. Filter Params: LootboxID.

Real-money store purchase (IAP). Server-only source: fired in PurchaseV2 AFTER the receipt is verified and rewards are granted. The multiplier equals the number of product units granted. Filter Params: ProductID, Store. Deliberately separate from StorePurchase, which covers in-game currency spending.
Crypto deposit credited to the in-game balance. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Crypto withdrawal CONFIRMED on chain. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Spending crypto currency in-game. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.

In-game currency GRANT — mirror of CurrencySpent. The multiplier equals the amount granted, so ScaleWithRollMultiplier picks the meaning: "earn N currency" or "receive currency N times". Filter Params: CurrencyID and Origin ("Gameplay" | "RewardClaim"), the latter separating gameplay earnings from reward payouts — without it a goal like "earn N" would be closed by another quest's reward.
CRYPTO currency GRANT in-game (wallet deposits are NOT included — that is CryptoDeposit). The multiplier equals the amount granted. Filter Params: CurrencyID, Origin.

Leaderboard ScoreSources only: the board accepts the NUMBER the game submits itself (SubmitScore / SubmitScoresBatch). Not an event — it grants nothing and matches nothing, it only allows. Without it the board refuses a score from the game: an empty ScoreSources list means the board is not set up. Caps live in Limits: PerActivationCap = max score of ONE submission, DailyCap / DailyWeightCap = submissions / total score per UTC day, CooldownSeconds, MaxPerWindow + WindowSeconds, TotalCap = submissions for all time. A submission over a cap is refused, not trimmed. BaseWeight is not read. Set caps the game can really reach: the client is not trusted, they are the only limit on a forged score.
The player joined a clan (Clan section): by themselves, by application or by invitation. Params: KindID, ClanID. Use for a tutorial step 'join a clan', quests, event tokens.

The player helped the clan: donated to a request (Params.Kind = Request, weight = units) or helped a timer (Params.Kind = Help, weight = 1). Params: KindID, Kind, RequestKindID, ResourceID. Filter by Params.Kind.
The player claimed a clan gift. Params: KindID, GiftID.
The player upgraded an item (Item upgrade, batch included). Weight = levels gained. Params: ItemID, CatalogID, Level (the new level). Server-side only.
The player took revenge for a clanmate on the board (clan Revenge): an attack or raid on the offender of a taken revenge. Params: KindID, ClanID, Action (Attack / Raid). Server-side only.

LimitSpec.description: Unified anti-farm limits ("how much / how often"). Replaces TriggerLimits (Scheduling), DealNodeLimitsDefinition (DealOffer), StoreOfferRules caps (Store) and ClaimRewardDefinition sliding fields (Reward). 0 on an axis = no limit. Superset of axes with DIFFERENT enforcement semantics: DailyCap/DailyWeightCap = calendar UTC day; MaxPerWindow/WindowSeconds = sliding window. Usually one set is filled per system, the rest = 0. Counters are stored/enforced by each system; this is config thresholds only.

TotalCap.description: Lifetime cap per user. 0 = no limit.

DailyCap.description: Cap on triggers/actions per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

DailyWeightCap.description: Cap on weight (e.g. token amount) per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

PerActivationCap.description: Cap within a single activation/session. 0 = no limit.

MaxPerWindow.description: Sliding window: max triggers within WindowSeconds. 0 = disabled.

WindowSeconds.description: Sliding-window length (seconds). Used only when MaxPerWindow > 0.

RelativeWindow.description: Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see ScheduleMode.Relative). Window start = parent.StartUtc + OffsetSecondsFromParentStart. End = start + DurationSeconds, or (if DurationSeconds <= 0) the parent's end; never extends past the parent's end. Lets one config auto-repeat: sub-entity dates are computed from the current parent instance instead of being written absolutely.

OffsetSecondsFromParentStart.description: Window start offset in SECONDS from the parent instance start. 0 = open immediately with the parent. E.g. "Day N" = (N-1) * 86400.

DurationSeconds.description: Window length in SECONDS. 0 (or less) = the window lasts until the parent's end (typical for "stage opens and stays until the event ends"). >0 = lasts exactly that long (but never longer than the parent).

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after the window ends (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after the window ends for claiming rewards. Default 0.

Gate.description: Gate for the right to write. null = anyone who sees the channel may write. An announcement channel is expressed as a gate nobody passes.

Limits.description: Anti-spam: cooldown between messages (slow mode), daily cap, sliding window. Counters are written ALWAYS, even when no limit is set, so enabling a limit later works on live players immediately.

MaxLength.description: Maximum message length in characters. Not set = 500.

HotTailSize.description: Depth of the hot tail kept in Redis (messages). This is how much catch-up a returning player gets in one poll, and the range over which the unread badge is counted. Not set = 200.

HistoryHours.description: Durable history window in hours (collection TTL). Not set = 72. 0 means 'keep nothing beyond the hot tail' and leaves GetHistory empty.

ChatChannelPresetBindings.description: Preset wiring of a channel: one PresetBinding per preset-able block.

Availability.description: Preset for the Availability block.

PresetBinding.description: Wiring for one preset block of an entity: a reference into the module's preset registry + optional keys to drop. Reusable Core container, one per preset-able block, held inside the entity's Presets container. Replaces the former scattered flat *PresetID / *Remove fields. Combination is data-driven, no mode (PresetResolver): no PresetID -> inline only; preset + empty inline -> preset; preset + inline -> merge (preset base + inline overrides/adds by key), Remove drops keys. For a single object (Character Equipment) there is nothing to key-merge, so inline wins when both are present.

PresetID.description: Preset key in the module registry (e.g. LeaderboardDefinitions.Presets.Milestones[PresetID]). Empty/null = preset unused (inline layer only).

Remove.description: Keys removed from the merged result. Dictionary key for dictionaries; element key for keyed lists (Rank / SlotID / RuleID). null = remove nothing. Ignored when no preset is set.

DirectMessageSettings.description: Direct (1-on-1) message settings. A direct channel is never declared in the catalog - its address is derived from the pair of participants, so all direct channels share these settings.

IsEnabled.description: Whether direct messages are enabled. Not set = false - this is opt-in.

Gate.description: Gate for the right to use direct messages at all. null = allowed for everyone.

WhoCanMessage.description: Who may open a conversation: Anyone, or Friends only (an accepted edge in the Social graph). Not set = Anyone.

Limits.description: Anti-spam limits for direct messages, same model as channels.

MaxLength.description: Maximum message length in characters. Not set = 500.

HistoryHours.description: Direct history window in hours. Not set = 720 (30 days) - deliberately much longer than a world channel: a lost direct message is a real loss, a lost world line is not.

MaxConversations.description: Cap on the number of conversations one player may keep. Not set = 100. 0 = no cap.

x-enum-descriptions: Anyone.
Friends only - an accepted edge in the Social graph.
Clanmates only - members of the same clan of any kind.
Friends and clanmates.

ChatModerationSettings.description: Moderation rules shared by all channels and direct messages.

BlockedTerms.description: Blocklist of forbidden words/substrings (case-insensitive). The server normalizes the text before matching - strips diacritics, collapses repeats and separators, folds simple leet-speak - so spaced-out and homoglyph spellings are caught by the same list. Empty = no blocklist.

BlockedTermAction.description: What to do with a message containing a blocked term: Reject it outright, or Mask the term with asterisks and let the message through. Not set = Reject.

MaxIgnoreListSize.description: Cap on a player's personal ignore list. Not set = 200. 0 = the ignore list is disabled.

ReportsEnabled.description: Whether players may report messages. Not set = true.

ReportLimits.description: Anti-spam for reports: cooldown and daily cap per reporting player.

x-enum-descriptions: Reject the whole message.
Mask the term with asterisks and let the message through.

ChatPollingSettings.description: Polling economics. Every poll counts against the publisher's API quota, so the interval comes FROM THE SERVER rather than being hard-coded in the client: 1000 players online at a 1-second interval is 1000 requests per second. The client must also poll only while the chat screen is open - a closed chat updates its badge from the ordinary state response.

MinIntervalSeconds.description: Recommended and minimum poll interval in seconds. Not set = 5. The client must honour it; the server rate-limits on top of it anyway.

MaxMessagesPerPoll.description: Cap on messages returned by one poll, across all channels combined. Not set = 100.

MaxHistoryPageSize.description: Cap on a history page. Not set = 50.

ChatPresetRegistry.description: Chat preset registry: shared blocks reused across channels.

Availability.description: Availability presets, key = PresetID.

tools.name: get_community_marketing
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'CommunityMarketing' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Community Marketing - the program that rewards community members for posting about the game on external social platforms (YouTube/TikTok/Instagram). A campaign declares WHO may take part (Participation + SegmentGate), WHEN it runs (ScheduleSpec), WHICH platforms count and at what weight, WHAT the post must contain (hashtags, mention, the creator verification code), and HOW it pays: RateCards give a linear rate per metric (e.g. 60 GOLD per 1000 views, optionally multiplied by a per-submission moderator coefficient), while Milestones give threshold rewards using the shared platform milestone primitive. Spending is bounded by a campaign Budget plus per-submission, per-creator and per-team Caps - all evaluated against what has been PAID, never what has been earned. Providers says where the view/like/comment/share numbers come from per platform (the title's own API key or aggregator key, addressed BY NAME in TitleSecrets - never the value itself), Moderation says what a human reviews, and AntiFraud sets the hold period before earnings mature plus the anomaly thresholds that freeze a suspicious submission. Creators, submissions, metric snapshots, accruals and the payout journal are NOT here - they are operational data in their own collections. The Community Marketing pool bucket is funded by a fee on player crypto withdrawals, configured in the Currency section (CryptoCurrencyDefinition.CommunityMarketingWithdrawalFeePercent), not here.

tools.name: get_push
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Push' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Push notifications - the title's settings for messages delivered to a player who is NOT in the game right now (Web Push in the browser, FCM/APNs on mobile). IsEnabled is the master switch and defaults to DISABLED: notifications spend a real person's attention and require their browser permission, so a title opts in explicitly. MaxSendsPerUserPerDay caps how many a single player receives; MaxSendsPerTitlePerDay caps the title as a whole and is the ONLY ceiling on a broadcast that exists anywhere - the publisher API quota does not see sends at all, because they run in a queue worker rather than in a request pipeline. QuietHoursStart/End suppress sends during the night in the SUBSCRIPTION's locale (the window may cross midnight); waking a person at 3am is the fastest way to lose the browser permission permanently. Mobile holds only the NAMES of TitleSecrets entries for the publisher's Firebase service account and APNs .p8 key, never the credentials. VAPID keys are NOT here and never will be - they are platform-wide environment variables shared by both backends. Subscriptions themselves are not config either: they live in the shared PushEndpoints/PushBindings collections, one row per browser or device plus one row per topic it follows.

tools.name: save_push
