tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'PlatformBridge' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Platform bridge - what the game takes from the player's idosgames.com account and what it lets players show on their public profile. Profile: Off / Default (unset: the platform name and avatar until the player renames themselves in the game) / Always (every platform login overwrites them). Friends: TitleOnly (unset) / TitleAndPlatform (plus mutual follows on idosgames.com whose both sides play this game) / PlatformOnly (only those; in-game friend requests are refused) - applies to EVERY friends-based system: friends list and leaderboard, gifts, attack targets, friends-only Workshop items, recommendations. Notifications: which in-game notifications (Attack, Raid, FriendAdded, WorkshopSale) also reach the idosgames.com notification bell; empty = none. Guests never get platform data; the economy never crosses the bridge; turning the bridge off deletes nothing.

value.title: PlatformBridgeDefinitions
value.description: Platform bridge: what the game takes from the player's idosgames.com account and what it lets the player show on their public profile. Everything is off by default except the profile. What the PLAYER shares about themselves on the platform (the Played and Workshop tabs of their profile) is not the publisher's decision and is not configured here. Guests (no platform account) never get platform data. The economy never crosses the bridge.

Profile.description: Where the in-game name and avatar of a player with a platform account come from. Off = game only; Default (unset) = the platform ones until the player renames themselves in the game, after which the game choice is kept; Always = every platform login overwrites them.

Friends.description: Where 'friends' come from for EVERY game system (friends list, friends leaderboard, gifts, attack targets, friends-only Workshop items, recommendations). TitleOnly (unset) = in-game friendships; TitleAndPlatform = plus mutual follows on idosgames.com whose both sides play this game; PlatformOnly = only those, and in-game friend requests are refused with FRIENDS_FROM_PLATFORM.

Notifications.description: Which in-game notifications are also delivered to the notification bell on idosgames.com for players with a platform account. Unset/empty = none. Allowed: Attack, Raid, FriendAdded, WorkshopSale.

Recording.description: Lets players record videos of the game on idosgames.com (the Clip and Record buttons, background recording of the last minute, Best moments). Unset = on; false = no recording buttons and no background recording. Recording happens in the player's browser; nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: get_multiplayer
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Multiplayer' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Realtime multiplayer (WebRTC peer-to-peer) - the engine is only the signaling server: it creates rooms, relays WebRTC offer/answer/ICE between room members and optionally relays lobby chat; game traffic then flows directly between players' browsers and never touches the server. The section is ABSENT by default, which means multiplayer is DISABLED: add it (SystemState.Enabled = true) to turn the Multiplayer module on. DefaultTopology: Mesh (everyone connects to everyone, 2-4 players) or Host (star: every player connects to the host, which runs the authoritative game simulation - required by host-authoritative games such as VoxelCraft). MaxPlayersPerRoom is a hard cap (default 8). MemberTimeoutMs is also how long a silent host keeps the host role before another member may take it over. IceServers are PUBLIC: list only STUN servers there; short-lived TURN credentials are issued by the engine to room members on create/join.

tools.name: save_multiplayer
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Multiplayer' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Realtime multiplayer (WebRTC peer-to-peer) - the engine is only the signaling server: it creates rooms, relays WebRTC offer/answer/ICE between room members and optionally relays lobby chat; game traffic then flows directly between players' browsers and never touches the server. The section is ABSENT by default, which means multiplayer is DISABLED: add it (SystemState.Enabled = true) to turn the Multiplayer module on. DefaultTopology: Mesh (everyone connects to everyone, 2-4 players) or Host (star: every player connects to the host, which runs the authoritative game simulation - required by host-authoritative games such as VoxelCraft). MaxPlayersPerRoom is a hard cap (default 8). MemberTimeoutMs is also how long a silent host keeps the host role before another member may take it over. IceServers are PUBLIC: list only STUN servers there; short-lived TURN credentials are issued by the engine to room members on create/join.

value.title: MultiplayerDefinitions
value.description: V2 definition of the title's realtime multiplayer (WebRTC signaling). Public-only data: feature switch, topology/chat defaults, limits, ICE servers.

DefaultTopology.description: Default p2p connection topology for rooms: Mesh (everyone connects to everyone, small rooms) or Host (star: every player connects only to the host, which runs the authoritative simulation).

AllowCreatorTopologyOverride.description: Whether the room creator may override the topology at creation time.

DefaultChatMode.description: Default chat mode: ServerRelay (chat goes through the server, works in the lobby) or P2P (chat goes over the players' own DataChannel, the server does not relay it).

AllowCreatorChatOverride.description: Whether the room creator may override the chat mode at creation time.

MaxPlayersPerRoom.description: Max players per room (hard cap; the creator may request fewer).

VoiceEnabled.description: Voice chat in rooms. On by default; the room creator may turn it off for their room. Voice goes peer-to-peer in the same connection as game data (the server never sees it).

RecordVoices.description: Whether OTHER players' voices are included in videos a player records on the platform. On by default (the game then shows a 'Conversations may be recorded' notice); off = only the game sound and the recording player's own voice. Read by the client SDK (the multiplayer module), not by the server: videos are recorded in the player's browser.

RoomTtlSeconds.description: Room key TTL in Redis (seconds). Renewed on every interaction; the room disappears after this many idle seconds.

MaxRoomLifetimeSeconds.description: Hard room lifetime in seconds since creation. Unlike RoomTtlSeconds, activity does NOT renew it. When it passes the room is closed (members receive RoomClosed with Kind "expired"). Read from the current config. 0 = no limit.

HeartbeatIntervalMs.description: Recommended client poll interval (ms) while players are connecting.

MemberTimeoutMs.description: Threshold (ms) since the last heartbeat after which a member is treated as offline. Also the threshold after which another member may take over the host role of a room whose host stopped responding.

MaxSignalPayloadBytes.description: Max size of a single WebRTC signal payload (bytes). Guards against Redis bloat.

RoomLogCap.description: How many most-recent broadcast envelopes to keep in the room log (tail trimming).

IceServers.description: Extra ICE servers returned to the client verbatim. PUBLIC data: put only STUN servers here (or a TURN server whose credentials you are fine publishing). Short-lived TURN credentials are issued by the engine itself to room members. Empty = default public STUN servers.

IceServer.description: A single ICE server (maps to RTCIceServer on the client).

tools.name: get_ai
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'AI' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. InApp AI generation features of the title - what a PLAYER can generate at runtime through the engine (text/NPC chat, images, video, speech, music, 3D). Enabled is the master switch; Features maps a stable FeatureKey (no '.' or '$') to one feature: its Modality, a Model = the id of a MODE (Text: an AI Coder mode such as "standard") or a TIER (media: an asset generation tier such as "image-balanced") - list the usable ones, with what the publisher's plan allows, with the dashboard action GetInAppAIModels (Text features that AllowImages need a mode that AcceptsImages), Behavior defaults per modality (no platform caps: MaxTokens is bounded only by what the mode's model can produce), Safety prompt checks, an audience Gate (SegmentGate), a Schedule (ScheduleSpec), per-player Limits (LimitSpec) and the in-game PriceOptions the PLAYER pays (in-game resources and/or ONE store purchase per generation - a Purchase entry in the option's base price; never inside PremiumTiers, never two per option). Each generation is charged to the PUBLISHER's credits by the engine at the model's price; per-title spend caps (in credits) live in the PRIVATE config (InAppAIBudget), not here. Server-only section: never sent to the game client or the CDN.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Analytics' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Custom events - Firebase Analytics parity. The game sends its own events (logEvent(name, params, value)); the engine stores them per player per UTC day and the dashboard reports counts, unique players, value sums and breakdowns by platform, app version, OS, device, language, country, new/returning and acquisition source; A/B experiment goals and custom funnel steps can use these events. Enabled is the master switch and defaults to OFF. EventNaming: "Open" (any valid name is accepted and joins the title's event catalog up to the PLAN limit) or "Declared" (only names listed in Events). Events maps an event name (^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$; prefixes idos_/firebase_/google_/ga_ are reserved, except the automatic idos_* events) to a display name, description and a Blocked flag. Dimensions registers event parameters as reporting dimensions (like GA4 custom dimensions) - the count is capped by the plan; unregistered parameters are accepted but not stored. RetentionDays is how long per-player event data is kept (default 90, capped by the plan); daily title summaries are kept forever. AutomaticEvents (default on) accepts the SDK's automatic events: idos_first_open, idos_session_start, idos_app_update, idos_os_update, idos_screen_view.

tools.name: save_analytics
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Analytics' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Custom events - Firebase Analytics parity. The game sends its own events (logEvent(name, params, value)); the engine stores them per player per UTC day and the dashboard reports counts, unique players, value sums and breakdowns by platform, app version, OS, device, language, country, new/returning and acquisition source; A/B experiment goals and custom funnel steps can use these events. Enabled is the master switch and defaults to OFF. EventNaming: "Open" (any valid name is accepted and joins the title's event catalog up to the PLAN limit) or "Declared" (only names listed in Events). Events maps an event name (^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$; prefixes idos_/firebase_/google_/ga_ are reserved, except the automatic idos_* events) to a display name, description and a Blocked flag. Dimensions registers event parameters as reporting dimensions (like GA4 custom dimensions) - the count is capped by the plan; unregistered parameters are accepted but not stored. RetentionDays is how long per-player event data is kept (default 90, capped by the plan); daily title summaries are kept forever. AutomaticEvents (default on) accepts the SDK's automatic events: idos_first_open, idos_session_start, idos_app_update, idos_os_update, idos_screen_view.

value.title: AnalyticsDefinitions
value.description: Custom events (Firebase Analytics parity). Everything here is chosen by the publisher within their plan's analytics limits. Absent section or Enabled != true = events are not stored and cost no database access.

Enabled.description: Master switch. Unset = off: events are dropped without touching the database, and the SDK does not send them.

EventNaming.description: Event naming mode: "Open" (default — any valid name is accepted and joins the title's event catalog up to the plan limit) or "Declared" (only names listed in Events are accepted).

Events.description: Described events keyed by event name. In Declared mode the only accepted names; in Open mode — display names and blocks.

Dimensions.description: Event parameters registered as dimensions (like GA4 custom dimensions): reports can break events down by them. Unregistered parameters are accepted but not stored. Count is capped by the plan.

RetentionDays.description: Retention of per-player event data, days. Unset = 90 (or the plan maximum if lower). Clamped to the plan maximum. Daily title summaries are kept forever.

AutomaticEvents.description: Automatic SDK events (idos_first_open, idos_session_start, idos_app_update, idos_os_update, idos_screen_view). Unset = on: DAU and sessions by version/platform/device are computed from them.

Description.description: What the event means and when the game sends it.

Blocked.description: Blocked: events with this name are dropped in any naming mode.

Highlight.description: Highlight weight 1-10 for auto-clips: when the game logs this event, the player's background recording marks the moment, and the heaviest marks become their Best moments clips. Unset = not a highlight. Works even with analytics off (marking happens in the browser).

AnalyticsDimensionDefinition.description: An event parameter registered as a reporting dimension.

ParamName.description: Parameter name as the game sends it (^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$).

tools.name: get_data_collections
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'DataCollections' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Data collections - the creator's own data structures, a Firebase/Supabase-like store inside the platform for games, apps and sites. USE A READY PLATFORM MODULE FIRST (currencies, items, store, lootboxes, quests, leaderboards, chat, social, workshop, match, season, tutorial, localization, push, analytics); declare a collection only for what no module provides (guilds, auctions, orders, catalogs, articles, saved levels, feeds, mail) or for extra data attached to module entities. NEVER store currencies or items inside a record: reference them with a Ref field (Kind Item/Currency/User/…) and move value with Economy (Cost/Grant in engine resource format, charged in the same transaction as the write). Collections maps a collection id (letters, digits, '_', '-', ':' up to 64; a front-end module prefixes its namespace, e.g. 'guild-system:guilds') to: Kind (UserOwned: each record belongs to one user; Shared: records used by many users; Temporary: short-lived, mandatory TTL up to 30 days; Log: append-only, read by time); Mode (Strict = only declared fields); Fields (String, Text = searchable by words, Int, Number, Bool, Date, Json, Array with ItemType, Ref with Ref.Kind, File) with Required/Default (JSON literal)/Min/Max/MaxLength/MaxItems/Enum/Unique/Indexed/Visibility (Everyone/Owner/Server)/ClientWritable=false for server-only fields/Immutable; SortKeys (id + 1..4 components, each a scalar field or createdAt/updatedAt, optionally Descending) - every ordered query uses one, and equality filters on its leading components narrow the range; Access with Read/Create/Update/Delete lists of rules OR-ed together (Anyone - Read only, Authenticated, Owner, Members with MembersField = an Array of Ref(User), Role with a role id from Roles, Server); Limits (MaxItemBytes, MaxItemsPerOwner, TtlSeconds); OnOwnerDeleted (Delete/Anonymize/Keep); Counters (Count or Sum, optional GroupBy - maintained atomically, not allowed for expiring records); Integrations (QuestMetricOnCreate/Update/Delete advance quest objectives with Source ServerApi, AnalyticsEventOn*, TriggerOn* run a CloudCode handler asynchronously); Moderation.BlockedTerms; WriteGate (SegmentGate); PublicViews (published to the CDN for anonymous/site reads: SortKey, optional PartitionField, PageSize, MaxItems, PublishItems) and AnonymousSearch. Queries from a game may filter ONLY by Indexed fields and sort ONLY by declared SortKeys - there are no table scans on the shared cluster. Roles lists title user roles; they are assigned only by CloudCode (server.SetUserRoles) and the dashboard. The count of collections, searchable fields, sort keys, record size and storage are capped by the plan. Records themselves are NOT here - they live in the engine's DataCollection* collections; CloudCode reads and writes them with server.GetDataItem/QueryDataItems/CreateDataItem/UpdateDataItem/DeleteDataItem/BatchDataItems/GetDataCounter.

tools.name: save_data_collections
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'DataCollections' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Data collections - the creator's own data structures, a Firebase/Supabase-like store inside the platform for games, apps and sites. USE A READY PLATFORM MODULE FIRST (currencies, items, store, lootboxes, quests, leaderboards, chat, social, workshop, match, season, tutorial, localization, push, analytics); declare a collection only for what no module provides (guilds, auctions, orders, catalogs, articles, saved levels, feeds, mail) or for extra data attached to module entities. NEVER store currencies or items inside a record: reference them with a Ref field (Kind Item/Currency/User/…) and move value with Economy (Cost/Grant in engine resource format, charged in the same transaction as the write). Collections maps a collection id (letters, digits, '_', '-', ':' up to 64; a front-end module prefixes its namespace, e.g. 'guild-system:guilds') to: Kind (UserOwned: each record belongs to one user; Shared: records used by many users; Temporary: short-lived, mandatory TTL up to 30 days; Log: append-only, read by time); Mode (Strict = only declared fields); Fields (String, Text = searchable by words, Int, Number, Bool, Date, Json, Array with ItemType, Ref with Ref.Kind, File) with Required/Default (JSON literal)/Min/Max/MaxLength/MaxItems/Enum/Unique/Indexed/Visibility (Everyone/Owner/Server)/ClientWritable=false for server-only fields/Immutable; SortKeys (id + 1..4 components, each a scalar field or createdAt/updatedAt, optionally Descending) - every ordered query uses one, and equality filters on its leading components narrow the range; Access with Read/Create/Update/Delete lists of rules OR-ed together (Anyone - Read only, Authenticated, Owner, Members with MembersField = an Array of Ref(User), Role with a role id from Roles, Server); Limits (MaxItemBytes, MaxItemsPerOwner, TtlSeconds); OnOwnerDeleted (Delete/Anonymize/Keep); Counters (Count or Sum, optional GroupBy - maintained atomically, not allowed for expiring records); Integrations (QuestMetricOnCreate/Update/Delete advance quest objectives with Source ServerApi, AnalyticsEventOn*, TriggerOn* run a CloudCode handler asynchronously); Moderation.BlockedTerms; WriteGate (SegmentGate); PublicViews (published to the CDN for anonymous/site reads: SortKey, optional PartitionField, PageSize, MaxItems, PublishItems) and AnonymousSearch. Queries from a game may filter ONLY by Indexed fields and sort ONLY by declared SortKeys - there are no table scans on the shared cluster. Roles lists title user roles; they are assigned only by CloudCode (server.SetUserRoles) and the dashboard. The count of collections, searchable fields, sort keys, record size and storage are capped by the plan. Records themselves are NOT here - they live in the engine's DataCollection* collections; CloudCode reads and writes them with server.GetDataItem/QueryDataItems/CreateDataItem/UpdateDataItem/DeleteDataItem/BatchDataItems/GetDataCounter.

value.title: DataCollectionsDefinitions
value.description: Title data collections: a Firebase/Supabase-like store inside the platform. The creator declares structures (collections) with typed fields, searchable fields, sort keys, access rules and limits; the platform enforces tenant isolation, access, indexes, limits, deletion and billing. Use a ready platform module first (currency, items, store, quests, leaderboards, chat, workshop…); use collections only for what no module provides, or for extra data attached to module entities. Never store currencies/items in a collection — reference them and move value through the engine economy (Cost/Grant).

Enabled.description: Master switch. Default false — data collections must be enabled explicitly.

Collections.description: Collections of the title. Key = collection id ('guilds', 'orders'; a front-end module prefixes its namespace: 'guild-system:guilds'). Allowed: letters, digits, '_', '-', ':' up to 64 chars. No '.' or '$'.

Roles.description: Title user roles (admin, editor, moderator…) referenced by 'Role' access rules. Key = role id. Roles are assigned only by the server (CloudCode) and the dashboard, never by the client.

DataCollectionDefinition.description: A data collection declared by the creator.

DisplayName.description: Display name (a localization key or a literal).

Description.description: What this collection stores (documentation for the dashboard and the AI coder).

Namespace.description: Creator's own namespace (grouping in the dashboard and for the AI coder). Does not affect storage.

Tags.description: Free-form tags (grouping and search in the dashboard).

Enabled.description: A disabled collection is neither readable nor writable. null = enabled.

Kind.description: Data class — decides physical storage, indexes and lifetime. UserOwned: each record belongs to one user (saves, orders, builds). Shared: records shared by many users (guilds, auctions, catalog, articles). Temporary: short-lived records with a mandatory TTL (invites, lobbies, carts). Log: append-only records read by time (history, feed, messages, audit).

Mode.description: Strict: only declared fields are accepted. Loose: declared fields are validated, undeclared ones are accepted as free-form JSON (not searchable).

SchemaVersion.description: Schema version, stamped on each record. After a field type change old records are re-validated lazily on their next write.

Fields.description: Record fields. Key = field name (letters, digits, '_' up to 64 chars).

SortKeys.description: Declared sort keys, including composite ones ('region' then 'score' descending). Every ordered query must use one of them. Equality filters on the leading parts narrow the range.

Access.description: Access rules for Read / Create / Update / Delete.

Limits.description: Limits: record size, records per owner, TTL.

OnOwnerDeleted.description: What happens to a user's records when the account is deleted: Delete (default), Anonymize (owner removed, record stays), Keep.

Counters.description: Declared aggregates maintained atomically on every write (count of records per field value, sum of a numeric field). Read them instead of scanning.

Economy.description: Economy of client operations in engine resource format: Cost is charged and Grant is given in the SAME transaction as the write ('create a guild = 500 gold'). Value always moves through the engine economy, never inside a record.

Integrations.description: Integration with other platform modules: quest progress, analytics events, leaderboard score, push notifications, CloudCode triggers.

Moderation.description: Moderation of user-written text fields (blocked terms).

WriteGate.description: Audience gate for client writes. null = everyone allowed by the access rules.

PublicViews.description: Public views published as static files to the CDN (R2) for anonymous and logged-in reads without touching the database. Requires Access.Read to include Anyone. Only fields visible to Everyone are published. Freshness is seconds, not instant.

AnonymousSearch.description: Allow live anonymous search by declared searchable fields (site search). Answers are cached in Redis for 30 s and limited per network. Default false. Requires Access.Read to include Anyone.

x-enum-descriptions: Each record belongs to one user (saves, builds, orders, documents, settings).
Records shared by many users (guilds, auctions, catalog, articles, world shards, tournaments).
Short-lived records with a mandatory TTL (invites, requests, lobbies, carts, codes).
Append-only records read by time (battle history, feed, order journal, messages, audit). No updates.
Only declared fields are accepted.
Declared fields are validated, undeclared ones are accepted as free-form JSON (not searchable, not sortable).

Type.description: Field type.

ItemType.description: Element type for Array fields (a scalar type or Ref). null = Json elements.

Ref.description: Reference target for Ref fields (and arrays of Ref).

Required.description: The field must be present on create.

Default.description: Default value as a JSON literal (1, "EU", true, []). Applied on create when the field is absent.

Min.description: Minimum (numbers and dates as unix ms).

Max.description: Maximum (numbers and dates as unix ms).

MaxLength.description: Maximum length: characters for String/Text, UTF-8 bytes for Json.

MaxItems.description: Maximum number of elements for Array fields.

AllowedMimeTypes.description: File fields: allowed content types (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif, application/json, model/gltf+json, model/gltf-binary, application/zip, text/plain, application/octet-stream). null = any of them. The server checks the real file signature against the declared type.

MaxFileBytes.description: File fields: maximum file size in bytes. null = 10 MB; at most 100 MB. Files live in the platform's private bucket, count toward the publisher's storage and are read through short-lived signed links.

Unique.description: Value must be unique within the collection (email, slug, nickname). Enforced by the database inside the write transaction.

UniqueIgnoreCase.description: Uniqueness ignores letter case (only for String fields with Unique).

Indexed.description: The field can be used in query filters (equality, in, range, array-contains, prefix). Queries from a game/app may filter ONLY by searchable fields. Text fields are searched by words and word prefixes.

Visibility.description: Who can see the field: Everyone (default), Owner (the record owner only), Server (CloudCode and dashboard only).

ClientWritable.description: false = only the server (CloudCode, dashboard) writes this field — scores, guild level, order status. Client writes to it are rejected. null = client-writable.

Immutable.description: The field cannot be changed after creation.

x-enum-descriptions: A string (up to MaxLength characters, default 256).
Long text searched by words and word prefixes (up to MaxLength characters, default 4000).
A 64-bit integer.
A floating point number.
true / false.
A date-time in UTC (ISO-8601 string or unix ms on input).
Any JSON value (not searchable). Size limited by MaxLength bytes.
An array. Element type is ItemType. Arrays of scalars are searchable with array-contains.

A reference to another entity: a record of a collection, a user, an item, a currency, an item instance, a store offer, a leaderboard, a quest, a workshop publication. Validated on write, expandable on read.
A file stored in the platform's private bucket; the record keeps a reference and clients get signed URLs.

Collection.description: For DataItem: the target collection id.

Validate.description: Check that the target exists on write. null = yes.

x-enum-descriptions: A record of a data collection (Ref.Collection).
A user of this title (user id).
An item definition of the title's Item config ("CatalogID/ItemID" or a unique ItemID).
A currency of the title's Currency config (virtual or crypto currency id).
A player's item instance id (non-stackable item).
A store offer id.
A leaderboard id.
A quest id.
A workshop publication id.
Visible to everyone who can read the record.
Visible only to the record owner.
Never returned to clients: CloudCode and dashboard only.

DataSortKeyDefinition.description: A declared sort key: one or more components. Queries order by a sort key; equality filters on its leading components select the range ('region = EU, by score').

Components.description: Components in order. Each is a scalar field (String, Int, Number, Bool, Date) or the built-in 'createdAt' / 'updatedAt'.

DataSortComponent.description: One component of a sort key.

DataCollectionAccess.description: Access rules. Each operation takes a list of rules combined with OR. null/empty list = Server only. The server (CloudCode, dashboard) is never restricted by these rules.

Read.description: Who can read records. A rule wider than Owner (Authenticated, Anyone) lets EVERY player read EVERY record — including other players' records in a UserOwned collection. Personal data (wallet addresses, transaction signatures, a player's ledger, emails) must stay Owner/Server: keep Read = Owner, or hide such fields with field Visibility = Owner/Server and open only the rest.

Create.description: Who can create records. For UserOwned the creator becomes the owner; for Shared the creator becomes the owner when the rule is Authenticated/Owner. A client-created record is whatever the player typed: a collection the game TRUSTS (ledger, balances, asset registry, transfers, results) must be written by the server only — leave Create empty (= Server) and write it from CloudCode.

Mode.description: Who the rule admits.

Role.description: For Role: the role id from DataCollections.Roles.

MembersField.description: For Members: the name of an Array field of Ref(User) listing the members.

ClanField.description: For Clan: the name of an Indexed String field that holds the ClanID the record belongs to. On client create the server fills it with the creator's clan; clients can never change it.

ClanKind.description: For Clan: the clan kind (KindID). Empty = the title's default kind.

ClanPermission.description: For Clan: a role permission the member must have (built-in like 'edit_info' or the game's own). Empty = any member of the clan.

x-enum-descriptions: Anyone, including visitors without a session (Read only; served from the CDN / cache, never straight from the database).
Any signed-in user of the title.
The owner of the record.
A user listed in the record's MembersField.
A user who has the Role.
Server only (CloudCode, dashboard).
A member of the clan the record belongs to (record field ClanField = ClanID), optionally with a role permission (ClanPermission). Own clan data of a game: clan base layout, war plan, shared notes.

DataCollectionLimits.description: Collection limits. Every value is additionally capped by the title's plan.

MaxItemBytes.description: Maximum record size in bytes (serialized data). null = 16384, capped by the plan.

MaxItemsPerOwner.description: Maximum records one user may own in this collection. null = unlimited (within the title limit).

TtlSeconds.description: Record lifetime in seconds. Mandatory for Temporary (max 30 days). For Log it is the retention (capped by the plan). null for UserOwned/Shared = permanent.

x-enum-descriptions: Records owned by the user are deleted (default).
The owner is removed, the record stays (e.g. a guild outlives its founder).
Records are kept as they are. The new owner of the same user id still does NOT inherit them (ownership is checked against the registration date).

DataCounterDefinition.description: A declared aggregate maintained on every write.

Kind.description: Count: number of records. Sum: sum of SumField.

SumField.description: For Sum: an Int or Number field.

GroupBy.description: Group by the value of a scalar field (e.g. members per guild, orders per status). null = one total per collection.

Visibility.description: Who can read the counter: Everyone (default) or Server.

x-enum-descriptions: Number of records.
Sum of a numeric field.

DataCollectionEconomy.description: Economy of client operations. Charged/granted in the same transaction as the write, idempotent per record operation.

OnCreate.description: Create: Cost is charged from the creator, Grant is given to the creator.

OnUpdate.description: Update by a client: Cost and Grant for the caller.

OnDelete.description: Delete by a client: Cost and Grant (e.g. a refund) for the caller.

DataOperationEconomy.description: Cost and grant of one operation.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Credits, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account (players see it as "Aspis" — write Aspis in player-facing text). Requires only Amount — the price in whole Credits. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCreditsPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted by every sale of the game author: Store, Lootbox, Collection packs, Craft, DealOffer, TimedBoost, Premium, Item and Character upgrades, skins, CoopEvent spins, GameLoop special mode entry, Workshop publish fee, InApp AI (charged only when the generation is ready). NOT accepted in player-to-player prices or refundable fees (Marketplace listing fee, PvP Match creation) - those refuse with CREDITS_NOT_ALLOWED_HERE; batch calls refuse too. Allowed only in Consume: Credits are never a reward anywhere.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

Type.description: System the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

QuestMetricOnCreate.description: Quest progress: objectives with Source = ServerApi and this MetricID advance by 1 for the acting user when a record is created.

QuestMetricOnUpdate.description: Quest metric advanced when a record is updated by a client.

QuestMetricOnDelete.description: Quest metric advanced when a record is deleted by a client.

AnalyticsEventOnCreate.description: Custom analytics event logged for the acting user on create (server-side, same rules as server.LogEvent). Params: collection, itemId.

TriggerOnCreate.description: CloudCode handler run asynchronously (queue, retries) after a record is created. args = { Trigger, Collection, ItemID, Item, Previous }.

TriggerOnUpdate.description: CloudCode handler run asynchronously after a record is updated.

TriggerOnDelete.description: CloudCode handler run asynchronously after a record is deleted.

BlockedTerms.description: Blocked terms checked in every String/Text field written by a client. A match rejects the write.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

DataPublicViewDefinition.description: A public view published to the CDN as static pages.

SortKey.description: Sort key id the pages are ordered by.

PartitionField.description: Optional: a separate page set per value of this searchable field (category, region). Must be the leading component of SortKey.

MaxItems.description: Maximum records published per partition (default 1000, max 5000).

PublishItems.description: Also publish one file per record (items/{id}.json).

Description.description: What the role is for (documentation only).

tools.name: get_mailbox
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Mailbox' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Mailbox - an in-game mailbox that holds VALUE the player claims (not notifications - those are Push). Enabled is the master switch, default OFF. Capacity (default 100) caps visible letters; on overflow the oldest letters WITHOUT unclaimed rewards are removed. RewardLetterDays (30) / PlainLetterDays (14) are letter lifetimes (an unclaimed reward is lost when it expires), ClaimedRetentionDays (7) keeps claimed letters visible. DefaultLanguage (en) is the text fallback. Templates maps a TemplateID to per-language Texts {Subject, Body with {Param} placeholders}, Category (System/Reward/Gift/Social tab), Icon, Banner, Link {FeatureID+Args to open a game screen, or an https Url}, SenderName, ExpirationDays; keys 'system.*' override built-in letters of modules (system.gift, system.transfer, system.transfer_return, system.leaderboard_reward, system.coop_grand_prize, system.coop_object_reward, system.season_unclaimed, system.referral_reward). Gifts.Social maps a GiftID to a friend gift (Grant of items/virtual currencies minted on claim; optional Cost the sender pays per friend, burned; one per friend per period; the period is IntervalSeconds (default 86400) counted from AnchorUtc (default 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC) like fixed-interval cycles of other systems; SendLimit/ReceiveLimit per period, default 20; SenderGate). Gifts.Transfer lets friends send their OWN resources: AllowedResources whitelist (VirtualCurrency or STACKABLE items; MaxAmountPerGift is a CAP - any amount from 1 up to it, entries separately or together), MaxEntriesPerGift (5), IntervalSeconds/AnchorUtc (same period model), SendLimit/ReceiveLimit per period (5), FeePercent (0-90, withheld from what the friend receives, the fee per entry rounds up) and FeeCost (fixed fee on top); both burn only when the friend claims - a declined or expired transfer returns everything charged, MinFriendshipHours (24, against alt-account funnelling), ExpirationDays (7, then returned to the sender). Integrations {Leaderboard, CoopEvent, Season, Referral} (empty = on) bring unclaimed rewards of those modules to the mailbox. Letters and broadcasts themselves are NOT config: they are sent from the dashboard (player letters, segment broadcasts with a SegmentGate and a schedule) or by CloudCode server.SendMail; letters with rewards require the player-admin plan right.

tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Mailbox' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Mailbox - an in-game mailbox that holds VALUE the player claims (not notifications - those are Push). Enabled is the master switch, default OFF. Capacity (default 100) caps visible letters; on overflow the oldest letters WITHOUT unclaimed rewards are removed. Gifts.Social maps a GiftID to a friend gift (Grant of items/virtual currencies minted on claim; optional Cost the sender pays per friend, burned; one per friend per period; the period is IntervalSeconds (default 86400) counted from AnchorUtc (default 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC) like fixed-interval cycles of other systems; SendLimit/ReceiveLimit per period, default 20; SenderGate). Gifts.Transfer lets friends send their OWN resources: AllowedResources whitelist (VirtualCurrency or STACKABLE items; MaxAmountPerGift is a CAP - any amount from 1 up to it, entries separately or together), MaxEntriesPerGift (5), IntervalSeconds/AnchorUtc (same period model), SendLimit/ReceiveLimit per period (5), FeePercent (0-90, withheld from what the friend receives, the fee per entry rounds up) and FeeCost (fixed fee on top); both burn only when the friend claims - a declined or expired transfer returns everything charged, MinFriendshipHours (24, against alt-account funnelling), ExpirationDays (7, then returned to the sender). Letters and broadcasts themselves are NOT config: they are sent from the dashboard (player letters, segment broadcasts with a SegmentGate and a schedule) or by CloudCode server.SendMail; letters with rewards require the player-admin plan right.

value.title: MailboxDefinitions
value.description: Title mailbox: letters with rewards, publisher broadcasts, friend gifts and unclaimed rewards of other modules. An in-game mailbox that holds VALUE the player claims — not notifications (those are Push) and not the social activity inbox.

Enabled.description: Module master switch. Default false — the mailbox must be enabled explicitly.

Capacity.description: How many visible letters a mailbox keeps. On overflow the oldest letters without unclaimed rewards are removed. Empty = 100.

RewardLetterDays.description: Lifetime of a letter WITH rewards, in days. An unclaimed reward is lost when it expires. Empty = 30.

PlainLetterDays.description: Lifetime of a letter WITHOUT rewards, in days. Empty = 14.

ClaimedRetentionDays.description: How many days a letter stays in the mailbox after its reward was claimed. Empty = 7.

DefaultLanguage.description: Fallback language when a letter has no text in the player's language. Empty = "en".

Templates.description: Letter templates keyed by TemplateID. Referenced by broadcasts, dashboard letters and CloudCode. Keys 'system.*' override the built-in letters of other modules.

Gifts.description: Gifts between friends. null = no gifts.

Integrations.description: Which modules bring their unclaimed rewards to the mailbox. null = all of them.

MailTemplateDefinition.description: Letter template: texts, look and lifetime.

Texts.description: Texts per language. Key = language code ("en", "ru"). Subject/Body may contain {Param} placeholders filled from TemplateParams by the client.

Category.description: Mailbox tab. Empty = derived from the letter source.

Banner.description: Banner inside the letter (path or URL).

SenderName.description: Sender name shown on a system letter (e.g. "Game team").

ExpirationDays.description: Letter lifetime in days. Empty = the section default; 0 = never expires (only for letters without rewards).

MailText.description: Letter subject and body in one language.

x-enum-descriptions: System messages and announcements.
Letters that carry rewards.
Gifts from friends.
Social notifications.

MailLink.description: Button inside a letter: open a game screen (FeatureID, like ctx.features.open) or a URL. One of the two.

FeatureID.description: Feature (system) to open in the game, e.g. "store". CLIENT contract: the game SDK opens it (ctx.features.open); the engine only stores and returns it.

Url.description: Absolute https URL to open instead of a feature.

MailboxGiftDefinitions.description: Gifts to friends: free social gifts and transfers of the player's own resources.

Social.description: Free gifts (like 'lives' in casual games), keyed by GiftID. The sender loses nothing; one gift of a kind per friend per UTC day.

Transfer.description: Transfer of the player's own resources to a friend. null = disabled.

Audience.description: Who may receive gifts and transfers: Friends (default), FriendsOrClanmates, Clanmates. Clanmates = members of the same clan of any kind.

Enabled.description: Switch of this gift kind. Empty = enabled.

Grant.description: What the friend receives. Items and virtual currencies only; minted when the friend claims it.

Cost.description: Price the SENDER pays per friend, charged in the same transaction as the letter (not enough = the gift is not sent). Burned; the friend still receives Grant. Items and virtual currencies only. Empty = free.

IntervalSeconds.description: Period length in SECONDS (60 to one year): 'once per friend' and the limits are counted in windows of this length from AnchorUtc - the same fixed-interval cycles as other systems (CyclicSchedule.IntervalSeconds). 21600 = 6 hours, 86400 = a day, 604800 = a week. Empty = 86400.

AnchorUtc.description: Anchor of the windows (UTC, time of day included): windows run every IntervalSeconds from it, both ways. It sets the alignment, e.g. 03:00 UTC makes days start at 03:00. Empty = 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC (as cycles of other systems).

SendLimit.description: How many gifts of this kind a player may send per period. Empty = 20.

ReceiveLimit.description: How many gifts of this kind a player may receive per period. Empty = 20.

SenderGate.description: Who may send this gift. null = everyone.

TemplateID.description: Template of the recipient's letter. Empty = built-in 'system.gift'.

ExpirationDays.description: Gift letter lifetime in days. Empty = the reward letter lifetime.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Credits, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account (players see it as "Aspis" — write Aspis in player-facing text). Requires only Amount — the price in whole Credits. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCreditsPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted by every sale of the game author: Store, Lootbox, Collection packs, Craft, DealOffer, TimedBoost, Premium, Item and Character upgrades, skins, CoopEvent spins, GameLoop special mode entry, Workshop publish fee, InApp AI (charged only when the generation is ready). NOT accepted in player-to-player prices or refundable fees (Marketplace listing fee, PvP Match creation) - those refuse with CREDITS_NOT_ALLOWED_HERE; batch calls refuse too. Allowed only in Consume: Credits are never a reward anywhere.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

Type.description: System the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

Clan.description: Clan condition (clans, stage 2): in a clan or not, clan level, role, membership age, a role permission. null = not applied. Read from the player's clan snapshot of the request, not from the player document; outside a client request the condition fails closed.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).
Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).

SegmentClanCondition.description: Gate condition on the player's clan. All fields are AND-ed; an empty field = no restriction.

KindID.description: Kind of clan (KindID). Empty = the default kind.

InClan.description: true = must be in a clan of the kind; false = must NOT be in one. Empty = true when any other field is set, otherwise no restriction.

RoleIDs.description: The member's role must be one of these RoleIDs. Empty = any role.

Permission.description: The member's role must have this permission (built-in or the game's own). Empty = no restriction.

MinMembershipHours.description: Hours in the clan at least. 0 = no restriction.

TransferGiftDefinition.description: Transfer of own resources to a friend. Resources are taken immediately and wait in the letter; returned to the sender if declined or expired.

Enabled.description: Switch. Default false.

AllowedResources.description: What may be transferred and how much per gift. Virtual currencies and STACKABLE items only; unique item instances go through the marketplace.

AllowItemInstances.description: Allow transferring the player's own unique item instances (with their level) through the shared item transfer. Which items: the Item rows of AllowedResources (MaxAmountPerGift = pieces per transfer). The item must be IsTradable; an equipped copy is refused. Empty = off.

IntervalSeconds.description: Period length in SECONDS (60 to one year): 'once per friend' and the limits are counted in windows of this length from AnchorUtc - the same fixed-interval cycles as other systems (CyclicSchedule.IntervalSeconds). 21600 = 6 hours, 86400 = a day, 604800 = a week. Empty = 86400.

AnchorUtc.description: Anchor of the windows (UTC, time of day included): windows run every IntervalSeconds from it, both ways. It sets the alignment, e.g. 03:00 UTC makes days start at 03:00. Empty = 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC (as cycles of other systems).

SendLimit.description: Transfers per period from one player. Empty = 5.

ReceiveLimit.description: Transfers per period to one player. Empty = 5.

FeePercent.description: Commission in percent (0-90): withheld from what the friend receives, per entry (the fee rounds up by the platform convention, the friend gets the rest). Burned only when the friend claims; a declined or expired transfer returns EVERYTHING charged, fee included. Empty = 0.

FeeCost.description: Fixed fee per transfer: charged from the sender on top of what is sent. Burned only when the friend claims; returned with the transfer if declined or expired. Items and virtual currencies only. Empty = no fee.

MinFriendshipHours.description: How many hours two players must have been friends before a transfer (against alt-account funnelling). Empty = 24.

ExpirationDays.description: How many days a transfer waits for the recipient before it returns to the sender. Empty = 7.

TemplateID.description: Template of the recipient's letter. Empty = built-in 'system.transfer'.

Type.description: VirtualCurrency or Item.

CurrencyID.description: Currency ID (Type = VirtualCurrency).

CatalogID.description: Item catalog (Type = Item).

ItemID.description: Stackable item ID (Type = Item).

MaxAmountPerGift.description: CAP per transfer, not a fixed amount: a player sends any amount from 1 up to the cap (and not more than they own). Resources of the list go separately or together - how many per transfer is MaxEntriesPerGift. Empty = no cap.

x-enum-descriptions: Friends only (an accepted friendship).
Friends and clanmates (members of the same clan of any kind).
Clanmates only.

MailboxIntegrationDefinitions.description: Which modules bring unclaimed rewards to the mailbox. An empty field = enabled.

CoopEvent.description: Coop event: grand prize and object rewards of completed groups.

Season.description: Season: tier rewards left unclaimed when the season ended.

Clan.description: Clan: unclaimed rewards of clan levels, projects, activities and clan quests (shown live while they can be claimed).

tools.name: get_clan
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'Clan' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. Clan - clans of the game for any genre: 4X alliances, midcore clans, casual teams. IsEnabled (empty = on) and Kinds: a map KindID -> kind; usually ONE kind with id 'clan' (then clients never pass KindID); a second kind (guild + club) is just another key. Each kind: Identity {NounKey - localization key of the word the player sees: Clan/Alliance/Guild/Team, DisplayName fallback, Icon}; Create {Gate (SegmentGate who may create), Price (PriceOption map: what creating costs, several payment options), NameMin/MaxLength (3/20), TagRequired, TagMin/MaxLength (2/5), DescriptionMaxLength/AnnouncementMaxLength (300), Emblem {Backgrounds, Symbols, Colors atlas keys}, Languages, Attributes (own clan attributes with allowed Values), RenamePrice, RenameCooldownHours, ReservedNames}; Membership {BaseCapacity (default 30), JoinModes (Open/Request/InviteOnly), DefaultJoinMode, JoinGate, ApplicationHours/InviteHours (72), MaxApplicationsPerPlayer (5)/PerClan (50), JoinCooldownHours (after leaving any clan), RejoinSameClanHours, TenureHoursForRewards (membership age before gifts and level rewards), MaxKicksPerDay (10)}; MemberStats {Power, Trophies: source PlayerLevel / CharacterLevel / CurrencyBalance (Key=CurrencyID) / Reported (the game reports it via CloudCode server.SetClanMemberStat), PowerTopN}; Roles {Roles: RoleID -> {Rank (higher = more power), NameKey, DisplayName, MaxCount, Permissions}, LeaderRoleID, DefaultRoleID, LeaderInactiveDays (leadership passes to the most senior active member)}; empty Roles = built-in leader/coleader/elder/member; built-in permissions: invite, manage_applications, kick, set_role, edit_info, edit_announcement, moderate_chat, create_request; any OTHER permission id is the game's own (e.g. start_rally) checked by the game via MyPermissions or server.HasClanPermission. Counters: CounterID -> {NameKey, Sources (TriggerSource list), Reset Never/Daily/Weekly, DailyCapPerMember} - own clan counters for rankings. Rankings {Metrics: Power, Level, Trophies, Members, counter:{id}; ByLanguage; ByRegion; PageSize}. Hooks: clan event (Created, Joined, Left, Kicked, RoleChanged, LeaderChanged, Updated, Donated, Helped, LevelUp, GiftCreated, Disbanded) -> CloudCode function name, run after the write. Progression {XpSources (TriggerSource list; events of members bring clan XP), DailyXpCapPerMember, Levels (explicit table; index 0 is LEVEL 2, level 1 needs 0 XP; each row RequiredXp, Capacity, RoleCaps, Perks: request_amount_percent, help_cap) or XpCurve/BaseXp/MaxLevel, CapacityPerLevel, LevelRewards (MilestoneDefinition list, RequiredProgress = clan level, every member present at that moment claims)}. Requests: RequestKindID -> {Type 'Resource' (members ask for a resource: Resources whitelist of VirtualCurrency or stackable Item with the asked Amount, Funding Donor (the donor pays) or System (free, like lives; SystemDailyCap per title per day), MaxPerDonor, DailyDonateCap, DonorReward per unit) or 'Help' (one tap help on the game's task key: MaxHelps, DailyHelpCap, DonorReward), Gate, CooldownMinutes, LifetimeHours, MaxOpenPerMember}. Gifts {Gifts: GiftID -> {Triggers (TriggerSource list, e.g. IapPurchase or StorePurchase of a member), Points (clan gift points), Content (ResourceGrant), ContentByLevel}, Levels (MilestoneDefinition list by gift points: gift levels and their rewards), LifetimeHours (72), ShowSender, IncludeSender}. A feature block left empty is off. Crypto and event tokens are never allowed in clan flows. Clan data of the game itself lives in DataCollections with the access rule Mode=Clan (ClanField = Indexed String field with the ClanID).

tools.name: get_early_access
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'EarlyAccess' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. EarlyAccess - early token purchase: while the game's token is on its bonding curve and its early phase is open, only players holding a pass may buy it. The phase itself (duration up to 7 days, total cap, no-sell) is fixed when the token is launched, allowed by the platform per title or publisher, and frozen on chain - this section cannot change it. Enabled is the master switch (default OFF). Tiers: each has TierID, MaxQuote (how much of the chain's quote token in wei the player's wallet may spend in the phase in total), NotBeforeUtc (the wave; empty = at once) and Conditions, ALL of which must hold: QuestCompleted {QuestID} (hours played, logins, kills and any metric are quests), ItemOwned {ItemID, MinAmount default 1, MinLevel}, LeaderboardRank {LeaderboardID, MaxRank}, CloudCodeGrant {GrantID, given by a script with server.GrantEarlyAccess}, Segment {Gate}. Empty Conditions = any player with a verified wallet. A player gets the best tier (higher MaxQuote, then the earlier wave); OR = several tiers. The player requests the pass himself (EarlyAccess.GetPass); it is personal, bound to one wallet, never published.

tools.name: save_early_access
tools.description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'EarlyAccess' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. EarlyAccess - early token purchase: while the game's token is on its bonding curve and its early phase is open, only players holding a pass may buy it. The phase itself (duration up to 7 days, total cap, no-sell) is fixed when the token is launched, allowed by the platform per title or publisher, and frozen on chain - this section cannot change it. Enabled is the master switch (default OFF). Tiers: each has TierID, MaxQuote (how much of the chain's quote token in wei the player's wallet may spend in the phase in total), NotBeforeUtc (the wave; empty = at once) and Conditions, ALL of which must hold: QuestCompleted {QuestID} (hours played, logins, kills and any metric are quests), ItemOwned {ItemID, MinAmount default 1, MinLevel}, LeaderboardRank {LeaderboardID, MaxRank}, CloudCodeGrant {GrantID, given by a script with server.GrantEarlyAccess}, Segment {Gate}. Empty Conditions = any player with a verified wallet. A player gets the best tier (higher MaxQuote, then the earlier wave); OR = several tiers. The player requests the pass himself (EarlyAccess.GetPass); it is personal, bound to one wallet, never published.

value.title: EarlyAccessDefinitions
value.description: Early token purchase: while the game's token is on its bonding curve and its early phase is open, only players holding a pass may buy it. Whether the token has a phase, how long it lasts and whether selling is blocked were fixed when the token was launched and are frozen on chain. This section only says WHO the engine signs a pass for: Tiers, each with its own purchase cap and wave. A player gets the best tier whose conditions all hold. The pass is personal and requested by the player; nothing is published.

Enabled.description: Module master switch. Default false — no passes are signed.

Tiers.description: Tiers. A player gets the BEST tier whose conditions all hold (higher MaxQuote; on a tie the earlier wave). For OR between conditions use several tiers.

EarlyAccessTier.description: An early-access tier: conditions (all of them), a purchase cap and a wave.

TierID.description: Tier ID (returned to the player and kept with the issued pass).

MaxQuote.description: How much of the token's pair currency (smallest units as a string: wei for the native coin, 6-decimal units for a 6-decimal ERC-20) the player's wallet may spend in the phase IN TOTAL, over any number of buys.

NotBeforeUtc.description: The wave: the pass works only from this moment (UTC). Empty = at once.

Conditions.description: Conditions, ALL of which must hold. Empty = any player with a verified wallet.

EarlyAccessCondition.description: One condition. Hours played, daily logins, enemies killed and any metric are counted by QUESTS (their objectives take any event), so there is no counter here: "played N hours" is a quest with that objective.

Type.description: Condition type: QuestCompleted (QuestID completed or claimed), ItemOwned (ItemID, MinAmount default 1, optional MinLevel), LeaderboardRank (LeaderboardID, current rank 1..MaxRank), CloudCodeGrant (GrantID given to the player by a CloudCode script with server.GrantEarlyAccess), Segment (Gate: level, premium, country, registration and activity, experiment, tutorial).

ItemID.description: ItemOwned: the item.

MinLevel.description: ItemOwned: only instances of at least this level count. Empty = any.

MaxRank.description: LeaderboardRank: the worst rank that still qualifies (1 = only the leader).

GrantID.description: CloudCodeGrant: the grant a script gives with server.GrantEarlyAccess({ GrantID, UserID? }).

tools.name: get_game_spec
tools.description: GET ONLY the 'GameSpec' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel. GameSpec - the WHOLE game of a game-constructor title (module kit-game) as data, stored as ONE JSON string (a JSON object serialized to text). The game reads it at sign-in and plays it; a spec that does not validate runs the built-in demo and logs why. Shape (format v1): {"v":1, "engine":"phaser"|"three" (the preset's own: "three" for the 3D genres "crowd", "parking", "wash", "arcade", "bus", "screws", "cannon", "hole" and "stack", "phaser" for the rest), "seed"?:string, "modes":[{"id", "preset" (a genre preset id, e.g. "runner"), "role":"core"|"meta"|"embedded", "params"?:{preset params, e.g. difficulty 0..1, generosity 0..1, lanes, lives}, "blockParams"?:{blockId:{param:value}} }], "resources"?:[{"id" (snake_case), "kind":"currency"|"item"|"score"|"local", "ref"? (the title's currency/item id for currency/item), "name"? (text key)}], "flows"?:[{who produces/consumes which resource}], "rules"?:[{"id", "on" (event), "when"? (formula), "do":[effects]}], "palette"?:{role:"#rrggbb"} (roles background, ground, lane, primary, secondary, danger, coin, accent, text, muted), "texts"?:{key:{language:text}} (keys title, hint and the resource name keys), "rewards"?:{"adMultiplier":3, "vipMultiplier":5}}. tools.name: plan_video
tools.description: Write a short vertical video with the iDos Games video studio's AI director: an idea becomes a VideoSpec (format, scene, characters, lines with emotions and actions, captions) built from the studio library, plus the plan — for each element whether the library fits or an AI asset should be generated (`next` lists the generate_asset calls: pass them the returned `package` and the item's slot, and the asset takes its place). Refs outside the library are replaced with the closest library asset (listed in `repaired`), the cast is fitted to the format. Costs one text generation of the publisher's credits (see estimate_media_cost, modality text). If it is not ready in about two minutes the answer carries the generation id — call plan_video again with generation_id to finish it without paying twice. The answer is a video PACKAGE ({ spec, assets }) and, when title_id names a game with the video studio, a `link` that opens it in that app's editor — the player watches, edits and exports the MP4 on the device (there is no server render). Formats and assets: list_video_formats, search_assets.
